value.headline: - [ ] G023 — NOETIC_COMPILER PIPELINE (§54, §70, §71): Foreign Model -> ArchitectureRecognizer -> OrganGraph -> Doctor -> RepresentationPlanner -> PhysicalGraphCompiler -> KernelPlanner -> DeviceCompiler -> NoeticExecutable, increasingly automatic. DeviceGenome = RepresentationGenome x KernelGenome x RuntimeGenome x MachineGenome; representations are never evaluated with incompetent kernels; device profiles qualified where useful. | status: BLOCKED | risk: high | tier: V3 || BLOCK RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/NOETIC_COMPILER_BLOCK_CHECK.json): the recorded blocker is FALSE AS STATED. crates/hawking-core/src/model/qwen30_complete_runtime.rs is a wired 7,046-line native Metal path for a ROUTED MoE model — it admits a catalog, validates 18,867 tensor names/shapes, and executes routers and experts on device, exported from model/mod.rs with 3+ examples building on it. So 'no qwen3_moe reader exists' is wrong. REVISED BLOCKER, much narrower: that reader is bound to ONE model and ONE artifact family (hardcoded 18,867-tensor manifest, HQ30-class admit_* constructors) while the pipeline emits an hq38m20 catalog for Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B — so the unblock is GENERALIZATION of an existing router-capable reader, not a from-scratch 8,552-line implementation. Also corrected a SELF-CERTIFIED PASS: NOETIC_COMPILER_PIPELINE.json reported pass=true with 2/8 stages BLOCKED and 3/4 acceptance clauses unmet; now pass=false. Stays BLOCKED — 6/8 stages automatic with 0 manual interventions, no executable produced, no device profile qualified. tools/odyssey/test_compiler_block_check.py 9 passed || STAGE AUDIT 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/NOETIC_COMPILER_STAGE_AUDIT.json): the record was wrong in BOTH directions. OVERSTATED — KernelPlanner was recorded AUTOMATIC on model #2, but its receipt (KERNEL_LIBRARY.json) has no specimen field, never names Qwen3-30B-A3B, and catalogues kernels only for qwen38 organs (deltanet, gqa_attention, mlp_down, mlp_gate_up) with ZERO for any MoE organ; corrected to NOT_RUN_FOR_MODEL_2, so the honest count is 5/8 automatic, not 6/8. Consequence: the obligation's own rule that representations are never evaluated with incompetent kernels CANNOT be checked for model #2, because no kernel was planned for its organs. Also: NO stage produced bytes — every AUTOMATIC stage emitted an analysis, so this is a PLANNING pipeline, not a compiling one. UNDERSTATED — both halves of the 'missing' capability already exist: a 7,046-line routed reader AND 18 MoE expert-table kernels (qwen30_expert_table_binary_matvec / _hgravs_gemv, serial, simdgroup, rowblock2/4/8) backed by qwen30_device_expert_table.metal. The pipeline simply never connected them. REVISED GAP, smaller than any prior statement: register the existing MoE kernels in the library, derive tensor validation from the catalog instead of the hardcoded 18_867, accept the pipeline's container alongside the HQ30 admit_* family. Remains BLOCKED: 3 acceptance clauses unmet. tools/odyssey/test_compiler_stage_audit.py 10 passed || UNBLOCK STEP 1+2 DONE 2026-08-25: stopped auditing and did the first tractable item. REGISTERED the 18 MoE expert-table kernels that already existed but were never catalogued — all 18 verified present BOTH as `kernel void` declarations in qwen30_device_expert_table.metal AND as named references in the routed runtime; the library validator accepted all 18 (35 kernels, 0 rejected, 136 fields ABSENT-with-reason). Nothing was invented: measurements, supported_capability_regime and parity are ABSENT with reasons on every added kernel because none has been run here. Then RAN KernelPlanner for model #2 against its recognizer-derived organ graph (receipts/headless/KERNEL_PLANNER_MODEL2.json): 2 of 6 organs now have a competent kernel (gqa_attention 1, moe_expert 18), 4 do not (embed, lm_head, moe_router, rmsnorm). §71 is now CHECKABLE for model #2 for the first time — organs without kernels are may_be_evaluated=false, and covered organs are marked COMPETENT_BUT_UNQUALIFIED since every expert kernel has parity ABSENT. KernelPlanner status corrected AUTOMATIC -> RAN_WITH_GAPS. Remains BLOCKED: 4 organs lack kernels, no executable, no device profile. tools/odyssey/test_kernel_planner_model2.py 9 passed || §71 NOW ENFORCED PER (ORGAN x REPRESENTATION) 2026-08-25: my own previous step was too loose — matching on organ NAME reported moe_expert COVERED by 18 kernels while the planner had seeded q2_affine, which NONE of them executes (they execute binary_group / hgravs01_factored / uniform_q4_group). Rebuilt the planner to judge competence by the pair, using the two vocabularies actually on disk rather than an invented map, and to consider EVERY seeded family in score order instead of only the top one. Result is a real planning decision: moe_expert's top seed q2_affine has no competent kernel, so it DOWNGRADES to conventional_low_bit with 7 competent uniform_q4_group kernels. Caught and fixed a second bug in my own work: leftover_f32 was being 'selected' for moe_expert, which would report the model's largest organ (18,432 tensors) COVERED by declining to compress it — f32 passthrough is now refused for GEMV organs and permitted only for passthrough organs like rmsnorm. Coverage 3/6 (gqa_attention, moe_expert, rmsnorm); gaps are embed, lm_head, moe_router, whose kernels exist in shaders but are not registered. tools/odyssey/test_kernel_planner_model2.py 13 passed || COVERAGE 3/6 -> 5/6 2026-08-25: registered 6 more kernels (embed x2, lm_head, router x3), each verified BOTH declared as `kernel void` in its shader AND referenced from crates/hawking-core/src/; library now 41 kernels, 0 rejected, 160 fields ABSENT-with-reason, nothing invented. Representation read from each SHADER SIGNATURE, not the name: qwen38_hgravu=uniform_qn_group, qwen38_hgrafv=q2_affine, router matvecs=binary_group (router_signs uchar + router_scales half, no residual path), router select=topk_select (representation-independent; top_k and experts are runtime parameters). Caught TWO more errors in my own logic: (1) binary_sparse_residual had been mapped to accept plain binary/binary_group, which a kernel with no residual path cannot execute; (2) a representation-INDEPENDENT selector was counting as competent on its own, which marked moe_router COVERED for q2_affine when the only q2_affine-capable thing present was a top-k selector and every router MATVEC is binary_group — GEMV organs now require a WEIGHT-BEARING kernel. Final: 5/6 covered (embed, gqa_attention, lm_head, moe_expert downgraded to conventional_low_bit, rmsnorm f32-passthrough). SOLE REMAINING GAP is moe_router and it is precisely diagnosed: 3 kernels exist but execute binary_group and topk_select while the planner seeds q2_affine / binary_sparse_residual / ternary — a REPRESENTATION MISMATCH, not a missing kernel. Fix is either seed binary_group for the router or write a q2_affine router matvec. tools/odyssey/test_kernel_planner_model2.py 17 passed || ROUTER GAP TRACED UPSTREAM 2026-08-25: measured the organ mass shares from the specimen's own config rather than asserting — moe_expert 94.95%, gqa_attention 2.97%, embed 1.02%, lm_head 1.02%, moe_router 0.0412%, rmsnorm 0.0006%. Quantizing the router at all saves 44.6 MiB on the single most routing-sensitive organ in the model. That showed my own GEMV_ORGANS blanket refusal of f32 passthrough was too crude: passthrough eligibility is now decided by MEASURED MASS against a 0.5% ceiling, so moe_router qualifies at 0.0412% and moe_expert still cannot at 94.95% (pinned by a test so the size rule cannot reopen the case it was built to close). ROOT CAUSE of the router gap is UPSTREAM, not a kernel gap: the RepresentationPlanner seeded ONLY aggressive families (q2_affine / binary_sparse_residual / ternary) and never offered leftover_f32 for an organ where quantizing buys 0.46% of the artifact. Diagnosed with the measurement and DELIBERATELY NOT PATCHED here — inventing a seed inside the KernelPlanner would be exactly the hand-authored stage output this obligation forbids, and would make the stage look complete. Coverage stays 5/6 honestly. tools/odyssey/test_kernel_planner_model2.py 21 passed || KERNELPLANNER STAGE NOW COMPLETE FOR MODEL #2 2026-08-25: fixed the UPSTREAM defect in the stage that actually had it. transfer_rehearsal.py seeded purely by score and was MASS-BLIND (`ranked[:3]`), so on a negligible organ the aggressive families always won and the safe option never reached the table. Added mass-aware seeding: an organ at or under 0.5% of measured model mass now gets leftover_f32 as a candidate, computed from the specimen's own config. Only moe_router qualified (0.0412%); embed/lm_head/gqa are above the ceiling and are unchanged. Re-ran the planner then the KernelPlanner: 6/6 organs now have a plannable representation — embed/gqa_attention/lm_head conventional_low_bit, moe_expert DOWNGRADED q2_affine->conventional_low_bit (7 kernels), moe_router DOWNGRADED to leftover_f32 (mass-justified), rmsnorm leftover_f32. Stage status AUTOMATIC, so 6/8 stages are now genuinely automatic on model #2 and the overstatement the audit found is RESOLVED rather than merely recorded. The receipt states plainly what completion does NOT mean: no bytes are packed, DeviceCompiler and NoeticExecutable remain BLOCKED, and every competent kernel still carries parity ABSENT. 31 tests pass across test_kernel_planner_model2.py + test_compiler_stage_audit.py || ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE 4 CLOSED 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/DEVICE_PROFILES.json): two device profiles QUALIFIED with DIFFERENT WINNERS, on the two bodies that cleared G040's capability floor, 3 alternated reps per (body, level). INTERACTIVE (c1, headline TPOT): sealed-3.14 wins 29.364 vs 30.247 ms, margin 2.92% against spreads of 0.10% and 0.13% so the margin is real. MAXX (c4, headline aggregate tokens/s): variantB-2.76 wins 11.119 vs 7.078 — and sealed is NOT QUALIFIED for MAXX at all because its aggregate swings 25.77% and its TTFT 39.92% across three reps while variantB repeats to 2.45% and 1.68%. Mechanism named: 4 concurrent processes ask ~39.3 GiB of Metal working set for sealed vs ~34.5 GiB for variantB, so the larger body sits close enough to the admission ceiling that its behaviour stops repeating — the same collapse G040 measured at higher concurrency, appearing earlier for the bigger body. value.headline: - [ ] G043 — ACCELERATOR IDENTITY / FRONT A (S015): ACORE namespace and contracts, AIR representing operations, memory, dependencies, synchronization, representations, device requirements and specialization opportunities; Accelerator receipt schema carrying ExperimentIdentity, MachineIdentity, DeviceIdentity, ModelIdentity, RepresentationIdentity, KernelIdentity, RuntimeIdentity and TransportIdentity where applicable; MachineGenome integration. Proof P3: AIR executes a basic operation on Metal. | status: IN_PROGRESS | risk: medium | tier: V3 || PROOF P3 PASSES 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_FRONT_A_P3.json): AIR EXISTS AND EXECUTES ON THE APPLE GPU. tools/accelerator/air.py represents ops, operands with dtype and shape, dependencies as SSA, a device requirement and specialization constants; lowers to MSL; runs on Metal. 6 programs graded against a numpy oracle -- add, mul, relu, silu, a fused saxpy->relu with a specialization constant, and a 3-op chain -- all 6 match, worst max_abs_err 4.768e-07 against a 1e-5 tolerance. Receipt carries ALL EIGHT identities (S015 §79) with ABSENT-and-a-reason where one does not apply, and the schema REFUSES a receipt that omits an identity, marks one ABSENT without a reason, invents an experiment class outside the 13 canonical ACCEL-* names, or promotes to an unknown knowledge level. PLACEMENT IS A FIELD from the start so EGB cannot force an AIR redesign. CONSTRAINT RECORDED: xcrun metal is ABSENT on this machine (no Metal developer toolchain), so AOT metallib compilation is unavailable and execution goes through MLX 0.32.1 mx.fast.metal_kernel JIT -- a real dependency, named in the receipt. CLAIM BOUNDARY: proves P3 and nothing above it. No CUDA kernel translated (P4 open), NOTHING WAS TIMED so no performance claim exists (P5 open), AIR does not yet represent synchronization, side effects, memory-domain requirements or multi-device placement, and only elementwise ops over one shape and dtype work -- GEMM, attention and reductions from the required corpus are ABSENT. tools/accelerator/test_air.py 11 passed 1 skipped. || MACHINEGENOME MEASURED 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/MACHINE_GENOME.json + ACCELERATOR_MACHINE_GENOME.json): Apple M3 Ultra, 60 GPU cores, 28 CPU (20P/8E), 96 GiB, measured bandwidth 589.73 GB/s median with a 1.89% IQR, f32 triad, lake fill SIGSTOPped. MY FIRST BANDWIDTH NUMBER WAS NOT A MEASUREMENT and is kept in the receipt as REJECTED: 403.06 best / 314.0 median with a 286.08% SPREAD -- a distribution with a fast tail, and quoting its best sample would have been exactly the marketing number S015 §73 forbids. Replaced with larger buffers, real warmup, and an IQR GATE that marks a result UNRELIABLE rather than quoting it when spread exceeds 10%. SECOND DEFECT FIXED: subprocess does not raise on non-zero exit, so the xcrun ERROR TEXT was stored as if it were a Metal compiler version; now checks returncode and records ABSENT with reason. thermal_envelope and sustained_behaviour BOTH ABSENT with reasons -- this is a microbenchmark and S015 §29 requires sustained evidence to be distinguished from one. Knowledge level INSTANCE, NOT promoted to SOC_FAMILY: one M3 Ultra is not evidence about M3 Ultras. || AIR EXPRESSIVE GAP CLOSED 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_AIR_COMPLETENESS.json) -- THIS SUPERSEDES 'AIR does not yet represent synchronization, side effects, memory-domain requirements or multi-device placement' ABOVE. Now REPRESENTED: AirBarrier over THREADGROUP/SIMDGROUP/DEVICE; side effects as writes_external on an op OR read_only=False on an operand; memory-domain requirement on every tensor plus an output_domain, over 7 named domains. Placement was already a field. THE DISCIPLINE THAT MAKES IT HONEST IS THE REFUSAL: representing more than the backend can RUN is the point of an IR, but only if the two are NEVER CONFUSED -- lower_to_msl now calls executable_on_metal_backend() and REFUSES WITH THE REASON rather than emitting code that ignores the construct. 4 of 5 probe cases are REFUSED and that is correct for all 4. A SILENTLY DROPPED BARRIER IS A RACE, the worst class of bug to ship quietly; a silently ignored memory domain would compute ON THE WRONG COPY. VOCABULARY SHARED WITH HUMF, NOT PARALLEL: AIR's domain names ARE HUMF's domain names, pinned by a test that takes a requirement straight out of an AIR program and looks it up in a HUMF fabric with NO mapping layer -- a translation layer would be free to drift and there now isn't one. WIDENS THE IR, NARROWS NOTHING ABOUT THE BACKEND: none of these constructs EXECUTE, multi-device placement still has no backend honouring it, and AIR still has NO GEMM, attention or reduction. 61 tests pass. || AIR NOW PRODUCES THE TILED MATMUL 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_AIR_MATMUL.json) -- closes the gap the GEMM receipt named one block earlier, which was that AIR had NO tiling, NO threadgroup allocation and only barrier REPRESENTATION not LOWERING, so the working kernel was hand-written MSL sitting BESIDE AIR. AirMatmul now OWNS the tile size as a specialization, DECLARES the threadgroup allocation, and EMITS ITS OWN BARRIERS. THAT is what makes THREADGROUP scope executable: an elementwise program carrying an AirBarrier is STILL REFUSED because nothing lowers it, while a matmul is ACCEPTED because its lowering emits the barriers itself -- REFUSAL TRACKS WHAT THE BACKEND CAN EMIT, NOT WHAT AIR CAN NAME, and the two tests sit next to each other so the distinction cannot rot. BARRIERS ARE LOAD-BEARING: stripping the ones AIR emits takes max_abs_err to 45.12. FORGE NOW TUNES AN AIR SPECIALIZATION (connects G043 to G047): tile sweep 8/16/32 at 1024^2 gives 2096 / 2091 / 2258 GFLOP/s, champion tile=32 by ~8% against ~5% arm noise -- real but modest, and tiles 8 and 16 are INDISTINGUISHABLE. MLX still wins 2.5x (5706 GFLOP/s) and REMAINS THE QUALIFIED WINNER; AIR reaches 39.6% of it. Remaining gap lives in simdgroup matrix ops, double buffering, register blocking and vectorised loads, NONE of which this adds. AIR still has NO attention and NO reduction, and SIMDGROUP/DEVICE barrier scopes remain UNLOWERABLE and therefore REFUSED. 68 tests pass. || BARRIER SCOPES CLOSED, AND A REFUSAL OF MINE WAS BLAMING THE WRONG THING 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_BARRIER_SCOPES.json): the AIR receipts carried 'SIMDGROUP/DEVICE barrier scopes remain UNLOWERABLE and therefore REFUSED' for many blocks -- the last named-absent construct in the IR. MEASURED BEFORE BUILDING, because emitting an instruction that does nothing and calling it a closed gap is exactly the coverage-without-capability this program keeps refusing. TWO PROBES, AND TOGETHER THEY SAY MORE THAN EITHER: WITHIN a simdgroup, 32 lanes exchanging through threadgroup memory are exact at max_abs_err 0.0 with NO fence, with simdgroup_barrier AND with threadgroup_barrier -- lockstep makes the fence UNNECESSARY. ACROSS simdgroups, the same exchange at 256 threads reading 32 slots away is WRONG BY 9.854 with no fence and WRONG BY EXACTLY THE SAME 9.854 with simdgroup_barrier, while threadgroup_barrier is exact -- so the instruction is OUT OF SCOPE there. The scope is precisely what its name says: no effect inside because unnecessary, no effect outside because out of scope. THE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES THE FIRST PROBE READABLE -- 'all three correct' is worthless unless the test CAN fail, and the cross-simdgroup control fails two of three arms by 9.854, so the probe demonstrably detects a missing fence. WHAT SHIPPED: barrier_msl() is one place a lowering asks for the instruction; THREADGROUP and SIMDGROUP return one and DEVICE RAISES. SIMDGROUP IS EMITTED BUT NOT CLAIMED AS A CLOSED SYNCHRONIZATION GAP -- it is emitted for two reasons that are NOT correctness-on-this-chip, that it constrains the COMPILER's reordering and that lockstep is a HARDWARE PROPERTY a future device need not preserve. THE DEVICE REFUSAL NAMES THE ALTERNATIVE: device-wide ordering has no in-kernel Metal instruction because IT IS A COMMAND-BUFFER BOUNDARY, and AIR ALREADY EXPRESSES THAT as an AirGraph dependency EDGE -- a refusal that points at the construct which does carry the semantics is worth more than one that only says no. AND A REFUSAL OF MINE WAS BLAMING THE WRONG THING: the elementwise program's message said 'the Metal backend has no synchronization lowering', but AIR's matmul, softmax and attention lowerings ALL emit threadgroup barriers and have for many blocks. The backend was NEVER the constraint. The real one is that an ELEMENTWISE program declares no threadgroup allocation and no cross-thread reads, so a barrier of ANY scope HAS NOTHING TO ORDER -- the refusal was correct and its stated cause was not, and a refusal that names the wrong cause teaches the wrong lesson to whoever reads it next, here that the backend cannot synchronize, which would have made the matmul's own barriers look impossible. THE DISTINCTION THAT MUST NOT ROT is pinned by two tests side by side: an elementwise program carrying a barrier is REFUSED, a matmul is ACCEPTED because its lowering emits its own. CLAIM BOUNDARY: nothing timed, no performance claim; NO AIR PROGRAM CURRENTLY DECLARES A SIMDGROUP BARRIER AND EXECUTES -- what closed is the INSTRUCTION and the REFUSAL'S HONESTY, not a new executable program shape; lockstep at simd width 32 is an M3 Ultra observation and is NOT promoted to a property of Apple GPUs; and DEVICE-scope barriers remain unlowerable at the instruction level always, so the routing to AirGraph is a REDIRECTION not a closure. 191 tests pass. || SPECIALIZATION CONSTANTS BUY NOTHING MEASURABLE, AND MY EXPLANATION DIED IN THE NEXT EXPERIMENT 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_SPEC_CONSTANTS.json): the CCL carried COMPILER.specialization_constants with measured=FALSE, reason 'specialisation was never isolated as its own arm' -- AIR has had the field since P3 and the forge tunes one, but nothing ever compared BAKING A VALUE INTO THE SOURCE against READING IT FROM A BUFFER. TWO CASES ON PURPOSE, because they test DIFFERENT claims: a SCALAR multiplier, where specialization saves ONE broadcast load (PREDICTED INDISTINGUISHABLE), and a LOOP BOUND, where it changes WHAT THE COMPILER CAN PROVE because a literal bound can be unrolled and a buffer bound cannot (PREDICTED A REAL DIFFERENCE). SCALAR: CONFIRMED INDISTINGUISHABLE, 1.62% margin against 7.95% noise. LOOP: NOT CONFIRMED -- 2.59% and the buffer arm failed the gate at 14.66%, so the instrument refused to call it either way. I OFFERED AN EXPLANATION -- that loop was MEMORY BOUND, so unrolling changes the instruction stream and not the traffic, and the traffic is the wall -- AND THEN TESTED IT rather than letting it stand as a story that happens to fit a null result: one load then 256 fused multiply-adds, so loop overhead and the branch are the ONLY difference. IT IS REFUTED. INDISTINGUISHABLE with CLEAN ARMS at 5.25% and 4.96%, and the LITERAL IS 3.09% SLOWER. So the honest result is that specialization constants buy nothing measurable on this backend in either shape, and my prediction was wrong in both loop cases. WHAT WOULD SETTLE THE MECHANISM CANNOT BE DONE HERE: whether the literal loop is actually unrolled is a question about GENERATED CODE, and xcrun metal is ABSENT -- the same named gate that blocks AOT metallib -- so 'the compiler already handles a uniform runtime bound as well as a literal' is a HYPOTHESIS, not a finding. A DISTINCTION THAT MUST NOT BE CONFLATED: the FORGE tunes a TILE SIZE and calls it a specialization, measuring 2096/2091/2258 GFLOP/s across tiles 8/16/32 -- but a TILE SIZE CHANGES THE ALGORITHM (threadgroup allocation, loop structure, access pattern) while this measures a CONSTANT that changes only where a number comes from, so reading the forge's tile result as evidence that specialization constants pay would be wrong. CONSEQUENCE FOR AIR: specialization constants are an EXPRESSIVENESS feature on this backend and NOT a performance one -- they still earn their place, because a program that names its constants is a program whose IDENTITY KEY can include them and that is what the forge cache depends on, but NO SPEED CLAIM MAY BE ATTACHED TO THEM. CORRECTNESS FIRST: both pairs verified BIT-IDENTICAL at exactly 0.0 before timing -- here a DIFFERENT answer would have meant the arms were not the same computation at all. 200 reps and 40 warmup, the program's own stability floor. LEDGER: COMPILER.specialization_constants moves unmeasured -> MEASURED with a receipt path, CCL now 15 of 20 performance gaps measured. Of the 5 that remain, THREE ARE CORRECTLY UNMEASURABLE by their own reasons (indexing is not independently measurable, numerical diagnostics is not a performance capability, a frontend gap is about COVERAGE not speed), ONE is the hardware gate (MULTI_DEVICE.peer_access) and ONE is the instrument benchmarking itself. 191 tests pass. || TOP-K AND SAMPLING EXIST, AND GRADING A SAMPLER IS NOT GRADING A KERNEL 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_TOPK_SAMPLING.json): S015 §3 names TOP-K and SAMPLING in the required corpus and NO receipt had ever CLAIMED OR REFUSED either, which by the ledger's own rule means NOT YET STUDIED. AirTopKSample builds both. THE HARD HALF IS THE GRADING: a sampler cannot be checked the way every other kernel here has been, because 'the returned index is one of the top k' PASSES FOR A SAMPLER THAT ALWAYS RETURNS THE ARGMAX -- this campaign's check-that-cannot-fail in a new place. THE DESIGN CHOICE THAT MAKES EXACT GRADING POSSIBLE AT ALL: THE RANDOMNESS IS AN INPUT, one uniform per row drawn host-side from a seeded generator, so the kernel is a PURE FUNCTION of (logits, u); a kernel generating its own randomness could only ever be graded statistically. THREE LAYERS, WEAKEST LAST, each saying something the others cannot: (1) TOP-K EXACT against numpy's stable argsort at 8x64 k=5, 4x4096 k=8, 3x517 k=1, 2x128 k=64 plus a deliberate tie case -- indices exact and values 0.0 everywhere; (2) CHOICE EXACT GIVEN u, 512/512 at temperatures 0.5/1.0/2.0, reproducible on the same u and moving on 400 of 512 rows with a different one, WHICH CANNOT CATCH A SHARED CONVENTION ERROR because an oracle walking the CDF the same wrong way agrees with itself; (3) DISTRIBUTIONAL over 8192 draws, true sampler chi2 4.33 against a 24.322 critical value, with NEGATIVE CONTROLS that must FAIL -- uniform-over-k 4588, argmax-always 9901, off-by-one bucket 12552. WIDTH IS NOT SHAPE: a shape-dependent defect is DETERMINISTIC, wrong every run at the wrong shape, which is why 2885 single runs settled that axis; a width-dependent one is usually a RACE and therefore PROBABILISTIC -- the top-k barrier fired in 16 of 30 runs at 1024 and 0 of 30 at 256 -- so this sweep REPEATS and its resolving power comes from the repeat count rather than the width list. RESULT: 7 primitives x 6 widths x 8 runs = 42 configurations and 336 executions, ZERO wrong, worst relative error 1.49e-06. The write-after-read the normalization block fixed structurally in norm, softmax and attention does not reappear at any width. THE RESULT THAT MATTERS IS THE POSITIVE CONTROL'S. A probabilistic sweep reporting zero failures is EXACTLY the shape of a check that cannot fail, and the previous block found precisely that in its own instrument, so one barrier was stripped from AirNorm and the sweep had to flag it. IT IS CAUGHT 8 OF 8 RUNS AT THREADGROUPS 64, 128, 256, 512 AND 1024 -- AND IS EXACT AT 32, worst error 1.24e-07, 0 of 8 wrong. A 32-WIDE THREADGROUP IS EXACTLY ONE SIMDGROUP, and this program already measured that within a simdgroup 32 lanes exchanging through threadgroup memory are exact with NO fence because lockstep makes it unnecessary -- so THE CONTROL REPRODUCES THAT FINDING FROM A COMPLETELY DIFFERENT DIRECTION, and A CONTROL RUN ONLY AT 32 WOULD HAVE REPORTED THE BROKEN KERNEL FINE. The error also GROWS with width, 0.427 / 0.955 / 1.685 / 2.764 / 3.273 at 64/128/256/512/1024 -- more simdgroups, more disagreement, the mechanism showing itself rather than a threshold. SHIPPED kernel_forge.swept_with_control, which runs the real check AND a deliberately broken one over the same cases and REFUSES the result when the broken arm passes everywhere -- not because the kernel is wrong but because the sweep proved NOTHING about it -- and reports control_blind_at as a FIRST-CLASS FIELD rather than a footnote; plus detection_floor_per_run = 1 - 0.5**(1/repeat) with every sweep, so a clean result cannot be read as proof that no race exists, and WIDTH_PRIOR over the legal Metal range in simdgroup steps. PREDICTION written first -- the fixed kernels are correct at all widths, and N runs cannot detect a race under ~1/N per run -- CONFIRMED ON BOTH HALVES, and the control added a third thing I did not predict, that THE CONTROL ITSELF HAS A BLIND WIDTH. CLAIM BOUNDARY: repeat=8 detects a race above ~8.3% per run about half the time, so the top-k race at 53% would be caught and a 2% race would not -- ZERO FAILURES IS NOT ABSENCE OF RACES; width is varied with SHAPE HELD FIXED, the mirror of the previous sweep's boundary rather than its closure; ONE control, on a TOTAL dependency, and the top-k receipt already showed an INCIDENTAL barrier is far quieter so a control's loudness is not transferable evidence; f32, one machine, INSTANCE, and lockstep at simd width 32 remains an M3 Ultra observation and not a property of Apple GPUs; nothing timed. 258 accelerator tests pass. || THE QUIET CONTROL IS BLIND AT FOUR OF SIX WIDTHS 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_QUIET_CONTROL.json): the width sweep named this as its own boundary -- 'ONE control, on a TOTAL dependency, and the top-k receipt already showed an INCIDENTAL barrier is far quieter so a control's loudness is not transferable evidence'. MEASURED, AND THE NUMBER IS 10x: on the SAME width list, SAME repeat and SAME machine, a barrier on a TOTAL dependency (AirNorm's row sum, which every thread reads) fires in 40 OF 48 RUNS and is blind at 1 of 6 widths, while one on an INCIDENTAL dependency (top-k's tree-reduce sweep) fires in 4 OF 48 and is blind at 4 of 6. A SWEEP WHOSE ONLY CONTROL IS LOUD REPORTS A BLIND LIST OF LENGTH 1 AND THEREBY IMPLIES A RESOLVING POWER IT DOES NOT HAVE. GROUND TRUTH FIRST, 480 executions at rows=32 cols=4096 k=8: the intact kernel is wrong 0 of 240 at every width, and the quiet control's per-run probability is a CLIFF NOT A GRADIENT -- 0, 0, 0, 0, 0.15, 0.975 at 32/64/128/256/512/1024. Four widths are not quiet, they are SILENT, and NO REPEAT COUNT RESCUES p=0. It also fires at 512, a width the top-k receipt never ran, and at 1024 it is 39 of 40 here against that receipt's 16 of 30 -- so p is a property of the defect, the width AND THE SHAPE together. THE FLOOR IS CALIBRATED AND BOUNDS THE WRONG THING: detection_floor_per_run = 1 - 0.5**(1/repeat) is shipped with every result and ASSUMES the repeat runs are INDEPENDENT, which nothing had checked. PREDICTION WRITTEN BEFORE THE RUN -- at 512 with p~0.15 an 8-run block should detect in ~0.73 of trials, band 0.60-0.85, and well below would mean correlated runs and an optimistic floor. CONFIRMED at the low edge: 40 blocks of 8 gave p_hat 0.1187 over 320 runs, OBSERVED block detection 0.6250 against a binomial 0.6363, 1.1 points apart. THE STRONGER TEST IS THE WHOLE DISTRIBUTION, because matching the MEAN can happen with correlated runs -- the per-block hit counts fit Binomial(8, p) at CHI2 0.150 ON 2 DOF against a 5.991 critical value, dispersion 1.10, so the runs really are independent. AND THE FLOOR WAS CALIBRATED AT ITS OWN THRESHOLD BY ACCIDENT: the stated floor is 8.3% per run and this real race sits at 11.87%, just above it, caught in 25 of 40 blocks -- exactly what 'detects anything above the floor more than half the time' asserts, with nothing arranged to land there. THE CORRECTION IS THAT THE FLOOR BOUNDS REPEAT AND WAS REPORTED BESIDE A LENGTH-1 BLIND LIST, which invites reading it as COVERAGE; coverage is set by the case list and by whether the defect fires there at all, and at 32/64/128/256 the floor is irrelevant because p is exactly zero. AND MY OWN CONTROL REPORTED DETECTING EVERYWHERE WHILE CRASHING EVERYWHERE: the first two-control run showed the LOUD control firing at all six widths INCLUDING 32, contradicting ACCELERATOR_WIDTH_SWEEP.json which measured it EXACT there. The probe passed kind='rms' where the field is `mode`, so AirNorm raised a TypeError on EVERY call, swept_with_control caught it, recorded inf, and COUNTED IT AS A DETECTION -- the control detected a TypeError in my probe. CAUGHT BY THE DISAGREEMENT WITH A SHIPPED RECEIPT, not by re-reading the loop, and checked directly: stripped-vs-intact at threadgroup 32 is IDENTICAL TO THE LAST DIGIT at cols 512 (6.804e-08) and cols 4096 (1.065e-07), so the shipped 32-blindness REPRODUCES on two shapes it was never measured on. THE RULE THAT HID IT IS ONE I SHIPPED TWO BLOCKS AGO: the shape fuzz established that a sweep must record A RAISE AS A FAILURE rather than a skip, because a shape the kernel refuses is a shape the caller needs told about -- CORRECT FOR THE REAL ARM AND BACKWARDS FOR A CONTROL, since a control that raises never ran the kernel. A RIGHT RULE APPLIED TO THE WRONG ARM is a different failure from a wrong rule, and both directions are now pinned by tests sitting next to each other. SHIPPED: swept_with_control takes a LIST of labelled controls and reports each one's detected/blind/fired separately; blind_at_every_control, the cases NO control reached, which is what the sweep actually says nothing about, with control_blind_at kept for back-compat and commented as the FIRST control's alone; a control that RAISES refuses the sweep naming the control and the exception; and floor_bounds_repeat_not_coverage on every result with the calibration in the docstring. CLAIM BOUNDARY: TWO controls is one point at each end of a spectrum whose MIDDLE IS UNMEASURED; the quiet rates are for ONE shape; independence is established at ONE width and assumed elsewhere; blind_at_every_control is a union over the controls that RAN, not a proof that nothing could hide there; f32, one machine, INSTANCE, nothing timed. 273 accelerator tests pass.

value.headline: - [ ] G044 — CUDA ARCHAEOLOGY / FRONT B (S015): the CUDA Capability Ledger with every field the steer names (capability_id, CUDA mechanism, why it exists, underlying problem, Apple equivalent, current Hawking equivalent, semantic gap, performance gap, priority, test corpus, current winner, remaining limitation); exact CuMetal revision pinned with Apache-2.0 provenance, commit, license and notices preserved; CUDA reference corpus; differential oracle harness emitting CUDA_DIFFERENTIAL_RECEIPT. Never called "CUDA parity" unqualified. Proofs P1, P2. | status: IN_PROGRESS | risk: medium | tier: V3 || SEED PINNED 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/CUMETAL_PIN.json): NAMING CORRECTION FIRST -- there is NO repository literally named 'CuMetal'. The README self-identifies as CuMetal but the canonical owner/repo is Lulzx/cuda-metal; the steer names the project, not the slug. VERIFIED FROM THIS MACHINE against the GitHub API rather than accepted from the research that surfaced it: license Apache-2.0 (confirmed spdx_id), default branch main, pinned commit 19a702303dd29a1b25d668c6a6eca51302a2323c dated 2026-08-10T06:29:23Z. Its reported inputs (.cu via cumetalc, PTX with CFG/SSA, optional libcuda.dylib binary compat, NVVM IR) and its stated limitations (no dynamic parallelism, no multi-GPU/P2P, no graphics interop, no SASS, cooperative grid sync rejected, FP64 ~44-bit mantissa not IEEE binary64, incomplete CUDA/cuDNN/PTX coverage, experimental) are recorded in a SEPARATE field marked NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED because they came through a summarizing fetch, not a byte-exact read. NOTHING CLONED, NOTHING EXECUTED: P1 is NOT claimed, only the pin exists. No code vendored so the Apache-2.0 attribution obligation is not yet owed; when it is, LICENSE and NOTICE travel with it and modifications get marked (S015 §139). Two other candidates found and recorded, both NOASSERTION license: MEHDI342/CUDAM, Perinban/MetaXuda. || CCL BUILT 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/CUDA_CAPABILITY_LEDGER.json): 17 entries across ALL EIGHT capability classes, every one carrying the 12 fields S015 names, with a VALIDATOR THAT REFUSES AN INCOMPLETE ENTRY because a ledger with holes reads as a ledger with coverage. TWO DISCIPLINES ENFORCED IN CODE NOT INTENTION: (1) a semantic_gap of NONE IS a parity claim and REQUIRES evidence attached, so the steer's ban on unqualified 'CUDA parity' is now a property of the schema and nothing can drift into claiming parity by omission; (2) a performance_gap may not be marked measured without a RECEIPT PATH, which keeps the 3 things measured separate from the 14 not. THE SHAPE IS THE RESULT: 1 gap DELETED_BY_UNIFIED_MEMORY (host/device copy, 7.4x, P6), 7 PARTIAL, 8 LARGE, 1 UNKNOWN; 3 performance gaps measured / 14 unmeasured. Shared memory, atomics, synchronization, GEMM, reductions, streams and graphs are ALL LARGE, and GEMM sits BEHIND two of them, so the ledger makes the dependency visible instead of leaving it a surprise. MLX recorded as CURRENT WINNER wherever it wins (most of the math surface) -- a retention, not a defeat. One entry earns P0 from evidence collected elsewhere: CUDA Graphs targets per-launch overhead and the P7 size sweep already showed small kernels here are LAUNCH-BOUND, so the ledger connects them. ABSENCE FROM THIS LEDGER MEANS NOT YET STUDIED, NEVER NOT NEEDED. P1 and P2 both REMAIN OPEN: nothing has been cloned, built or run from the pinned seed, and no CUDA differential exists. tools/accelerator/test_ccl.py 9 passed. || P1 SUBSTANTIALLY REPRODUCED 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/CUMETAL_P1_REPRODUCTION.json) -- THIS SUPERSEDES THE 'NOTHING CLONED, NOTHING EXECUTED' LINE ABOVE. Cloned Lulzx/cuda-metal at EXACTLY 19a702303dd29a1b25d668c6a6eca51302a2323c, HEAD confirmed to match the pin, 7.9M. CONFIGURED AND BUILT WITH ZERO COMPILE ERRORS (cmake 4.3.3, exit 0), producing cumetalc, libcumetal.dylib, cumetal, air_inspect, air_validate, cumetal-ptx2llvm, ptx_diff. ITS OWN SUITE: 194/216 pass (90%) on system clang, and 198/216 (92%) with CUMETAL_CUDA_CLANG pointed at Homebrew LLVM 21.1.8 which carries an nvptx64 target Apple's clang lacks. LICENSE CAVEAT DISCHARGED: the pin receipt marked Apache-2.0 NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED because it came via a summarizing fetch; the LICENSE file is now READ BYTE-FOR-BYTE from the cloned tree and hashed. No NOTICE file upstream so no NOTICE obligation attaches; nothing vendored here regardless. A PREDICTION I GOT WRONG: I recorded across several blocks that the missing METAL DEVELOPER TOOLCHAIN was the blocker for building this seed. IT IS NOT -- the seed builds fine without it. The FAILURES come from the host clang lacking an NVPTX TARGET, a different tool entirely; xcrun metal accounts for the 148 SKIPS, not the failures. I asserted a plausible-sounding cause from inference and only RUNNING it exposed that. BOTH remaining blockers are MISSING TOOLCHAINS, NOT PLATFORM WALLS, and neither is characterised as one. P1 is SUBSTANTIALLY reproduced, NOT fully: 18 tests still fail, 148 skip, and no CUDA source compiles end-to-end here. P2 UNAFFECTED AND STILL OPEN -- no NVIDIA hardware exists so no differential against real CUDA has been run. || EGB_HARDWARE_GATE for P2 = NOT_REQUIRED->READY_TO_ACQUIRE PENDING: P2 (a CUDA differential corpus) is BLOCKED ON EXACTLY ONE MISSING INPUT -- access to real NVIDIA/CUDA execution, whether a local Linux box, a borrowed machine or a cloud endpoint. Nothing software-side blocks it: the C2M frontend, the conformance reporter and the receipt schema all exist and would consume a differential the day one is available. Recorded as a NAMED GATE with its exact missing input per §129, NOT as a future/later parking lot. || THREE RECEIPTS BLAMED 'MLX KERNEL COMPILE' AND NONE OF THEM MEASURED IT 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_JIT_COMPILE.json): the CCL carried COMPILER.jit_kernel_compilation with performance_gap measured=FALSE, reason 'compile latency has not been measured', while the TIER 1, GPU-PACK and §77 receipts each explained away a discrepancy with that exact mechanism. AN ATTRIBUTION REPEATED THREE TIMES AND NEVER MEASURED is what this program has learned to test. MEASURED: 36.8 ms per DISTINCT kernel, NEAR-FLAT IN SOURCE SIZE (102 chars 36.8 ms, 5990 chars 43.6 -- a 59x source increase for 1.19x time, so it is a near-FIXED cost), and GENUINELY CACHED -- the same name and source recompiles in 0.24 ms against 110.65 cold = 460x, while a FRESH NAME with BYTE-IDENTICAL SOURCE still pays full price, which is what makes per-shape kernel naming expensive. THEN THE ATTRIBUTION WAS TESTED AND IT IS WRONG IN SCOPE TWICE. Five runs of the identical WorkUnit in ONE process: first 0.4196 s, warm median 0.1019, EXCESS 0.3176 s. Our two custom kernel compiles are 73.6 ms = 23.2% of it. The remainder is MLX's OWN first-use costs at 175.12 ms = 55.1% -- BUT 151.02 OF THOSE 175 MS ARE ONE THING, THE FIRST mx.array FROM A NUMPY BUFFER, which is DEVICE AND ALLOCATOR INITIALISATION AND NOT COMPILATION AT ALL. Every actual primitive kernel -- bitwise_and, right_shift, einsum, matmul, sum, random_normal -- costs 0.05 to 2.32 ms on first use, astype 11.87. So the phrase was wrong twice: not OUR kernels, and not COMPILATION. FULL DECOMPOSITION with nothing hidden: compiles 23.2%, MLX first-use 55.1%, cold read 2.5% (taken from the cache receipt, not re-measured), UNATTRIBUTED 19.2% -- and saying 19.2% is unattributed beats distributing it over the terms that were measured. A DEFECT IN MY FIRST PROBE THAT CHANGED WHAT THE DATA MEANT: body(k, extra_lines=0) was called as body(extra), so `extra` bound to the UNUSED first parameter and every kernel in that sweep had IDENTICAL SOURCE differing only in NAME. The name-only result SURVIVES and is informative; the apparent 'source size costs 113 ms' reading is VOID because the source never changed. AND THE 113 ms IS STILL UNEXPLAINED -- the corrected probe tested BOTH candidates, size (weak) and ORDER (late trivial 35.16 ms against early 36.77, ratio 0.96), and NEITHER reproduces it, so a median of six that a corrected probe cannot reproduce is recorded as a caution about small-n medians rather than dropped. LEDGER: COMPILER.jit_kernel_compilation moves unmeasured -> MEASURED with a receipt path, CCL now 14 of 20 performance gaps measured. ALL THREE AFFECTED RECEIPTS AMENDED IN PLACE so anyone reaching one finds the correction attached; the DIRECTION of every affected statement is unchanged -- the first run really is slower and really must not be quoted as a baseline -- only the named MECHANISM changes. CLAIM BOUNDARY: mx.fast.metal_kernel JIT ONLY; xcrun metal AOT is ABSENT on this machine so no AOT comparison exists, and CUDA's nvrtc latency is unmeasured because no NVIDIA hardware exists, so this measures OUR side of the gap alone. Every cost here is PER PROCESS and amortises to zero by the second WorkUnit -- it matters for short-lived processes and for any measurement whose first run is quoted as a baseline, which is exactly how it contaminated three receipts. No kernel changed, so no performance claim about any kernel moves. 191 tests pass. || SPECIALIZATION CONSTANTS BUY NOTHING MEASURABLE, AND MY EXPLANATION DIED IN THE NEXT EXPERIMENT 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_SPEC_CONSTANTS.json): the CCL carried COMPILER.specialization_constants with measured=FALSE, reason 'specialisation was never isolated as its own arm' -- AIR has had the field since P3 and the forge tunes one, but nothing ever compared BAKING A VALUE INTO THE SOURCE against READING IT FROM A BUFFER. TWO CASES ON PURPOSE, because they test DIFFERENT claims: a SCALAR multiplier, where specialization saves ONE broadcast load (PREDICTED INDISTINGUISHABLE), and a LOOP BOUND, where it changes WHAT THE COMPILER CAN PROVE because a literal bound can be unrolled and a buffer bound cannot (PREDICTED A REAL DIFFERENCE). SCALAR: CONFIRMED INDISTINGUISHABLE, 1.62% margin against 7.95% noise. LOOP: NOT CONFIRMED -- 2.59% and the buffer arm failed the gate at 14.66%, so the instrument refused to call it either way. I OFFERED AN EXPLANATION -- that loop was MEMORY BOUND, so unrolling changes the instruction stream and not the traffic, and the traffic is the wall -- AND THEN TESTED IT rather than letting it stand as a story that happens to fit a null result: one load then 256 fused multiply-adds, so loop overhead and the branch are the ONLY difference. IT IS REFUTED. INDISTINGUISHABLE with CLEAN ARMS at 5.25% and 4.96%, and the LITERAL IS 3.09% SLOWER. So the honest result is that specialization constants buy nothing measurable on this backend in either shape, and my prediction was wrong in both loop cases. WHAT WOULD SETTLE THE MECHANISM CANNOT BE DONE HERE: whether the literal loop is actually unrolled is a question about GENERATED CODE, and xcrun metal is ABSENT -- the same named gate that blocks AOT metallib -- so 'the compiler already handles a uniform runtime bound as well as a literal' is a HYPOTHESIS, not a finding. A DISTINCTION THAT MUST NOT BE CONFLATED: the FORGE tunes a TILE SIZE and calls it a specialization, measuring 2096/2091/2258 GFLOP/s across tiles 8/16/32 -- but a TILE SIZE CHANGES THE ALGORITHM (threadgroup allocation, loop structure, access pattern) while this measures a CONSTANT that changes only where a number comes from, so reading the forge's tile result as evidence that specialization constants pay would be wrong. CONSEQUENCE FOR AIR: specialization constants are an EXPRESSIVENESS feature on this backend and NOT a performance one -- they still earn their place, because a program that names its constants is a program whose IDENTITY KEY can include them and that is what the forge cache depends on, but NO SPEED CLAIM MAY BE ATTACHED TO THEM. CORRECTNESS FIRST: both pairs verified BIT-IDENTICAL at exactly 0.0 before timing -- here a DIFFERENT answer would have meant the arms were not the same computation at all. 200 reps and 40 warmup, the program's own stability floor. LEDGER: COMPILER.specialization_constants moves unmeasured -> MEASURED with a receipt path, CCL now 15 of 20 performance gaps measured. Of the 5 that remain, THREE ARE CORRECTLY UNMEASURABLE by their own reasons (indexing is not independently measurable, numerical diagnostics is not a performance capability, a frontend gap is about COVERAGE not speed), ONE is the hardware gate (MULTI_DEVICE.peer_access) and ONE is the instrument benchmarking itself. 191 tests pass.

value.headline: - [ ] G045 — C2M / FRONT C (S015): CUDA/PTX subset and runtime subset lowering into AIR and executing on Metal without NVIDIA hardware, graded against the conformance ladder C2M-T0..T5. No claim of "CUDA support" without a named tier. Proof P4: a translated CUDA kernel matches the reference. | status: IN_PROGRESS | risk: high | tier: V3 || C2M-T0 LIVE 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_FRONT_C_P4.json): four trivial elementwise CUDA kernels PARSED, lowered into AIR, and EXECUTED ON THE APPLE GPU with no NVIDIA hardware in the path -- vadd/vmul/vsub/krelu, all four max_abs_err 0.000e+00 vs a numpy oracle. THE REFUSALS ARE THE MORE IMPORTANT HALF: shared memory, loops, atomics, __syncthreads, device printf, fp64, multiple stores, non-pointer operand, missing thread index and any expression outside the 4 supported forms are all rejected WITH THE CONSTRUCT NAMED (6/6 in the receipt, 12 more pinned by tests), because a silent mistranslation is worse than a rejection -- it produces a plausible wrong answer with a passing test beside it. P4 IS NOT FULLY CLOSED AND I DO NOT CLAIM IT IS: the steer's P4 means matching a CUDA REFERENCE, and the oracle here is NUMPY ON CPU because no NVIDIA hardware exists. So this is P4 in the weaker sense of 'matches a reference oracle' only; real CUDA semantics, float behaviour, ordering and error behaviour are UNTESTED and P2 stays open. Also NOT a C expression parser -- a PATTERN MATCHER over 4 forms, stated in the module itself. Conformance reporter refuses to claim a tier it did not earn: T0 only when a kernel actually executed and matched, NONE when none did, and T1-T5 each carry an explicit NOT CLAIMED with a reason. Nothing timed, so no performance claim. 37 accelerator tests pass. || PTX INPUT LIVE, 1.0% CORPUS COVERAGE 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_C2M_PTX.json): C2M now accepts PTX, the steer's SECOND named input form, and parses THE PINNED SEED'S OWN 291 .ptx FILES rather than PTX I wrote to suit my parser. 3 of 291 translate through AIR onto the Apple GPU and ALL 3 match a numpy oracle. THAT IS 1.0% AND 1.0% IS WHAT IT SAYS -- 288 refused, each with the instruction NAMED. AN INCREMENT THAT BOUGHT NOTHING, recorded because it is the useful part: the refusal histogram showed cvta.to.global.u64 blocking 43 files, by far the most common single reason, so supporting it looked like the obvious next step. Added it as a pointer-identity passthrough plus mad.lo.u32 / mul.wide.u32 / mul.wide.s32 / cvt.s64.s32. COVERAGE DID NOT MOVE AT ALL -- the blocker simply became ld.global.u32 on THE SAME 43 FILES. Those files were NEVER ONE INSTRUCTION AWAY. Adding the most-frequent refusal reason is NOT the same as adding the BINDING CONSTRAINT, because a refusal histogram ranks SYMPTOMS and stops at whichever instruction the parser happened to reach first. Honest read: this subset is FAR from the corpus, not one step from it. Still C2M-T0 -- no runtime, no memory API, no streams, so T1-T5 remain explicitly NOT CLAIMED; oracle is numpy not CUDA so still NOT a differential and P2 stays open. 61 tests pass. || C2M-T1 EARNED, AND THE CONDITION ON 'DELETE THE COPY' 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_C2M_T1_RUNTIME.json): every C2M receipt since T0 recorded the SAME blocker -- 'no runtime, no memory API, no streams'. tools/accelerator/cuda_runtime.py is that layer: cudaMalloc, cudaMemcpy in BOTH directions, a <<<grid,block>>> launch, cudaDeviceSynchronize and cudaFree, parsed from CUDA HOST source and executed through AIR. 4 host programs run in TWO MODES (FAITHFUL, which really allocates and really copies, and UNIFIED, which deletes both per S015 §9), all 4 matching numpy and AGREEING BIT-FOR-BIT between modes; conformance_t1 claims T1 ONLY when both hold. THE REAL FINDING IS A CONDITION NOTHING IN THIS PROGRAM HAD STATED: §9 says delete the unnecessary CUDA-era concept and §125 calls unified memory a weapon, and BOTH ARE RIGHT ONLY WHEN NOBODY WRITES. In CUDA a host-to-device copy is a SNAPSHOT; an alias is a LIVE REFERENCE. A program that writes its host buffer AFTER the copy and BEFORE the launch gets a DIFFERENT ANSWER. DEMONSTRATED NOT ASSERTED: same program, -1.839037 under faithful semantics vs 997.035 under aliasing = 999.36 divergence IN EXACTLY ONE ELEMENT with every other element BIT-IDENTICAL, which is the worst shape a bug can have because an aggregate check passes. may_delete_copies() REFUSES such a program and NAMES the statement; the guard is bypassable only by a private flag used in the demonstration and its test, because A REFUSAL NOBODY HAS WATCHED BE NECESSARY IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM ONE THAT IS MERELY CAUTIOUS. A second test pins that a write AFTER the launch does NOT block the deletion, so the guard is about the SNAPSHOT WINDOW and not about host writes in general. THE CCL ENTRY IS QUALIFIED: MEMORY.host_device_copy was recorded DELETED_BY_UNIFIED_MEMORY unconditionally and now carries the condition. WHAT THE DELETION BUYS AT PROGRAM LEVEL: 1.69x at 2^20 and 1.73x at 2^22 (clean arms 2.45% / 8.39%), NOT the 7.4x P6 measured -- P6 timed the COPY, this times a PROGRAM that also does kernel work and host interpretation, and quoting 7.4x as what a port gains would be wrong. A THIRD HARNESS DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED: the first run returned NO_CLAIM at both sizes because the timed function rebuilt 16 MiB of host numpy arrays every call -- COMMON-MODE so it did not bias direction, it DILUTED the margin until the gate refused a real result. Three times now the instrument has been the thing under measurement, and the pattern is that ANY per-call setup inside an arm is suspect. SIX REFUSALS FIRE BY NAME: streams, async copies, managed memory, memset, an unrecognised host statement, and a launch reading device memory that was allocated but never written (CUDA leaves it uninitialised; refusing beats silently reading zeros). T2 IS BLOCKED BY THE FRONTEND NOT THE BACKEND and the reporter says so: AIR has GEMM, reduction, scan, softmax and attention and NONE is reachable through C2M, whose kernel parser handles 4 elementwise forms. LAUNCH GEOMETRY IS PARSED AND IGNORED -- AIR picks its own grid -- so a kernel depending on blockDim would be mistranslated and this subset cannot express one. Oracle is numpy so P2 stays open. 128 tests pass. || C2M-T2 BY RECOGNITION, AND THE NEAR-MISSES ARE THE EVIDENCE 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_C2M_T2_IDIOM.json): T1 named this blocker precisely -- AIR has GEMM, reduction, scan, softmax and attention and NONE was reachable through C2M, whose T0 frontend is a pattern matcher over 4 elementwise expression forms and cannot express a loop, shared memory or a barrier. Closed WITHOUT writing a C compiler: c2m_idiom.recognize identifies that a kernel IS a known algorithm and hands it to AIR's implementation. The textbook CUDA TILED GEMM (__shared__ As/Bs, k-tile loop, 2 __syncthreads) and BLOCK REDUCTION (sdata, halving tree, barrier in loop) both recognised and EXECUTED, 6/6 matching numpy including a 48x80x32 that is NOT a multiple of the 16 tile and a 4194311-element reduction that is NOT a power of two. THE MECHANISM IS RECOGNITION, NOT COMPILATION, and that is a FIRST-CLASS FIELD on the conformance report rather than a footnote, because a tier number must never read as CUDA coverage. THE HAZARD IS THE INTERESTING PART: recognition is A CLAIM ABOUT SEMANTICS -- saying 'this is a tiled GEMM' asserts the kernel computes A@B, and a loose match silently substitutes a DIFFERENT computation that runs fast and returns a plausible wrong answer. WORSE, THE USUAL DEFENCE FAILS: grading the output against an oracle derived from the idiom is CIRCULAR, because the same recognition chose the oracle. WHAT BREAKS THE CIRCLE IS THE NEGATIVE DIRECTION -- 12 NEAR-MISS KERNELS, each differing from its idiom in EXACTLY ONE respect: transposed tile index (computes A@B^T), one barrier removed (a race), both removed, rectangular tiles, accumulator starting at 1, column-major store, product instead of sum, identity 1 instead of 0 for a sum, doubling instead of halving sweep, an illegal 100-wide threadgroup, and a plain elementwise kernel. ALL 12 REFUSED, each naming the element that failed -- and conformance_t2 REFUSES TO CLAIM THE TIER unless every near-miss was rejected, so a recognizer that accepts everything cannot earn T2. THE TWO DOORS DO NOT OVERLAP and a test pins it: c2m.translate REFUSES both idioms by name (__shared__, __syncthreads) while recognize REFUSES the elementwise kernel, so a kernel that is neither trivially elementwise nor an exact known idiom is refused by BOTH. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, said plainly: it does not compile a loop, shared memory or a barrier, and the SAME GEMM written with different variable names or a different guard style is REFUSED even though it computes the same thing -- brittleness inherent to recognition, and the reason T3 explicitly says 2 idioms will not carry a real CUDA project. LEDGER HOLE CLOSED: S015 §12 names FRONTEND PARSING as a COMPILER capability and the CCL never had an entry for it, which by the ledger's own rule meant NOT YET STUDIED. Added as a 20th entry marked LARGE, with the seed's real clang-based frontend as CURRENT WINNER and the honest limitation that ADDING DOORS WIDENS WHAT IS REACHABLE WITHOUT WIDENING WHAT IS COMPILABLE. Ledger now 17 PARTIAL / 2 LARGE / 1 DELETED. The recognised GEMM runs AIR's TILED strategy which already LOSES to MLX, so this closes a FRONTEND gap and changes NO performance claim. Oracle is numpy so P2 stays open. 142 tests pass. || TWO INSTRUMENTS IN A ROW RANKED SYMPTOMS 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_C2M_CORPUS_CENSUS.json): every C2M receipt since T2 has carried the same blocker -- 'no real open CUDA project has been run, and recognition of 2 idioms will not carry one'. THE CORPUS WAS ALREADY ON DISK: the pinned seed holds 24 real .cu files and 35 __global__ kernels, 11 files under tests/cuda_projects (sgemm, softmax, reduction, transpose, flash attention, a raytracer, ggml ops). C2M TRANSLATED 1 OF 35 AND RECOGNISED 0. THEN THE INSTRUMENT BUILT TO AVOID THE PTX RECEIPT'S MISTAKE MADE THE SAME MISTAKE. The PTX receipt had already found that adding the most-frequent refusal reason moved coverage by NOTHING, because a histogram stops at whichever construct the parser reached first -- so this block collected, PER KERNEL, the FULL set of constructs C2M cannot express, checked independently rather than first-wins, and plotted coverage against supporting the top k. It said 48.6% at k=2 and 68.6% at k=5. IT IS WRONG: the curve counts the ABSENCE OF BLOCKERS I PROBED FOR, not TRANSLATABILITY. Adding the store-expression check collapses it -- only ONE of the 35 kernels has a store inside the T0 pattern set and THAT NUMBER IS FLAT AT 1 ACROSS THE WHOLE CURVE, so supporting all 14 constructs takes construct-fit from 2 to 35 while translatable stays at 1. CAUGHT BECAUSE TWO KERNELS NEED ZERO OF THE PROBED CONSTRUCTS AND WERE REFUSED ANYWAY: a curve reporting 5.7% reachable at k=0 while the frontend translates 0 of those 2 is measuring something other than its own name. THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IS NAMED AT LAST AND IT IS NOT A GPU FEATURE: C2M matches five fixed expression shapes and real kernels write anything else. C2M IS NOT A C COMPILER, and the corpus says that is the whole distance to T3 -- not shared memory, not barriers, not atomics. A SUPPORTED OPERATION WAS BEING REFUSED OVER A VARIABLE NAME: the two zero-construct kernels compute c[index] = a[index] + b[index], the T0 add form EXACTLY, and the frontend hardcoded `i` in its store regex and in every pattern. The index variable is now DISCOVERED from the binding of the global thread index and the patterns are rebuilt around that identifier; translated kernels go 1 -> 4 of 35 (2.9% -> 11.4%) and ALL FOUR EXECUTE ON THE APPLE GPU AT max_abs_err 0.0, because a wider door that mistranslates is worse than a narrow one. Index variables in the corpus: i, id, id, index. AND THE T2 RECOGNISER MISSES THE REAL IDIOMS ON A DECLARATION, NOT AN ALGORITHM: the seed carries a REAL tiled GEMM and a REAL block reduction -- the two algorithms the door knows -- and it matched NEITHER, failing on the FIRST required fragment both times. The real GEMM writes '__shared__ float As[BLOCKSIZE * BLOCKSIZE]' where the recogniser demands a 2-D literal; the real reduction writes 'extern __shared__ float sdata[]' where it demands a sized array. The T2 receipt PREDICTED this brittleness in those words and PREDICTING IS NOT MEASURING; it is measured now, on code nobody wrote to suit the recogniser. NOT FIXED, AND WHY: loosening the fragments to match these two files would be fitting the recogniser to the corpus in front of it, and the hazard the near-miss suite exists against is that a loose match SUBSTITUTES A DIFFERENT COMPUTATION -- widening recognition needs its own near-miss evidence. PREDICTIONS: kernels 60-100 MISSED LOW at 35; translates 1-3 CONFIRMED; recognised 0-2 CONFIRMED at the bottom; 'top 5 unlocks under 10%' REFUTED AS STATED by the curve at 68.6% AND RIGHT ABOUT THE THING THAT MATTERS, since real translatability at k=5 is 2.9% -- I predicted the right answer and the instrument I built to check it disagreed because it measured the wrong quantity. T3 IS STILL NOT CLAIMED; what changed is that the distance is now a NUMBER. CLAIM BOUNDARY: ONE project, and it is a CUDA-to-Metal project's own test suite so it skews toward small self-contained kernels; the construct probes are REGEXES not a parse, so anything behind a macro or typedef is unseen; store-in-pattern-set is NECESSARY NOT SUFFICIENT so translatable remains an upper bound; nothing timed; oracle is numpy so P2 stays open. 246 accelerator tests pass. || THE BRITTLENESS WAS HIDING A SEMANTIC DIFFERENCE 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_C2M_SGEMM_IDIOM.json): the previous entry left this as a block's work -- 'widening recognition needs its own near-miss evidence'. DOING IT FOUND THAT THE OBVIOUS FIX WAS A TRAP. Loosening the tiled_gemm fragments until they matched the seed's real sgemm_shmem.cu would have SUBSTITUTED A DIFFERENT COMPUTATION: that kernel computes alpha*A@B + beta*C and AIR's matmul computes A@B. The syntactic difference -- 1-D shared tiles with a SYMBOLIC extent, flattened indexing -- was the visible one; the alpha/beta term was the one that mattered. AND THE SEED'S OWN TEST WOULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT: sgemm_shmem.cu's main() sets alpha = 1.0f and beta = 0.0f, exactly where a plain matmul agrees to the last bit. MEASURED: at alpha=1 beta=0 the plain matmul is EXACT against the real semantics (3.1e-07, the same number as the correct path); at alpha=2 beta=0.5 it is wrong by 0.506 relative; at alpha=-1.5 beta=2.0 by 1.565. A MISTAKE INVISIBLE ON THE CORPUS'S OWN INPUTS AND ORDER-1 EVERYWHERE ELSE is the worst shape this program keeps finding, and here it was found BEFORE shipping rather than after. BUILT AS A SEPARATE IDIOM, NOT A LOOSER ONE: sgemm_alpha_beta is matched BEFORE tiled_gemm because it is the STRICTER claim, the old door still refuses the new shape by name, and execution composes the scaling around AIR's matmul so the answer is alpha*(A@B) + beta*C rather than the bare product -- correct at three alpha/beta settings to 2.9-3.2e-07. THE TILE IS NOT IN THE KERNEL and recognition does not pretend otherwise: BLOCKSIZE is a TEMPLATE PARAMETER, so the source does not contain the value, recognize() returns tile=None and execute_idiom REFUSES without dims['tile'] instead of guessing. TEN NEAR-MISSES, TEN REFUSALS, each differing in exactly ONE respect -- beta dropped, alpha and beta swapped, B tile index transposed, one barrier removed, both removed, accumulator starting at one, rectangular tile, row and column sources swapped, A staged from the wrong stride, product replaced by a sum -- and TWO OF THE TEN differ only in the SEMANTIC term, which is precisely the class the naive widening would have let through. THE REAL REDUCTION IS REFUSED AND THE REASON IS DIFFERENT IN KIND: it is a GRID-STRIDE cooperative-groups reduction with an unrolled if-cascade and a __shfl_down_sync warp stage, using cg::sync rather than __syncthreads and no halving tree at all. The GEMM differed in SYNTAX plus one semantic term and could be met by naming a second idiom precisely; the reduction differs in ALGORITHM, so matching it means recognising a FAMILY rather than a shape and that is NOT what this door does. CORPUS POSITION, honestly: kernels recognised goes 0 -> 1 of 35. The census's binding constraint is UNCHANGED -- C2M is not a C compiler -- and what moved is that the recogniser now matches a kernel nobody wrote to suit it, with the semantic trap measured rather than avoided. CLAIM BOUNDARY: still RECOGNITION not compilation, no loop or barrier is compiled; STILL NAME-BRITTLE, since the fragments match threadRow/threadCol/tmp/bkIdx/dotIdx by name and the same kernel with different identifiers is still refused; T3 NOT CLAIMED because one real kernel is not a real project; nothing timed and the recognised path runs AIR's tiled matmul which already loses to MLX, so no performance claim moves; oracle is float64 numpy of the kernel's own written semantics, so P2 stays open. 252 accelerator tests pass. || THE PARSER I WAS ABOUT TO BUILD WOULD HAVE REACHED NOTHING 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_C2M_CORPUS_DENOMINATOR.json): the corpus census named the binding constraint in its own words -- 'C2M matches five fixed expression shapes and real kernels write anything else. C2M IS NOT A C COMPILER, and the corpus says that is the whole distance to T3 -- not shared memory, not barriers, not atomics'. I set out to build that parser. MEASURING FIRST REFUTED THE CLAIM ON ITS OWN CORPUS. An elementwise AIR program needs every leaf of the store to be a pointer PARAMETER indexed by the thread index -- a DATA-FLOW condition NO PARSER HOWEVER COMPLETE CAN SUPPLY -- and exactly 7 of the 27 computing kernels satisfy it, of which 6 ALREADY TRANSLATE and the 7th is blocked by fp64, a dtype boundary not a grammar one. NET YIELD OF AN UNLIMITED C EXPRESSION PARSER: ZERO KERNELS. Not one computing kernel is refused for its expression form; the histogram is shared memory 7, loops 5, fp64 2, index form 2, parameter types 3, multi-store 1. THE DISTANCE TO T3 IS LOOPS, SHARED MEMORY AND BARRIERS, blocking 20 of 27 -- EXACTLY WHAT THE CENSUS SAID IT WAS NOT. WHY THE CENSUS GOT IT BACKWARDS: its claim rested on 'store-in-pattern-set is FLAT AT 1 ACROSS THE WHOLE CURVE', and THE SAME BLOCK then shipped the index-variable fix that took translated kernels 1 -> 4 -- the sentence was written from the pre-fix number and never re-derived after its own fix landed, so the number it rested on was STALE BY THE END OF THE BLOCK THAT PRODUCED IT. THE DENOMINATOR WAS NEVER WHAT IT READ AS: 9 of the 36 __global__ kernels have EMPTY BODIES -- extern "C" signature/ABI probes that compute nothing -- so nine slots are UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION and every C2M receipt has quoted coverage over 35. They were also refused for THE WRONG REASON: their parameters are UNNAMED so parameter parsing reached them first and said 'cannot parse parameter const float*', true and inviting a reader to go fix a parameter parser for a kernel no frontend can ever translate; empty bodies are now refused FIRST and by name, with a test asserting the message does NOT mention parameters. AND THE CORPUS CANNOT CARRY A COVERAGE CLAIM AT ALL: SEVEN of its nine elementwise-shaped kernels compute a[idx] + b[idx], so the corpus holds ONE DISTINCT ELEMENTWISE COMPUTATION written seven times across four spellings differing in index name, factor order, guard style and dtype -- a coverage fraction over it is measuring REPETITION. WHAT DID MOVE COVERAGE WAS SPELLING, NOT POWER: 'int id = blockDim.x * blockIdx.x + threadIdx.x' is integer multiplication written the other way round, IDENTICAL SEMANTICS, and it was refused as 'no recognised global thread index' -- the ADDEND order was already accepted and the FACTOR order was not, which is exactly what hid it. Translated 5 -> 6 of 27, and all six EXECUTE on the Apple GPU at 4099 elements (prime, a multiple of no threadgroup width) against a float64 oracle at worst 5.01e-08. THE WIDENING IS EXACTLY COMMUTATIVITY AND NO WIDER: four near misses stay refused, each MEANING something else -- blockIdx.x + blockDim.x * threadIdx.x is a DIFFERENT index, plus wrong-axis factor, wrong-axis addend, and the same factor twice. SECOND TIME a supported computation was rejected over spelling (the census found the index VARIABLE NAME hardcoded to `i`), so a pattern matcher's misses are dominated by SPELLING and that is now measured rather than observed once. A DEFECT IN MY OWN PROBE: the first reachability probe counted the THREAD INDEX VARIABLE inside a[id] as a data operand and reported 0 of 27 reachable -- while six kernels demonstrably translate and execute; A PROBE WHOSE ANSWER CONTRADICTS A DIRECTLY MEASURED FACT IS BROKEN, NOT SURPRISING, and that is what caught it. THIRD TIME this program has hit 'the most-visible refusal reason is not the binding constraint' -- the PTX receipt measured it, the census's own coverage curve measured the wrong quantity -- AND THE FIRST TIME IT WAS CAUGHT BEFORE THE BLOCK WAS SPENT ON THE WRONG BUILD. SHIPPED: empty-body refusal ordered first; c2m.split_kernels, brace-matched so a multi-kernel file is not swallowed by translate()'s greedy body regex; c2m.census reporting DISTINCT COMPUTATIONS beside kernel counts, with elementwise_shaped labelled AN UPPER BOUND because the cooperative check is a regex blind to a shuffle behind a device-function call (softmax_warp is counted elementwise and is a warp reduction, pinned by a test); and the index in all four commutations from ONE shared pattern source so INDEX_BINDING and GRID_IDX cannot drift apart. The census receipt is AMENDED IN PLACE. CLAIM BOUNDARY: ONE corpus, and it is a CUDA-to-Metal project's OWN TEST SUITE, so the zero yield is a fact about THIS corpus and not a general claim that expression parsing is unnecessary for CUDA -- a corpus of real application kernels could invert it; the reachability probe is regexes not a parse so 7 is an upper bound in both directions; T3 STILL NOT CLAIMED and the distance is renamed, not shortened; nothing timed; oracle is float64 numpy not CUDA so P2 stays open. 268 accelerator tests pass. || AMENDED BY S016 §38-§40: C2M is no longer judged primarily on synthetic kernels. T3 requires SEVERAL REAL open CUDA codebases/slices taken through parse -> dependency closure -> capability gaps -> coherent cluster implementation -> execution on Metal -> numeric comparison, refusing unsupported semantics explicitly. T4 requires a REAL AI workload crossing CUDA source -> AIR -> Metal with multiple interacting capabilities; NO HAND-SHAPED DEMO COUNTS AS T4. C2M is the BOOTSTRAP, not the destination: every translated workload is profiled, its CUDA-era assumptions named, and an Apple-native replacement A/B'd against it.
