value.headline: - [ ] G046 — APPLE-NATIVE IMPROVEMENT / FRONT D (S015): native kernels, memory, fusion and unified-memory exploitation that beat the naive translated path, with the Metal Improvement Score tracking semantic coverage and native improvement SEPARATELY. Existing winners (MLX, Apple primitives, llama.cpp Metal) are retained as qualified implementations where they win; replacement requires evidence, not authorship preference. Proof P5: Accelerator-native beats naive translation on a useful operation OR explains why it cannot. | status: IN_PROGRESS | risk: high | tier: V3 || PROOF P5 PASSES 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_FRONT_D_P5.json): FIRST TIMING IN THE ACCELERATOR PROGRAM. Three arms in a protected window, lake fill SIGSTOPped, all clearing a 10% IQR gate, margin required to clear BOTH arms' noise before a winner is declared. MLX baseline 1.329 ms | naive translation (3 separate kernels, what a faithful CUDA port gives) 0.866 ms | ONE FUSED AIR PROGRAM 0.507 ms. = 1.71x over naive translation (margin 70.99% vs noise 5.92%) and 2.62x over MLX (margin 162.2% vs noise 4.08%). CORRECTNESS CHECKED FIRST at 9.537e-07 -- a faster wrong answer is not a result. WHAT PRODUCED THE WIN MATTERS MORE THAN THE NUMBER: it is FUSION -- 3 dispatches and 3 full passes over memory collapse to 1 and 1, and the op is MEMORY BOUND so removing passes is the ENTIRE mechanism. This is NOT evidence our per-op kernel craft beats MLX's; MLX does not fuse this chain automatically so it materialises 2 intermediates the fused program never writes. MLX REMAINS THE QUALIFIED WINNER WHEREVER IT WINS (§141). Metal Improvement Score keeps semantic coverage and native improvement in SEPARATE fields (§86) so a tier can never be read as a speedup. SCOPE: one chain (mul->relu->silu), one shape (2^24 f32), one dtype, one machine, INSTANCE. Microbenchmark only -- no sustained or thermal evidence, and NO HCLI WorkUnit throughput measured, so it does NOT yet translate into the metric that actually counts (§77). || PROOF P7 PASSES 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_FRONT_D_P7.json): A GRAVITY REPRESENTATION EXECUTES NATIVELY. ws_rtn_q4_g64 (4.25 bpw grouped absmax, the representation the KernelPlanner actually selected for model #2's experts) runs DIRECTLY on the GPU -- the kernel reads packed nibbles + f16 group scales and accumulates the matvec, and THE DENSE TENSOR IS NEVER WRITTEN ANYWHERE, which is exactly what §19 demands. Graded on a REAL Qwen3-30B-A3B routed-expert tensor (model.layers.0.mlp.experts.0.gate_proj.weight, 768x2048, bf16 on disk), matching the representation's own answer to 2.861e-06 vs 3.816e-03 tolerance. PERFORMANCE IS CONDITIONAL AND THE CONDITION IS THE FINDING: NO advantage at 6 MiB or 64 MiB (both arms launch/occupancy-bound, so reading 7.5x fewer bytes buys NOTHING), then 2.08x at 256 MiB where it becomes bandwidth-bound, both arms inside the gate. Win is smaller than the 7.5x byte ratio because the native kernel TRADES ARITHMETIC FOR TRAFFIC (unpacking + scales) rather than getting the reduction free. CONSEQUENCE FOR MODEL #2: one expert is 6 MiB, BELOW the crossover, so representation-native execution does NOT pay for a single expert in isolation -- the advantage is an argument about BATCHING enough of the expert table to become bandwidth-bound. I REJECTED ONE OF MY OWN DATA POINTS: 16384x8192 reported 3.56x but reads 68 MiB against the 34 MiB of the point below it while reporting a SHORTER time, which a bandwidth-bound kernel cannot do; its 44.11% IQR says the same. My margin-over-noise escape hatch ADMITTED it (256% margin cleared 5x the 44% noise), so that hatch is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT -- a large margin on an IMPOSSIBLE result is evidence the measurement is broken, not that the effect is strong. bench.compare now carries an explicit implausibility rejection. NOT AN ADEQUACY CLAIM: weight cosine 0.9940 per tensor and LOCAL ADEQUACY DOES NOT COMPOSE; no model was executed. || TILED GEMM: THREE CCL GAPS CLOSE, MLX KEEPS THE CROWN 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_GEMM.json): EXECUTION.shared_memory, EXECUTION.synchronization and MATH.gemm were ALL recorded LARGE with GEMM sitting BEHIND the other two. One 16x16 tiled kernel with threadgroup tiles + 2 barriers per k-tile exercises all three FOR REAL; all three move to PARTIAL with a MEASURED performance gap and a receipt. CCL now 10 PARTIAL / 5 LARGE / 1 DELETED / 1 UNKNOWN, 6 performance gaps measured vs 11 unmeasured (was 3 vs 14). THE KERNEL LOSES TO MLX AT EVERY SIZE: 12733 GFLOP/s vs ours 2683 at 2048^2 = 4.7x. THAT IS THE CORRECT OUTCOME TO RECORD, NOT BURY -- §141 says capability does not require Hawking authorship and §142 says replacement needs EVIDENCE; the evidence says DO NOT REPLACE. MLX retained as qualified winner, this GEMM must not be used. It loses because it is a SCALAR tile with no simdgroup matrix ops, no double buffering, no register blocking, no vectorised loads, while MLX reaches the matrix hardware. I DID NOT TRUST MY OWN PASSING CHECK: an exact 0.000e+00 error across 512 accumulations looked too good, so I BROKE THE KERNEL TWICE first -- barriers removed gives 54.46 error, index transposed gives 98.89 -- proving the check CAN FAIL, and the barrier control is how we know the barriers are doing something rather than being decorative. Hand case [[1,2],[3,4]]@[[5,6],[7,8]] exact. CLOSES NOTHING ABOUT PERFORMANCE and was never going to; it establishes CAPABILITY. AIR STILL CANNOT EXPRESS THIS KERNEL -- no tiling, no threadgroup allocation, and only barrier REPRESENTATION not barrier LOWERING -- so this is hand-written MSL sitting BESIDE AIR, not produced by it. 61 tests pass. || SIMDGROUP MATRIX MATMUL IN AIR, AND THE 2048 COLLAPSE IS THE FINDING 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_SIMDGROUP_GEMM.json): the GEMM receipt named simdgroup matrix ops as where the gap to MLX lived. AIR now has them as a SECOND MATMUL STRATEGY, worth ~1.6x over the scalar tile at every size (1.42x at 512, 1.62x at 1024 and 2048). AGAINST MLX THE RESULT SPLITS SHARPLY: 97.6% at 512, 91.3% at 1024, 36.7% AT 2048. The first two say the matrix units really WERE most of the gap at those sizes. THE THIRD SAYS MLX's ADVANTAGE AT SCALE IS SOMETHING ELSE ENTIRELY, because MLX ALREADY HAD simdgroup ops -- it is HIERARCHICAL BLOCKING (multiple simdgroups per threadgroup, threadgroup staging, operand reuse), none of which this kernel has: one 8x8 tile per simdgroup streams A and B straight from device memory every step, so at 2048 it is BANDWIDTH-BOUND on operands MLX reuses from faster storage. THE 2048 NUMBER IS THE HONEST HEADLINE because it is the size that matters for real work; MLX REMAINS QUALIFIED WINNER AT EVERY SIZE. BOTH STRATEGIES KEPT, loser not deleted: simdgroup wins on speed everywhere but REQUIRES every dimension to be a multiple of 8 and REFUSES otherwise rather than reading out of bounds, while tiled has NO shape constraint -- deleting tiled would have removed the only strategy that handles a 60x60 matmul. simdgroup emits NO barrier (a simdgroup runs in lockstep, synchronization implicit in SIMD width) and a test pins that against tiled's two so they cannot be conflated. CCL now 11 PARTIAL / 5 LARGE / 1 DELETED, 7 of 17 performance gaps measured; EXECUTION.warp_primitives moves UNKNOWN->PARTIAL (matrix ops work; shuffle, ballot, vote untouched and Apple divergence semantics UNCOMPARED to CUDA's). 75 tests pass. || REGISTER BLOCKING CONFIRMS THE DIAGNOSIS, AND RETRACTS A NUMBER I NEARLY KEPT 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_REGISTER_BLOCKING.json): the previous receipt DIAGNOSED MLX's 2048 advantage as HIERARCHICAL BLOCKING / OPERAND REUSE rather than simdgroup ops. That was FALSIFIABLE so I TESTED IT: give each simdgroup a 2x2 grid of 8x8 tiles so 4 loads feed 4 MACs instead of 2 feeding 1, doubling arithmetic intensity and changing nothing else. DIAGNOSIS HELD -- at 2048 the kernel goes 4703 -> 11576 GFLOP/s (2.48x), taking 36.7% of MLX to 96.0%. THE MORE IMPORTANT PART IS WHAT GOT RETRACTED: the first sweep showed 149.5% OF MLX AT 1024, which would have been the first AIR kernel to BEAT MLX at GEMM outright. MY RELIABILITY GATE REFUSED IT (block2 IQR 19.89% -> NO_CLAIM). Re-measured at 120 reps / 40 warmup, 1024 comes out at 0.9999 = EXACT PARITY, NOT a 1.5x win -- MLX itself measured 3963 GFLOP/s in the noisy run and 5801 in the clean one, so the apparent victory was MLX BEING UNDER-MEASURED, not us being fast. THE MOST EXCITING NUMBER IN THE SWEEP WAS THE LEAST TRUSTWORTHY ONE. WHAT STANDS: PARITY with MLX at 1024 (0.9999) and 2048 (0.96), MLX WINS 1.24x at 4096 (margin 19.19% vs 1.57% noise), 512 NO_CLAIM even at 120 reps (12.25% spread). PARITY IS NOT VICTORY and is not claimed as one; MLX remains qualified winner and at the LARGEST size measured it still wins outright. MATH.gemm performance gap updated from '36.7% of MLX' to 'parity to 2048, MLX 1.24x at 4096'. f32 only, square shapes, multiples of 16 for block=2, no batching, no transpose, no mixed precision, nothing run inside a model. 80 tests pass. || AIR REDUCTIONS + AN ASYMMETRY IN MY OWN GATE 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_REDUCTION.json): correct f32 SUM and MAX reduction in AIR, two-stage with simd_sum + 1 barrier, handling NON-POWER-OF-TWO sizes (rel_err 4.8e-07 to 1.0e-07). Barrier LOAD-BEARING: stripping it changes 1756.60 -> 1109.53. DELIBERATELY NOT ATOMIC -- atomics would collapse 3 passes to 1 but atomics are STILL A LARGE GAP in the ledger, and borrowing an unbuilt capability to look faster would be a lie about what executes. MLX WINS ~3x (0.343 at 2^20, 0.327 at 2^24) and is RETAINED; we lose to 3 separate launches and one element per thread. STATING THAT LOSS REQUIRED FIXING MY INSTRUMENT: compare() measured margin as |speedup-1|, BOUNDED BY 100% FOR ANY SLOWDOWN however severe, while a speedup is UNBOUNDED -- so a 3x slowdown scored 67% and was REFUSED while a 3x speedup scored 200% and PASSED. The gate was QUIETLY HARDER ON LOSSES THAN ON WINS, exactly the wrong bias for something whose job is to stop overclaiming, and it was suppressing this real 3x loss as NO_CLAIM. Margin is now max(speedup, 1/speedup)-1, symmetric by construction. EVERY EARLIER COMPARISON RE-EVALUATED AND NONE FLIPS: P5 fusion 1.7081 / 2.6213 still CANDIDATE_WINS, P7 native 2.0796 still CANDIDATE_WINS, GEMM 4096 still BASELINE_WINS 0.8081, GEMM 1024 still INDISTINGUISHABLE, forge champion still INDISTINGUISHABLE from runner-up -- the fix only ever made LOSSES easier to state. CCL now 12 PARTIAL / 4 LARGE, 8 of 17 performance gaps measured. Reduction moves OFF LARGE but SCAN DOES NOT EXIST AT ALL and softmax with it, so ATTENTION STAYS BLOCKED even though the reduction it needs now exists. 84 tests pass. || FUSED ROW SOFTMAX 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_SOFTMAX.json): softmax was the MISSING PREREQUISITE between the reduction and attention. AIR now produces it as ONE FUSED KERNEL -- one threadgroup per row, row read ONCE, max and sum both in the SIMD units with 2 barriers between, instead of 3 separate passes each re-reading what the last touched. FUSION WORTH 1.46x and 1.35x over the naive three-pass shape, both CANDIDATE_WINS with clean arms. AGAINST MLX INDISTINGUISHABLE (133.5 vs 141.1 and 133.5 vs 131.1 GB/s) -- NO CLAIM EITHER WAY. Correct at 64x128, 512x1024, NON-POWER-OF-TWO 128x4099 and tiny 8x3, rows summing to 1 within 3e-07 everywhere. Row max subtracted before exp: [1000,1001,1002] comes back FINITE and correct where the unguarded form would overflow to inf and produce nan. NEGATIVE CONTROL IS THE SHARPEST EVIDENCE: stripping the 2 barriers takes rows from summing to 1 within 3e-07 to being WRONG BY UP TO 0.973 -- the barriers ARE the correctness, not decoration. MATH.softmax joins the CCL as an 18TH ENTRY rather than being folded into an existing one, since it has its own corpus and limitations; ledger now 13 PARTIAL / 4 LARGE, 9 of 18 performance gaps measured. ATTENTION ITSELF REMAINS ABSENT -- this is ONE OF ITS PIECES and the receipt says so rather than letting a prerequisite read as the thing it enables. 88 tests pass. || FUSED ATTENTION EXISTS AND LOSES 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_ATTENTION.json): correct single-head scaled dot-product attention WITH CAUSAL MASKING now in AIR -- one threadgroup per query row, score row in threadgroup memory, 4 barriers -- verified to 3e-07 including causal and a NON-POWER-OF-TWO 37x40. IT LOSES, AND TO THE SHAPE IT WAS SUPPOSED TO BEAT: at 1024 the NAIVE MATERIALISED path (Q@K^T, softmax, @V as 3 MLX calls) is 1.37x FASTER; at 2048x128 it is 3.5x faster. Corpus still ABSENT: FFT, convolution. 227 accelerator tests pass. || CONVOLUTION WHERE USEFUL, ANSWERED BY A CENSUS -- AND FFT REFUSED WITH A REASON ABOUT THE ALGORITHM 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_CONVOLUTION.json): S015 §3 says CONVOLUTION WHERE USEFUL and FFT WHERE USEFUL, and THE QUALIFIER IS LOAD-BEARING. A CENSUS of the four specimens answers it rather than an opinion: Falcon-H1-7B holds 88 CONV TENSORS (weight + bias for each of 44 layers) while Qwen3MoE, Qwen3VLMoE and KimiVL hold ZERO BETWEEN THEM -- and KimiVL is the one I EXPECTED to have a conv patch embedding, checked, and it does not, its vision tower uses a linear projection. So AirCausalConv1d is built in EXACTLY THE SHAPE THE ONE SPECIMEN THAT NEEDS IT USES: depthwise, kernel width 4, 3584 channels = mamba_d_ssm 3072 + 2 x n_groups 1 x d_state 256, read from the real bf16 tensor model.layers.0.mamba.conv1d.weight [3584, 1, 4]. FFT IS REFUSED AND THE REASON IS NOT A GREP: zero tensors named fft/fourier/hyena/filter is WEAK EVIDENCE and is not relied on, because FFT is an ALGORITHM not a stored tensor. THE ACTUAL REASON is that FFT convolution beats direct convolution only for LONG kernels, and the one convolution that exists on disk here has WIDTH 4 -- direct costs four multiply-adds per output while an FFT costs two transforms and a pointwise product, so FFT WOULD BE THE WRONG ALGORITHM FOR THE ONLY CONVOLUTION THESE SPECIMENS CONTAIN. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER is a long-convolution specimen (Hyena, S4, kernels in the hundreds), recorded as a NAMED CONDITION not a parking lot; and this is a REFUSAL NOT AN OMISSION, which is a different ledger status and is recorded as one. CORRECT ON THE REAL WEIGHTS at L = 1, 4, 7, 64, 1024, and THE ABSOLUTE NUMBER MUST NOT BE MISREAD -- worst absolute error 2.58e-05 with RELATIVE error 5.24e-08, because these weights reach |328| and the outputs reach |493|, so the absolute figure is f32 rounding on large values and nothing else. L SHORTER THAN THE KERNEL IS THE DECODE SHAPE: L=1 with W=4 means three of four taps read the ZERO PAD, exactly what a Mamba mixer does at decode, and getting it wrong breaks generation and nothing else -- pinned with distinct taps 1/10/100/1000 so only the last can match. CAUSALITY IS THE CORRECTNESS AND IT NEEDED AN EXPLICIT CONTROL: a conv that reads t+1 in an autoregressive model CHANGES NO NORM, it just makes teacher forcing mysteriously easy and shows up nowhere else. Shifting the tap window forward differs by 640.78 with 0 OF 3584 ROWS UNCHANGED, so the control is LOUD and demonstrably can fail. THE SUBMISSION FLOOR IS SIGHTED A FOURTH TIME, and the prediction was written before the run: at decode the conv is 14336 multiply-adds over ~57 KB, so predict 0.15-0.30 ms at L=1 and no meaningful growth until L is large. L=1 MEASURED 0.176 ms -- CONFIRMED -- and the striking pair is L=1 against L=64, 3584 elements against 229376, A 256x INCREASE IN WORK with times 0.176 vs 0.1735 = 1.4% APART. That is the submission floor and nothing else. WHERE THE PREDICTION STARTS TO BREAK IS STATED RATHER THAN STRETCHED: L=1024 is 0.2434 ms, 38% above the floor, so 'no growth until L is large' holds to L=64 and is already breaking by 1024. FOUR EXPERIMENTS, FOUR DIFFERENT WORKLOADS, ONE CONSTANT: the AirGraph sweep measured ~0.157 ms per cross-command-buffer submission directly, the normalization block watched batching shed 0.10-0.20 ms per call, the expert-batch fit found a ~0.25 ms shared intercept across two unrelated kernels, and this floor sits at ~0.174 ms. NOISE CAVEAT NOT BURIED: the L=1 and L=64 arms carry 39.7% and 19.8% IQR, ABOVE the gate, so their 1.4% agreement sits well INSIDE their own noise -- what that establishes is that NO LARGE growth exists across a 256x work increase, not that they agree to 1.4%; L=1024 and L=8192 are clean at 7.4% and 4.8%. CONSEQUENCE FOR FALCON-H1: at decode the mixer's convolution is PURE SUBMISSION OVERHEAD, so any optimisation of this kernel is worth NOTHING and the only lever is FUSING it into a neighbouring dispatch -- exactly the ordering value AirGraph already measured. CLAIM BOUNDARY: ONE layer of ONE specimen, the other 43 the same shape by the index but not executed; NO MODEL EXECUTED -- this is the mixer's convolution in isolation with the SSM recurrence, the gating and the norm all ABSENT; f32 only, weights upcast from bf16; and NOTHING was timed against a baseline so no winner is claimed either way. THE §3 CORPUS IS NOW CLOSED: FFT was the last named item and it is REFUSED with a reason; every other one exists. 231 accelerator tests pass. || COMPOSING THE CORPUS FOUND TWO LAUNCHES THAT NEVER ASKED THE KERNEL 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_GRAPH_COMPOSITION.json): the §3 corpus closed last block with every primitive verified ALONE, and this campaign's own law is that LOCAL ADEQUACY DOES NOT COMPOSE -- stated about representations and equally open about KERNELS. Composing five primitives into one graph found TWO INDEPENDENT DEFECTS OF THE SAME CLASS: THE LAUNCH GEOMETRY DID NOT ASK THE KERNEL WHAT IT NEEDED. (1) AirGraphNode carried only an element count and a scalar threadgroup, so the executor DERIVED a 1-D grid and a flat output shape -- right for elementwise, wrong for every real AIR primitive, and NONE of AirNorm, AirMatmul, AirSoftmax or AirAttention could be held by a graph at all. IT FAILED IN THE WORST WAY: at 8x1024 it launched 32 threadgroups for 8 rows, 24 ran OUT OF BOUNDS on both buffers, AND THE ANSWER MATCHED THE ORACLE TO 2.6e-07; at 8x64 it launched 2 for 8 rows and was wrong by 2.62; at 64x128, wrong by 5.21. Same defect, opposite appearances -- correct BY ACCIDENT OF SHAPE, the same class as a race that does not fire. FIXED: grid, threadgroup, output shape, parameter names and output name are now FIELDS, and node_for() fills them from the op's own launch() and out_shape(), so THE GEOMETRY COMES FROM THE OP rather than from a guess -- the same principle as the HUMF block's 'the plan names its source', arrived at independently. (2) FOUND WHILE COMPOSING, NOT BY AUDITING: the tiled AirMatmul is WRONG whenever m is not a multiple of the tile. ACCELERATOR_SIMDGROUP_GEMM.json justified keeping the tiled strategy in its own words -- 'tiled has no shape constraint. Deleting the loser would have removed the only strategy that handles a 60x60 matmul' -- and THAT 60x60x60 WAS OFF BY 3.84. 8x64x32 off by 4.65, 17x64x32 by 5.84; every wrong case has m not a multiple of the tile and n and k do not matter. The kernel body is FULLY GUARDED (gy<m, gx<n, k0+lx<k) so the tile was never the constraint -- launch() returned (n,m,1) against a (tile,tile) threadgroup and UNDER-DISPATCHED. One line, round both dimensions up; all 7 shapes correct after, 60x60x60 included. It survived because every GEMM ever measured in this program was a square multiple of 16, so the claim about odd shapes was NEVER TESTED AT AN ODD SHAPE. The simdgroup receipt is AMENDED IN PLACE: its conclusion (keep both strategies) survives, the evidence it offered for that conclusion does not. COMPOSED: y = x + W_down @ silu(W_gate @ rmsnorm(x)), the gated MLP that follows attention in all four specimens, at Qwen3-30B-A3B expert shapes C=2048 H=768, five nodes, one submission, verified end to end against an f64 oracle at T=8/64/96 (worst rel 6.33e-07). ONE SUBMISSION vs ONE PER NODE: predicted 1.5-3.0x AND SHRINKING WITH T; measured 2.216x at T=8 and 2.035x at T=64 (inside), 1.415x at T=512 (BELOW the band). The shrink is confirmed; the magnitude MISSED LOW, the first miss in that direction after six consecutive misses HIGH, and it is reported rather than the band widened. FIFTH SIGHTING of the ~0.16-0.25 ms submission floor and the first on a COMPOSITE. CLAIM BOUNDARY: the MLP half of one block -- no attention, no KV cache, no rotary, no cross-layer residual; real shapes and SYNTHETIC weights, no model executed; serial_depth 5 of 5 nodes so this measures ORDERING and BATCHING and says nothing about concurrency; the per-node arm is a CONTROL, not a mode anyone would run; f32, one machine, INSTANCE. The T=64 graph arm carries 19.41% IQR and is admitted by a 5.3x margin-over-noise rather than a clean gate. 234 accelerator tests pass. || QUIESCENCE WAS NEVER AN INSTRUMENT 2026-08-26 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_QUIESCENCE_INSTRUMENT.json): FUSION_GAIN_IS_LENGTH_INDEPENDENT named this as its own next step -- 'a quiescence check that ENUMERATES every process over a CPU or RSS threshold rather than grepping for known names'. I expected to find a function with a name filter in it. THERE IS NO SUCH FUNCTION: grep for 'quiesc' in tools/accelerator/bench.py returns NOTHING, and every 'the machine is quiet' claim in this program came from an AD-HOC pgrep typed into a shell command whose silence was then written into a receipt as prose. TWO FAILURES, NOT ONE: it was NEVER A FIELD, so although S015 §73/§74 require uncontended measurement NO receipt here carries a machine-state field and no timed claim can be audited for the condition its own steer demands; and it MATCHED NAMES, so it could only ever find the contender already met. SHIPPED bench.machine_quiescence, which enumerates via ps and returns quiet, contenders, total_cpu_pct and max_rss_gib as FIELDS -- with DELIBERATELY NO names PARAMETER, because the blind spot WAS a filter and an instrument whose blind spot is configurable is one somebody will configure blind; a test asserts the signature is exactly {cpu_pct, rss_gib} and FAILS if names= is ever added. RSS IS THE GATE NOT CPU AND THE REASON IS A MEASURED LAW: this campaign sealed on 2026-08-22 that METAL WORKING SET is the admission gate and not free RAM, so a large-RSS neighbour contends in the dimension that decides. THE TWO CHECKS DISAGREE AND IT WAS WATCHED LIVE, both called in one process one after the other: the enumerator reports quiet=FALSE with 2 contenders holding 195.6% CPU and 17.6 GiB, while the name filter on ('modellake','hf_transfer') reports quiet=TRUE with zero hits -- that filter is THE CHECK EVERY TIMED RECEIPT IN THIS PROGRAM USED, and what it missed was an unrelated 17.6 GiB Personal-Model MLX run at 95.6% and fileproviderd at 100%. A FAILED ENUMERATION IS NOT A QUIET MACHINE: if ps exits non-zero, quiet is None with a refused reason and NEVER True, because 0 of 0 reads identically to 0 of many and this program has confused 'I could not look' with 'I looked and found nothing' four times. THE CALLER IS NOT EXEMPT -- the harness's own process is reported like any other, since excluding it would be the same self-exemption the name filter made by accident. The broken check is KEPT EXECUTABLE as bench.name_filter_quiescence with a docstring forbidding its use for admissibility, because a refutation nobody has watched is indistinguishable from a rule nobody needed. SIX TESTS AND THREE MUTATIONS WATCHED FIRING, each caught by exactly the intended test: quiet-always-True caught by the anti-vacuity and disagreement tests, a failed-ps-reads-as-quiet caught by the None rule, and a names= parameter caught by the signature test. CLAIM BOUNDARY: THIS DETECTS CONTENTION AND DOES NOT ATTRIBUTE SLOWNESS TO IT -- the 42x capability stall and the 3-of-12 decoder outliers remain UNEXPLAINED, and naming a contender is not naming a cause; the 20% CPU and 2 GiB thresholds are JUDGEMENT not measurement so a contender below both is invisible; ps pcpu on macOS is a DECAYED AVERAGE over process life rather than an instantaneous sample, which is a second reason to prefer RSS; it is NOT wired into time_arm automatically and the reason is COST NOT PRINCIPLE, since a subprocess per call inside a sweep would perturb the thing being measured, WHICH MEANS THE OLD FAILURE MODE OF FORGETTING TO CHECK IS STILL POSSIBLE and is named rather than papered over; and NO PRIOR TIMED CLAIM IS RETROACTIVELY VALIDATED -- every earlier receipt's quiescence evidence is still the sentence it always was. 516 accelerator tests pass under the FRAMEWORK python3.12 recorded BY PATH, because `python3.12` names two different interpreters on this machine. Nothing timed; no kernel changed. || THE SAME NAME-FILTER DEFECT WAS IN A SECOND INSTRUMENT, AND MY OWN VALIDATOR CAUGHT ME 2026-08-26 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_QUIESCENCE_INSTRUMENT.json#THE_SAME_DEFECT_WAS_IN_A_SECOND_INSTRUMENT_AND_MY_OWN_VALIDATOR_CAUGHT_ME): I published '516 tests pass' and civilization/validate.py REFUSED it -- '1 tests FAILED in the run this count came from; a passed-count published unreported failures is a half-truth' -- a rule THIS session added, firing on me. THE COUNT WAS STALE BY THE END OF THE BLOCK THAT PRODUCED IT: 516 was measured BEFORE I wrote the receipt, and writing it made the suite 515+1. CHECKPOINT_002 sealed exactly this shape and I repeated it with a test count. THE FAILING TEST WAS CORRECT -- test_every_unextracted_receipt_carries_a_reason refused the UNCLASSIFIED newcomer, now classified PROSE_ONLY whose own wording fits. AND THEN THE BIGGER ONE: the AKB corpus globs ACCELERATOR_*.json, so the FOUR RECEIPTS THIS SESSION PRODUCED -- TOKEN_EXECUTION_ATLAS_COUNTS, TOKEN_GRAPH_REDUCTION_TIMED, CAPABILITY_FUSED_GRAPH_CLEARED, FUSION_GAIN_IS_LENGTH_INDEPENDENT -- ARE INVISIBLE TO IT, carrying this session's largest measured results (964 dispatches/token, the 2.19% fusion gain, the identity-bound 30/43) where the knowledge base can neither extract nor refuse them. IT IS THE SAME CLASS AS THE DEFECT THIS BLOCK FIXED: membership decided by a NAME, so a receipt outside the glob is INVISIBLE, which reads identically to 'triaged and found empty' -- the tripwire that refuses unclassified newcomers only sees newcomers it is allowed to look at. NOT FIXED BY WIDENING AND THE REASON IS NAMED: 348 receipts sit outside the glob and most are Q80, noetic and civilization work this lane cannot type, so widening would ingest another campaign's evidence as Accelerator evidence and a content classifier would be this lane GUESSING which 348 are its own. Scope UNCHANGED, exclusion REPORTED -- outside_scope_count plus an explicit KNOWN_ACCELERATOR_OUTSIDE_SCOPE list, with a test that it cannot go stale silently since a receipt renamed into the glob must LEAVE the list, because a gap list that only grows is one nobody reads. STILL OPEN: those four are NAMED as outside scope and still not extracted into laws, which is a different thing from closed. 518 accelerator tests pass, RE-DERIVED AFTER the last change in this block rather than before it, and the validator reports failed=0.

value.headline: - [ ] G047 — KERNEL FORGE / FRONT E (S015): generation, specialization and autotuning; per primitive a ReferenceKernel, AppleBaselineKernel, AcceleratorChampion and ExperimentalCandidates; parameterized templates through synthesis, compile, verify, benchmark into MachineGenome. Search by priors and bandits, not blind brute force. | status: IN_PROGRESS | risk: high | tier: V3 || FORGE RUNS, AND ITS RESULT IS NEGATIVE SCIENCE 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_FRONT_E_FORGE.json): 15 variants GENERATED from priors (threadgroup x elements-per-thread, not a sweep), EVERY ONE VERIFIED BEFORE IT WAS TIMED -- the fastest way to run a kernel is to compute the wrong answer. All 15 correct; 3 FAILED THE RELIABILITY GATE (tg128_ept2, tg512_ept1, tg1024_ept4) and were barred from winning. Champion tg256_ept2 at 0.508 ms beats the MLX baseline 1.350 ms by 2.66x -- BUT THAT MARGIN IS FUSION, WHICH P5 ALREADY ESTABLISHED, NOT AUTOTUNING. THE AUTOTUNE'S OWN FINDING IS NEGATIVE AND MORE USEFUL: champion beats runner-up by 0.38% against 4.94% arm noise = INDISTINGUISHABLE, so the TOP CLUSTER IS FLAT (bandwidth-saturated once one pass over memory is achieved). I first phrased that as 'autotuning buys nothing' and CORRECTED it: the FULL landscape spans 20.19% across the 12 reliable candidates, so a BAD config does cost real time. Correct conclusion = autotuning here buys AVOIDANCE OF BAD CONFIGURATIONS, not discovery of a single best one; and 3 variants were not merely slower but LESS REPEATABLE, which is its own result. DOES NOT SUPPORT P6: a reproducible MACHINE-SPECIFIC win needs something machine-specific, and a flat top cluster on a bandwidth-bound chain would look flat on any bandwidth-bound device. Champion cached under an IDENTITY KEY (SoC, GPU cores, OS, primitive, representation, shape, runtime) so retuning happens on material change, not on a timer (§27), with the within-noise caveat carried in the cache entry itself. || BANDIT SEARCH CLOSES THE UNBUILT HALF 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_BANDIT_SEARCH.json): G047 asks for search by priors AND BANDITS. Priors existed from the start; the search itself timed ALL 15 variants EQUALLY = exactly the brute force the obligation names. SUCCESSIVE HALVING now gives every candidate a cheap look, keeps the better half, doubles reps on survivors: 245 reps vs 600 = 2.45x SAVING, champion 0.11% off the exhaustive winner. THE FIRST BANDIT HAD A REAL DEFECT: it ranked on MEDIAN TIME ALONE and crowned tg512_ept1 -- a candidate that FAILED the forge's own reliability gate at 13.56% IQR in the original run. A BANDIT INHERITS EVERY BLIND SPOT OF ITS OBJECTIVE; correctness was already excluded by construction, RELIABILITY WAS NOT. Final round now applies the gate and BARS an unreliable survivor, with a test that hands it a fast jittery candidate beside a slower steady one and requires the steady one. AGREEMENT IS THE WRONG SUCCESS METRIC: the two searches DISAGREE on the winner and THAT IS NOT A FAILURE -- this landscape was already measured FLAT at the top (0.38% over runner-up vs ~5% noise), so two honest searches WILL name different winners; the question is whether the bandit's pick is CLOSE, and it is +0.11%. REQUIRING AGREEMENT WOULD HAVE DECLARED A WORKING SEARCH BROKEN. ALSO RECORDED: the same candidate failed the gate at 13.56% in one run and PASSED at 3.19% in another -- A SINGLE RELIABILITY SAMPLE IS NOT A STABLE PROPERTY OF A KERNEL, which weakens the GATE not the kernel. NOT UCB, not Bayesian, not the learned performance model §113 asks for; saving is in REPS and wall-clock saving is smaller because warmup is paid per candidate per round. 102 tests pass. || I AUDITED THE GATE EVERY CLAIM RESTS ON, AND IT FLIPS BELOW 200 REPS 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_IQR_STABILITY_AUDIT.json): the bandit receipt noticed the same candidate failing the reliability gate at 13.56% in one run and PASSING at 3.19% in another. EVERY performance claim in this program is admitted or refused by that gate, so I measured the gate's own input: 8 INDEPENDENT IQR estimates per candidate at 20/40/100/200 reps on 3 forge variants. AT 20 AND 40 REPS THE VERDICT FLIPS FOR EVERY CANDIDATE -- tg256_ept2 ranges 1.84%-13.38% across eight 20-rep runs, so the SAME KERNEL is judged reliable or unreliable depending on which run you happened to do. At 100 reps 2 of 3 still flip. At 200 all three hold inside a 3-point band. LARGE-MARGIN CONCLUSIONS DO NOT MOVE: fusion 1.71x, unified memory 7.4x, representation-native 2.08x, atomics 3.05x and the GEMM results all rest on margins far larger than any plausible noise-estimate error. WHAT DOES MOVE IS THE FORGE'S OWN BARRING: the original run refused 3 candidates for failing the gate at ~25 reps; TWO OF THOSE ARE PROBED HERE AND THEIR TRUE IQR SITS NEAR 5%, comfortably INSIDE the gate -- they were most likely BARRED BY NOISE IN THE MEASUREMENT OF NOISE. Recorded AGAINST the forge rather than quietly corrected, because the original receipt reported those three as a finding. time_arm now reports reliability_verdict_is_stable and attaches a caveat below 200 reps so a `reliable` flag from too few samples cannot be cited as a property of a kernel. COST IS REAL: a stable verdict needs 200 reps where this program typically spent 20-60 = 3-10x the budget for any claim admitted BY THE GATE rather than by a large margin. 104 tests pass. || RE-RAN THE FORGE AT 200 REPS: TWO OF ITS OWN FINDINGS WERE WRONG 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_FORGE_REVERDICT.json): the stability audit PREDICTED the 3 barred candidates were barred by noise. PREDICTING IS NOT CHECKING, so all 15 were re-measured at 200 reps. CORRECTION 1 -- ALL THREE BARRINGS WERE WRONG: at 200 reps EVERY ONE of the 15 is reliable, IQR 3.52%-7.27%, all inside the gate. The forge reported '3 variants were not merely slower but LESS REPEATABLE' and called it a result; IT WAS AN ARTIFACT of measuring noise with too few samples. CORRECTION 2 -- THE LANDSCAPE CLAIM WAS OVERSTATED: the forge said the landscape spans 20.19% so a bad config costs real time. At 200 reps that spread is driven almost ENTIRELY BY ONE CONFIGURATION (tg64_ept1, smallest threadgroup at 1 elem/thread = the lowest-occupancy point); EXCLUDING IT the other 14 span ~2.4%. So 'autotuning buys avoidance of bad configurations' is really avoidance of ONE bad configuration, which a prior would have skipped anyway. WHAT SURVIVES is the finding the forge was most careful about: THE TOP CLUSTER IS FLAT -- best 9 span 0.65% against ~4.5% noise; champion name changes tg256_ept2 -> tg1024_ept1 on a 0.33% difference and NEITHER IS DISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE OTHER, which is exactly what a flat cluster means. THE ORIGINAL FORGE RECEIPT IS AMENDED IN PLACE so anyone reaching it finds the correction attached rather than reading a superseded finding as current. No large-margin result anywhere in the program moves. 104 tests pass. || THE LEARNED PERFORMANCE MODEL: MY FALSIFIER FIRED, THEN THE DIAGNOSIS SAVED IT 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_PERF_MODEL.json): the bandit receipt named this as the unbuilt half -- 'NOT UCB, not Bayesian, not the learned performance model §113 asks for'. tools/accelerator/perf_model.py is that model, deliberately the SMALLEST thing that can answer whether the idea pays: ridge on 4 features over the forge's own 200-rep table, closed form. THE LANDSCAPE MAKES THE QUESTION SHARP -- the re-verdict measured the top cluster FLAT (best 9 span 0.65% against ~4.5% arm noise) with the whole 20.19% spread driven by ONE configuration, so a model predicting within 0.65% there is not accurate, it is predicting a constant, AND SO IS `PREDICT THE MEAN`. The grader therefore keeps TWO questions apart, because averaging them would let 14 easy points hide the failure on the one that decides. FLAT: model 1.13% median error against the mean baseline's 1.68%, BOTH far inside arm noise, so 'beats the baseline' is not evidence of anything -- predicted and vacuous exactly as written. CLIFF: I predicted direction right and magnitude undershot; I WAS WRONG IN BOTH HALVES. Trained on 14 flat variants it put the held-out tg64_ept1 at a 0.34% penalty against an ACTUAL 16.88% -- 14.15% error and NOT ranked slower than every flat point. MY OWN FALSIFIER FIRED and is recorded as fired. THEN THE FAILURE WAS DIAGNOSED RATHER THAN LEFT AS A VERDICT: modelling failure or DATA failure? tg64_ept1 has 64 elements per threadgroup and the next smallest sampled points are 128, BOTH FAST, so the training data contains NO GRADIENT pointing at the cliff -- it is a THRESHOLD and a linear model cannot represent one it has never crossed. TESTED BY MEASURING BELOW THE GRID at 200 reps: per_tg 32 -> 0.9559 ms, 64 -> 0.5954, 128 -> 0.512, >=256 -> 0.511-0.522. IT IS AN OCCUPANCY THRESHOLD, and THE SHARPEST EVIDENCE IS A COLLAPSE: tg32_ept2 and tg64_ept1 have DIFFERENT threadgroup sizes and DIFFERENT elements per thread but the SAME per_tg of 64, and measure 0.5954 and 0.5955 -- agreeing to 0.02%. Two configurations differing in both parameters landing on the same time is far stronger than a correlation: per_tg is the controlling variable and the feature bet was right. RETRAINED WITH ONE CLIFF SAMPLE the model gives 2.78% error and ranks the cliff LAST -- but that sample has the SAME per_tg as the target, so it is INTERPOLATION AT A KNOWN POINT, not discovery; training on per_tg 32 instead still ranks it last but OVERSHOOTS 13.37% because the relationship is STEEPER THAN LINEAR in 1/per_tg (32->64 costs 0.361 ms, 64->128 costs 0.083), so the linear term captures DIRECTION and not CURVATURE. THE ACTIONABLE CONCLUSION: on this landscape a learned performance model does NOT replace search -- it becomes useful exactly once one sample from the cliff region exists, which is the measurement autotuning would have made anyway, so it could only compress a search already run once. WHAT IT LICENSES IN THE FORGE: THREADGROUP_PRIOR stops at 64 and that exclusion is now MEASURED rather than assumed, recorded as a comment with the cliff shape; tg32 is deliberately NOT ADDED because a prior's job is to skip known-bad configurations and adding measured-bad points to it would be backwards. NO CHAMPION MOVES -- every tg32 variant is slower than every point in the top cluster. REPRODUCIBILITY: tg64_ept1 re-measured at 0.6002 ms against 0.5955 from a different day, 0.8% apart. CLAIM BOUNDARY: ONE primitive, a MEMORY-BOUND fused chain at 2^24 f32 -- a compute-bound primitive could have real structure to learn and nothing here says otherwise; the new arms carry 7.99% and 8.04% IQR, inside the gate but above the flat cluster's 4.5%; and §113's model in the sense of something that GENERALISES across primitives, shapes or machines is STILL NOT BUILT, this one is fit per-landscape. 188 tests pass. || THE CLIFF MOVES WITH THE PRIMITIVE, SO THE PRIOR DOES NOT TRAVEL 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_CLIFF_TRANSFER.json): the perf-model receipt named its own unbuilt half -- '§113's model in the sense of something that GENERALISES across primitives, shapes or machines is STILL NOT BUILT, this one is fit per-landscape'. A MODEL THAT COULD GENERALISE WAS WRITTEN DOWN BEFORE THE RUN: time(per_tg) = max(T, threadgroups / R), with T the primitive's saturated time and R a MACHINE constant, so ONE fit predicts every other primitive's cliff without measuring it. The ADDITIVE form was considered and REJECTED ON THE EXISTING DATA (R 2.6x apart across the two cliff points against 1.25x for max), so the worse model was never carried. R WAS FIT ON THE CHAIN ALONE at 4.386e8 threadgroups/s and used to PREDICT the other two. VERDICT SPLITS: DIRECTION CONFIRMED, MAGNITUDE REFUTED. Measured at 2^24 f32, each primitive against ITS OWN floor -- write-only 2.94x / 1.90x / 1.37x / 1.11x / 1.02x at per_tg 32/64/128/256/512, fused chain 1.87x / 1.17x / 1.00x / 1.00x / 1.00x, heavy 256-FMA 1.15x / 1.05x / 1.05x / 1.05x / 1.00x. THREE PRIMITIVES, THREE DIFFERENT ANSWERS ABOUT THE SAME MACHINE: a CHEAPER kernel stays dispatch-bound to a LARGER per_tg and is still 1.90x off its floor exactly where the chain has already flattened. BOTH OUT-OF-SAMPLE PREDICTIONS MISS BY ~2x AND IN THE SAME DIRECTION (write-only predicted 128, degrades out to 256; heavy predicted no cliff above 15, still pays 1.15x at 32) -- A MODEL WRONG TWICE THE SAME WAY IS WRONG ABOUT ITS SHAPE, NOT UNLUCKY: max() predicts a KNEE and the write-only curve is a SMOOTH DECAY. The broken check is KEPT EXECUTABLE as bench.name_filter_quiescence with a docstring forbidding its use for admissibility, because a refutation nobody has watched is indistinguishable from a rule nobody needed. SIX TESTS AND THREE MUTATIONS WATCHED FIRING, each caught by exactly the intended test: quiet-always-True caught by the anti-vacuity and disagreement tests, a failed-ps-reads-as-quiet caught by the None rule, and a names= parameter caught by the signature test. NOT SHOWN: no kernel RUN on the VL variant's actual weights, no Doctor verification for any specimen but #2, and shape reuse does NOT make a representation adequate for that model. || THE KERNEL RAN ON THE VL VARIANT'S REAL WEIGHTS, AND THE REUSE CLAIM NEEDED A CONDITION 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_TRANSFER_VERIFIED.json): this pass listed as NOT SHOWN 'no kernel RUN on the VL variant's actual weights'. DOING THE THING IT SAID WAS NOT DONE is what found the correction. THE GAP IS CLOSED: reading expert 0's gate from Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B's real bf16 shards and executing the byte-identical MSL b17f0bad44a2bf90 gives 3.815e-06 against the representation's own answer inside a 3.176e-03 tolerance -- the kernel DOES transfer. BUT THE PASS'S CLAIM WAS TRUE OF A TENSOR THE VL VARIANT DOES NOT STORE. Model #2 keeps 384 separate 2-D tensors per layer (gate_proj [768, 2048]); the VL variant keeps TWO 3-D tensors per layer, gate_up_proj [128, 2048, 1536] -- every expert STACKED and gate FUSED WITH UP along the last axis -- so its gate half is stored [2048, 768], TRANSPOSED relative to what the kernel wants. THE TENSOR AS STORED EMITS cf7e64009d5d47be, NOT b17f0bad44a2bf90. Byte-identity holds ONLY AFTER a de-interleave and a transpose that the pass never counted as work. THE RANKING IS INVERTED BY STORAGE: the specimen scored 100% is the one whose storage diverges MOST, while the specimen scored 40% (Kimi-VL) uses the SAME per-expert 2-D convention as model #2 and needs NO preparation -- it simply has 1408-row experts instead of 768, emitting 876bee1830ae6f10, so it shares no kernel either. The pass ranked ARCHITECTURE-CONFIG SIMILARITY ('same MoE core'); on disk the relationship runs differently in exactly the dimension that decides transfer. KERNEL REUSE IS A CLAIM ABOUT STORAGE LAYOUT, NOT ONLY ABOUT GEMV SHAPE. WHAT STILL STANDS, and it is most of it: the Falcon zero (0 expert tensors of 751) still does the work of making the other numbers meaningful; the cache key being (organ, shape) rather than model name stands; and REPRESENTATION FIDELITY GENUINELY TRANSFERS -- weight cosine under ws_rtn_q4_g64 is 0.993952 on model #2 and 0.993965 on the VL variant, 0.993816 even in the on-disk orientation. Adequacy per tensor is ROBUST to layout; only the KERNEL is layout-sensitive, and separating those two is what running it bought. §19 IS NOT VIOLATED AND SAYING SO MATTERS: the transpose is PACK-time, offline, Gravity's -- P7's claim that no dense tensor is written DURING EXECUTION is untouched, and overreading this as a run-time rematerialization would be wrong. gravity_native now carries kernel_identity() (a hash of the MSL, not a similarity score) and stored_gate_shape() (which of the two on-disk conventions a tensor uses), with a test pinning that the fused layout emits a DIFFERENT kernel before preparation and the SAME one after. The original pass receipt is AMENDED IN PLACE. Still one expert, one projection, one layer per specimen; no model executed; local adequacy still does not compose. 145 tests pass. || THE SECOND EDUCATIONAL GOAL, DISCHARGED FOR ALL FOUR SPECIMENS, AND THE PRIOR LAW DOES NOT TRANSFER 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_ORGAN_REPRESENTATION_FLOOR.json): this obligation tracks TWO goals and had discharged ONE -- 'how does this computation want to EXECUTE' was answered for all 4 specimens while 'how does this architecture want to EXIST' was carried for model #2 ALONE. THE QUESTION WAS NARROWED ON PURPOSE rather than answered loosely: this campaign sealed on 2026-07-27 that every prior sub-bit negative was a GAUSSIAN-PROXY ARTIFACT and that compression must be judged on real ACTIVATIONS, and on 2026-08-17 that LOCAL ADEQUACY DOES NOT COMPOSE -- so the falsifiable form is DOES THE ORGAN RANKING TRANSFER ACROSS ARCHITECTURES. IT DOES NOT. Attention sets the floor on BOTH Qwen models (q_proj needs group 32 where every MLP and expert tensor clears at group 128; cosine spread 0.0084 across organs) and on Kimi-VL EVERY ORGAN sits in 0.99303-0.99324, a spread of 0.0002 = 40x TIGHTER, while Falcon-H1 spans only 0.0016 INCLUDING ITS MAMBA ORGANS. The prior law is ARCHITECTURE-SPECIFIC, not general. THE MECHANISM WAS A CLAIM SO IT WAS TESTED: grouped absmax spends its levels on the largest weight in a group, so cosine should fall as mean(amax/rms) rises -- PEARSON -0.9841 ACROSS 33 ORGANS AND 4 ARCHITECTURES, CONFIRMED, and it holds ACROSS architectures rather than within one, which is what makes it an explanation of the ranking instead of a restatement. THE GAUSSIAN CONTROL IS THE PART THAT GIVES THE NUMBERS MEANING: structureless noise of the same scale reaches 0.99321 at 4b/g128, stable to 2e-05 across three shapes, and it is a REFERENCE POINT NOT A FLOOR -- real weights sit AT it or BELOW it, never meaningfully above. Kimi-VL sits AT it on every organ, so under THIS measurement its weights are indistinguishable from noise of the same scale, which is a statement about the MEASUREMENT'S RESOLVING POWER on that model and NOT a claim that the weights are random; Qwen3-30B's attention_q sits 0.0085 BELOW it, 26x further than Kimi's largest deviation, which is exactly where the measurement has content. DEPTH ROBUSTNESS RUN BECAUSE THE SURPRISING CLAIM RESTED ON ONE TENSOR: Qwen3-30B attention_q is below the reference at ALL FIVE layers sampled (0,8,20,32,44) with a 0.0077 spread, and Kimi's expert_gate is AT the reference at all five (spread 0.00011) -- a layer-0 accident would have made the whole table worthless and there was no way to know without looking. THE STUDY IS ANCHORED ON THE SHIPPED REPRESENTATION, NOT A LOOKALIKE: quantize_grouped at bits=4 group=64 is pinned BY TEST to reproduce dequantize(pack_q4_g64(w)) EXACTLY, and THAT TEST FAILED FIRST -- the real representation QUANTISES with the f32 scale and RECONSTRUCTS with the stored f16 one, an asymmetry my first version got backwards, which is precisely the divergence the anchor exists to prevent. bits=1 is included as the DELETION CONTROL (bound = 2^(bits-1)-1 is ZERO) so the ladder has a floor whose answer is known in advance. A DEFECT IN MY OWN PROBE, RECORDED: the depth script imported the sweep script to reuse its reader, and that script does work at MODULE LEVEL, so the import silently RE-RAN the whole 205-second sweep -- harmless here because it is deterministic, corrupting for any probe with state or randomness. A LABEL KEPT HONEST: Qwen3-30B-A3B has NO dense MLP, so its 'mlp_gate' row is an EXPERT tensor and says so rather than being relabelled. CLAIM BOUNDARY: WEIGHT SPACE ONLY, no activations, no model executed and none could be -- the runtime lacks Qwen3-MoE, Falcon and Mamba readers; 256-row slices of ONE tensor per organ for the main table; the coarse floor SATURATES at 4 bits because 3 bits fails the 0.99 bar everywhere, so the informative axes are the GROUP and the continuous cosine and both are reported; knowledge level MODEL_FAMILY not ARCHITECTURE, since two Qwen MoE variants agreeing is one family and Kimi and Falcon are single specimens. 184 tests pass. || CONVOLUTION WHERE USEFUL, ANSWERED BY A CENSUS -- AND FFT REFUSED WITH A REASON ABOUT THE ALGORITHM 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_CONVOLUTION.json): S015 §3 says CONVOLUTION WHERE USEFUL and FFT WHERE USEFUL, and THE QUALIFIER IS LOAD-BEARING. A CENSUS of the four specimens answers it rather than an opinion: Falcon-H1-7B holds 88 CONV TENSORS (weight + bias for each of 44 layers) while Qwen3MoE, Qwen3VLMoE and KimiVL hold ZERO BETWEEN THEM -- and KimiVL is the one I EXPECTED to have a conv patch embedding, checked, and it does not, its vision tower uses a linear projection. So AirCausalConv1d is built in EXACTLY THE SHAPE THE ONE SPECIMEN THAT NEEDS IT USES: depthwise, kernel width 4, 3584 channels = mamba_d_ssm 3072 + 2 x n_groups 1 x d_state 256, read from the real bf16 tensor model.layers.0.mamba.conv1d.weight [3584, 1, 4]. FFT IS REFUSED AND THE REASON IS NOT A GREP: zero tensors named fft/fourier/hyena/filter is WEAK EVIDENCE and is not relied on, because FFT is an ALGORITHM not a stored tensor. THE ACTUAL REASON is that FFT convolution beats direct convolution only for LONG kernels, and the one convolution that exists on disk here has WIDTH 4 -- direct costs four multiply-adds per output while an FFT costs two transforms and a pointwise product, so FFT WOULD BE THE WRONG ALGORITHM FOR THE ONLY CONVOLUTION THESE SPECIMENS CONTAIN. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER is a long-convolution specimen (Hyena, S4, kernels in the hundreds), recorded as a NAMED CONDITION not a parking lot; and this is a REFUSAL NOT AN OMISSION, which is a different ledger status and is recorded as one. CORRECT ON THE REAL WEIGHTS at L = 1, 4, 7, 64, 1024, and THE ABSOLUTE NUMBER MUST NOT BE MISREAD -- worst absolute error 2.58e-05 with RELATIVE error 5.24e-08, because these weights reach |328| and the outputs reach |493|, so the absolute figure is f32 rounding on large values and nothing else. L SHORTER THAN THE KERNEL IS THE DECODE SHAPE: L=1 with W=4 means three of four taps read the ZERO PAD, exactly what a Mamba mixer does at decode, and getting it wrong breaks generation and nothing else -- pinned with distinct taps 1/10/100/1000 so only the last can match. CAUSALITY IS THE CORRECTNESS AND IT NEEDED AN EXPLICIT CONTROL: a conv that reads t+1 in an autoregressive model CHANGES NO NORM, it just makes teacher forcing mysteriously easy and shows up nowhere else. Shifting the tap window forward differs by 640.78 with 0 OF 3584 ROWS UNCHANGED, so the control is LOUD and demonstrably can fail. THE SUBMISSION FLOOR IS SIGHTED A FOURTH TIME, and the prediction was written before the run: at decode the conv is 14336 multiply-adds over ~57 KB, so predict 0.15-0.30 ms at L=1 and no meaningful growth until L is large. L=1 MEASURED 0.176 ms -- CONFIRMED -- and the striking pair is L=1 against L=64, 3584 elements against 229376, A 256x INCREASE IN WORK with times 0.176 vs 0.1735 = 1.4% APART. That is the submission floor and nothing else. WHERE THE PREDICTION STARTS TO BREAK IS STATED RATHER THAN STRETCHED: L=1024 is 0.2434 ms, 38% above the floor, so 'no growth until L is large' holds to L=64 and is already breaking by 1024. FOUR EXPERIMENTS, FOUR DIFFERENT WORKLOADS, ONE CONSTANT: the AirGraph sweep measured ~0.157 ms per cross-command-buffer submission directly, the normalization block watched batching shed 0.10-0.20 ms per call, the expert-batch fit found a ~0.25 ms shared intercept across two unrelated kernels, and this floor sits at ~0.174 ms. NOISE CAVEAT NOT BURIED: the L=1 and L=64 arms carry 39.7% and 19.8% IQR, ABOVE the gate, so their 1.4% agreement sits well INSIDE their own noise -- what that establishes is that NO LARGE growth exists across a 256x work increase, not that they agree to 1.4%; L=1024 and L=8192 are clean at 7.4% and 4.8%. CONSEQUENCE FOR FALCON-H1: at decode the mixer's convolution is PURE SUBMISSION OVERHEAD, so any optimisation of this kernel is worth NOTHING and the only lever is FUSING it into a neighbouring dispatch -- exactly the ordering value AirGraph already measured. CLAIM BOUNDARY: ONE layer of ONE specimen, the other 43 the same shape by the index but not executed; NO MODEL EXECUTED -- this is the mixer's convolution in isolation with the SSM recurrence, the gating and the norm all ABSENT; f32 only, weights upcast from bf16; and NOTHING was timed against a baseline so no winner is claimed either way. THE §3 CORPUS IS NOW CLOSED: FFT was the last named item and it is REFUSED with a reason; every other one exists. 231 accelerator tests pass. || THE WEIGHT GATE IS A GAUSSIAN-INPUT EVALUATION IN DISGUISE 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_ORGAN_DISCRIMINATION.json): the open half of this obligation is 'how does this architecture want to EXIST', which needs a Doctor-style adequacy grade per organ. Attempted it and found the STANDARD GRADE CANNOT ANSWER THE QUESTION. Prediction written first: attention organs need more bits than MLP organs. In WEIGHT space, four organs of MiniLM layer 0 at 3 bits/group 64 are separated by 0.0038 of cosine, all four floor at the SAME setting (4.125 bpw), and A GAUSSIAN SURROGATE with the same std scores WITHIN 0.002-0.005 OF EVERY REAL TENSOR while shuffling all structure away costs 0.001-0.007. output.dense has KURTOSIS 1585 against query's 4.0 -- 400x the outlier structure -- and its weight cosine differs by 0.0037. The weight-space table is measuring the DISTRIBUTION'S SCALE, not the organ. Captured REAL activations from the real model (5 sentences, 55 rows, forward hooks) and asked the same question through the matmul: the spread grows to 0.0269, 7.1x, the two ATTENTION organs are the two weakest exactly as predicted, AND THE RANKING INVERTS -- output.dense is the WORST organ by weight cosine (0.9647) and the BEST by real activations (0.9982). A gate ranking organs by weight-space error would spend its bit budget on precisely the wrong tensor. This INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCES the Q80 finding that down_proj inverts the ranking, on a different architecture family by a different route. THE MECHANISM IS SHOWN, NOT ASSERTED: feeding GAUSSIAN inputs through the same packs collapses the organ spread from 0.0269 back to 0.0052, reproducing the weight gate's blindness by supplying the inputs it implicitly assumes. And the organs differ in KIND: for mlp_down, shuffled inputs score 0.99819 against real 0.99818 so the per-feature MARGINALS carry all of it, while for attn_q correlation is worth 0.008. SHIPPED gravity_native.output_space_fidelity, which returns the real number WITH both controls beside it because the real number alone cannot be told apart from the blind one. THE LAKE IS I/O STARVED AND IT IS MEASURED, NOT GUESSED: /Volumes/corpdrive is USB, and an unrelated model-lake filler is fetching seven further specimens (Qwen2.5-72B, GLM-4.5, GLM-4.5-Air, Mistral-Small-3.1-24B, Kimi-Linear-48B, Kimi-K3, DeepSeek-V4-Flash) at 25-43 MB/s, which starves a cold 32 MiB read to 0.42 MB/s. That is somebody else's running work and was NOT killed; the four-specimen cross-architecture sweep is running in the background and IS NOT CLAIMED HERE. CLAIM BOUNDARY: ONE model, ONE layer, FOUR organs, ONE setting (3 bits/group 64), and a 5-sentence capture that is enough to show the controls DISAGREE and not enough to characterise the input distribution. Output-space cosine on one layer is not coherence; the claim is only that the WEIGHT gate is blind to something the OUTPUT gate sees. No bpw recommendation is made for any model. 240 accelerator tests pass. || WHICH x, AND HOW MANY 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_GATE_DISAGREEMENT.json): CORRECTION FIRST, found by wiring the new function into accept_pack and reading its body -- ACCEPT_PACK'S REPRESENTATION GATE IS ALREADY OUTPUT-SPACE, comparing w_true @ x against a matvec of the packed bytes. Every number in the previous entry stands, because it measured gravity_native.fidelity() which IS weight-space, but the finding MOVES rather than vanishing: a single GAUSSIAN x is exactly the directionless input shown to be blind, so the live question is WHICH x AND HOW MANY. ACCELERATOR_ORGAN_DISCRIMINATION.json is amended in place to say so. MEASURED over 108 packs (6 layers x 6 organs x 3 bit widths, 176 real activation rows): the weight-space and full-capture output-space gates agree 94.44% of the time. FIVE FALSE NEGATIVES, ALL THE SAME ORGAN -- output.dense at 3 bits on 5 of 6 layers, bits the weight gate refuses to save; the sixth layer is refused by BOTH gates at 0.9838, so the pattern is a property of that organ and not a scatter. ONE FALSE POSITIVE, and it is reported as the near-threshold case it is: layer 4's value projection at 4 bits, 0.99273 against a 0.99 bar in weight space and 0.98974 in output space -- a boundary disagreement, not a blowout. THE MECHANISM IS NOW A NUMBER, NOT AN ANALOGY: feeding DIRECTIONLESS inputs through the same packs reproduces the weight-space cosine to a MEAN ABSOLUTE DEVIATION OF 0.000535 across all 108 packs (max 0.0034) while real inputs differ by 0.0253 -- 47.3x. The weight-space number IS the directionless-input number, measured. WORTH: judged in output space the 35 organs where both gates resolve would pack at 3.9683 complete bpw against 4.25, a 6.63% saving -- which SIZES the disagreement and authorises nothing. AND THE EXPECTED FIX IS REFUTED: SAMPLE SIZE BEATS REALISM. ONE REAL ACTIVATION ROW agrees with the full capture LESS often (83.3%) than ONE GAUSSIAN VECTOR (91.7%), with mean cosine gaps within 0.0002 of each other, because a single token is high-variance while a Gaussian averages over directions. The convergence curve is the usable rule: a ONE-ROW gate flips its verdict on 12.6% of packs, falling to 11.5% at 2 rows, 8.9% at 8, 5.7% at 16, 3.1% at 32 and 0.7% at 64, with the mean gap falling 0.0104 to 0.0005. THIS IS THE UNDERSAMPLED-FIT DISEASE SEALED EARLIER IN THIS PROGRAM, ARRIVING FROM THE OTHER SIDE OF THE MATMUL. SHIPPED: accept_pack(activations=...) REPORTS the wider reading beside the verdict and never as the verdict, so a caller without activations cannot silently receive a weaker answer. CLAIM BOUNDARY: one small bidirectional encoder, which is not a decoder and not an MoE; group 64 throughout; the convergence curve is measured against the 176-row capture and therefore says how fast a subsample approaches 176 rows, NOT whether 176 is enough; one layer's output cosine is still not coherence and composition is untested; and the four-specimen lake sweep is still running I/O-starved at 0.22-0.42 MB/s behind an unrelated filler and is NOT claimed. 242 accelerator tests pass. || HEADROOM IS THE VARIABLE, NOT SAMPLE SIZE OR DOMAIN 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_GATE_HEADROOM.json): the previous entry's claim boundary said in its own words that the convergence curve 'says how fast a subsample approaches 176 rows, NOT whether 176 is enough'. ANSWERED, and BOTH KNOBS I REACHED FOR TURN OUT TO BE THE WRONG ONES. Against a 1518-row pooled capture over 50 sentences in 5 domains, 176 rows agrees on 98.7% of 72 packs -- PREDICTION CONFIRMED AND MY REASONING WRONG, because 512 rows is NO BETTER (1.39% flip against 176's 1.27%) even as the mean cosine gap keeps falling 0.00103 to 0.00038 to 0.00018. Sampling error shrinks; the distance to the bar does not. AND THE DOMAIN PREDICTION IS REFUTED IN BOTH HALVES: I predicted domain would change >=5% of verdicts with a narrow domain ACCEPTING what the pool rejects; measured mean is 2.6%, only multilingual reaches the bar at 5.56%, CODE DISAGREES ON NOTHING, and the direction is symmetric rather than dangerous. Only 5 of 72 packs see any inter-domain disagreement. THE BANDING EXPLAINS BOTH AT ONCE AND IT IS A CLIFF, NOT A GRADIENT: packs with under 0.002 of headroom flip on 20.8% of 176-row resamples and 4 of the 5 domain disagreements live there; packs between 0.002 and 0.01 flip on 0.19%; packs beyond 0.01 flip on NONE and no domain ever disagrees about them. THE FLOAT32 BAR WAS 28x TOO OPTIMISTIC: near_threshold_headroom already reported safe_at_float32 at 100x the measured 2.85e-06 float32 disagreement = 2.85e-04, and THREE OF SIX unstable packs PASS it -- one flipping on 8.3% of resamples at headroom 0.00632, another disagreeing across domains at 0.00815. When the gate's inputs are a SAMPLE, arithmetic precision is not the widest source of disagreement and was being reported as if it were. SHIPPED decided_under_resampling at a 0.002 bar, where the flip rate collapses 20.8% to 0.19%, AND THE BAR IS DELIBERATELY NOT SET AT THE WIDEST UNSTABLE PACK: an accepted pack's cosine headroom is CAPPED at 1 - min_cosine, so a 0.01 bar with min_cosine 0.99 would call EVERY acceptance undecided -- a bar that refuses everything is not a safer bar, and a test pins that so nobody tightens it into vacuity. It is labelled an INDICATOR NOT A GUARANTEE because 2 of 72 packs above it were still unstable. THE FOUR-SPECIMEN LAKE SWEEP LANDED and it saturates everywhere: 11 organs across Qwen3-30B-A3B, its VL variant, Falcon-H1-7B and Kimi-VL-A3B ALL floor at 4.125 bpw, and at 4 bits / group 64 their cosines span 0.00105 -- the weight-space number is nearly invariant not only across organs but ACROSS ARCHITECTURES, the strongest form of the previous finding that it measures the distribution's scale. The two-block-old prediction that 'a setting adequate for one architecture's MLP is adequate for another's' is CONFIRMED under this metric and the confirmation is nearly worthless, because the metric cannot tell them apart in the first place. A DEFECT IN MY OWN PROBE, AND I BLAMED THE DRIVE: the sweep ran 40 minutes without a line and I attributed it to the USB volume delivering 0.22-0.42 MB/s under an unrelated filler. safetensors framework='np' CANNOT READ bf16 -- 'data type bfloat16 not understood' -- and every shard is bf16, so the loader would have raised on EVERY tensor inside a broad except that recorded the error and PRINTED NOTHING. Found by one bounded probe on ONE tensor, which also showed the index and open costing 5.24 s and 2.77 s rather than the wall I had assumed. WHAT IS AND IS NOT ESTABLISHED: the bf16 defect is CERTAIN; whether the stall was I/O is NOT -- the process sat in uninterruptible disk wait with 1.08 s of CPU and the fixed run completed in ~5 minutes with per-tensor loads of 2.9-65 s, so both were probably true and only one was measured. A BROAD EXCEPT AROUND AN I/O CALL MAKES A TYPE ERROR LOOK LIKE A SLOW DISK. CLAIM BOUNDARY: activations from ONE model, the four lake specimens graded in WEIGHT space because no runtime here executes a Qwen3-MoE, Falcon or Mamba forward pass; the 0.002 bar rests on 72 packs of one model; the 20.8% band holds FOUR packs; the five domains are 10 sentences each, enough to show they mostly AGREE and not enough to characterise any one of them; one layer's output cosine is still not coherence. 243 accelerator tests pass. || THE BLOCKER FIVE RECEIPTS REPEATED IS MISATTRIBUTED: THE READER EXISTS, THE BUS IS THE GATE 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_RUNTIME_GATE.json): FIVE G048 receipts justified grading all four lake specimens in WEIGHT SPACE with the same sentence -- 'no runtime here executes a Qwen3-MoE, Falcon or Mamba forward pass'. IT CONFLATES TWO RUNTIMES AND STATES ONE. Hawking's own Rust body dispatches on llama / llama2 / llama3 / llama3.1 / llama3.2 / mistral / qwen2 / qwen2.5 / qwen (crates/hawking-core/src/model/mod.rs:143-156) and really does cover NO lake specimen -- which is why the sentence sounded right. But mlx_lm 0.31.3, ALREADY A HARD DEPENDENCY AND THE RUNTIME EVERY AIR KERNEL IN THIS PROGRAM EXECUTES THROUGH, carries model classes for qwen3_moe, qwen3_vl_moe, kimi_vl AND falcon_h1 -- all four, verified by import. WHY THE ERROR MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A QUIBBLE: weight space is the space this program MEASURED to be nearly invariant across organs and architectures -- 11 organs over 4 architectures all floor at 4.125 bpw and span 0.00105 of cosine -- so the only available grade is the blind one, and the stated reason for not fixing it was A MISSING READER, which would be weeks of Rust. THE GATE THAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN IS STORAGE, and it is now a number: Falcon-H1-7B is the smallest specimen at 15.17 GB over 4 shards, and under the operator-prioritised fill a sequential read of one shard DID NOT COMPLETE 256 MiB IN 120 SECONDS and was still running past eight minutes -- under ~0.5 MB/s against the 96-131 MiB/s this same volume sustains uncontended, a contention penalty over 190x and HOURS for one load. Recorded as a NAMED GATE per §129 with its exact missing input -- a quiesced window or a Tier 1 staged copy -- alongside the powermetrics/thermal gate, the NVIDIA/P2 gate and the sudo-purge cold-read gate; NOT forced, because the operator explicitly prioritised the fill and staging 15.17 GB competes with exactly that. A GAP NAMED 'NO READER' INVITES THE WRONG WORK FOR WEEKS; A GAP NAMED 'CONTENDED BUS' INVITES ONE QUIESCED WINDOW, and naming the wrong one parks an obligation forever. SHIPPED odyssey_pass.runtime_coverage, which reports the two runtimes SEPARATELY because the receipts collapsed them and names blocked_on = FAST_LOCAL_STORAGE with detail saying explicitly that it is NOT a model reader; plus three tests -- one pinning that mlx_lm covers all four so the claim stays false until it becomes true again, one pinning that the Rust body still covers none (the half that was right), and one pinning that the gate names storage. THE CHECK CAN FAIL AND THAT WAS VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: adding a bogus architecture to the probe list flips the verdict to False and names it in the per-module table. All five affected receipts are AMENDED IN PLACE. CLAIM BOUNDARY: NO FORWARD PASS WAS RUN -- what is established is that the RUNTIME EXISTS and the obstacle is storage, while the activations are still absent and every weight-space caveat in the G048 receipts stands UNCHANGED; mlx_lm class presence is an IMPORT not an execution, so a class that imports can still fail on a real config and that is untested; the contended rate is an UPPER BOUND because the probe was killed by a harness timeout rather than completing, so the true figure may be lower; the uncontended 96-131 MiB/s is from earlier this session and is not re-measured here; no kernel changed and no performance claim moves. 454 accelerator tests pass (was 451). || IMPORTS IS NOT EXECUTES: THREE OF FOUR RUN A FORWARD PASS, THE FOURTH DOES NOT BUILD 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_RUNTIME_EXECUTES.json): the previous receipt named its own boundary -- 'mlx_lm class presence is an IMPORT not an execution, so a class that imports can still fail on a real config and that is untested'. TESTED, IN TWO STEPS. FIRST, the REAL config of each specimen resolved through MLX_LM'S OWN DISPATCH (model_type -> module) rather than module names I guessed, and ModelArgs.from_dict accepted all four. SECOND, the stronger thing: the real config with num_hidden_layers cut to 1, the model CONSTRUCTED, and a token sequence pushed through. Qwen3-30B-A3B BUILT 1245.5M params and returned finite logits (1,4,151936); Kimi-VL-A3B 754.1M and (1,4,163840); FALCON-H1-7B, THE MAMBA HYBRID, 953.3M and (1,4,130049) -- all finite, peak RSS 0.44 GiB. QWEN3-VL-30B-A3B FAILS TO CONSTRUCT, so THE IMPORT CHECK WAS RIGHT ABOUT THREE SPECIMENS AND WRONG ABOUT ONE, which is exactly why the stronger check had to be run rather than inherited. THE FAILURE IS EXACT AND IS NOT THE CONFIG BEING UNUSUAL: qwen3_vl_moe.Model builds its language model as qwen3_moe.ModelArgs.from_dict(args.text_config), and tie_word_embeddings sits at the TOP LEVEL of the real config (False) and is ABSENT from text_config, while qwen3_moe.ModelArgs REQUIRES IT WITH NO DEFAULT. CONFIRMED BY A TWO-ARM CONTROL rather than asserted: arm A, the config unchanged, raises the TypeError; arm B, the SAME config with that ONE key copied into text_config, BUILDS 1245.5M and runs to finite (1,4,151936). ONE KEY IS THE WHOLE DIFFERENCE -- and without that control the failure could have been MY OWN shrink dropping a field, which reads identically to a runtime gap in a summary line. TWO DEFECTS IN MY OWN PROBE, AND ONE MISLABELLED WHAT HAPPENED: the parameter count called mx.utils.tree_flatten, which does not exist (it is mlx.utils), and THAT LINE RUNS AFTER Model(args) SUCCEEDED -- so three specimens had already built and my probe printed 'FAILED at build' for all three. A PROBE THAT LABELS ITS OWN CRASH AS THE SUBJECT'S FAILURE is the class this program keeps finding, and it was wrong in the direction that would have parked the obligation; caught because the exception named MY module and not the library under test. The second was a shallow copy of nested config dicts, replaced with a deep copy so no arm shares substructure. WHAT THIS CHANGES: the G048 blocker moves a third time -- not 'no reader' (refuted last block), not 'the reader imports' (weaker than it read), but THREE ARCHITECTURES EXECUTE and one has a named one-field gap. WHAT IT DOES NOT CHANGE: NO REAL WEIGHTS WERE LOADED, the storage gate is untouched and still stands between this and real activations, every weight-space caveat in the G048 receipts stands exactly as written, and no adequacy claim moves. SHIPPED odyssey_pass.execution_coverage, keeping the MEASURED build/forward table separate from the import table with one_layer_only and random_weights as FIRST-CLASS FIELDS and VL_GAP naming the missing key; the import test now also asserts built_and_ran == 3 so the weaker claim can never be read as the stronger; a second test pins that imports and executes DISAGREE ON EXACTLY ONE specimen; and a third ACTUALLY REBUILDS Falcon-H1 from its real config and runs a token through, so the recorded table is not a string somebody could edit into agreement -- Falcon because its config is on LOCAL storage and a test must not fight the operator's fill. CLAIM BOUNDARY: ONE LAYER each, so the layer graph and forward path construct and execute and a full-depth model is NOT established; RANDOM WEIGHTS, a CAPABILITY claim about the runtime that says nothing about adequacy and does not touch the 2026-07-27 gaussian-proxy law, which governs grading compression; both VL models exercised on the TEXT PATH ONLY with no image passed; the VL gap is diagnosed in mlx_lm 0.31.3 against THIS config and nothing was patched in the library; finite logits from random weights is a WEAK correctness signal that rules out a NaN-producing graph and nothing more; no kernel changed. 456 accelerator tests pass (was 454) -- I first wrote 457 from arithmetic rather than from the run, and the receipt says what the suite says. || THE FORWARD PASS IS CAUSAL, WHICH IS THE PROPERTY FINITE LOGITS CANNOT SEE 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_CAUSALITY.json): the previous receipt named its own weakest point -- 'finite logits from random weights is a WEAK correctness signal that rules out a NaN-producing graph and nothing more'. WHAT THAT CHECK CANNOT SEE: a graph that IGNORES ITS INPUT ENTIRELY passes it, and so does one that LEAKS INFORMATION BACKWARDS IN TIME -- the hazard ACCELERATOR_CONVOLUTION.json already named in its own words, that a conv reading t+1 CHANGES NO NORM and shows up nowhere else. MEASURED ON ALL THREE SPECIMENS THAT BUILD: deterministic (the same sequence twice is BITWISE identical), input-sensitive, and CAUSAL -- changing the token at position 2 moves logits at positions 2 and 3 and leaves 0 and 1 BITWISE UNCHANGED, while changing the LAST token moves ONLY the last. That is the autoregressive property, on the MoE core, on a vision-language decoder, and on the MAMBA HYBRID whose causality lives in the width-4 conv this program built and controlled two dozen blocks ago. WHY RANDOM WEIGHTS ARE LEGITIMATE FOR THIS AND NOT FOR ADEQUACY: causality and input-dependence are properties of the GRAPH, not of the weights -- a wrong-direction read is wrong at EVERY weight setting -- so this is a real structural claim random weights cannot mask, and it still says NOTHING about adequacy, leaving the 2026-07-27 gaussian-proxy law untouched. THE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES THREE OF THREE A RESULT: three of three passing is EXACTLY the shape of a check that cannot fail, sealed five times in this program already, so the SAME check was run on a BIDIRECTIONAL attention block IDENTICAL BUT FOR THE MASK -- it moves [True, True, True, True], leaking to positions 0 and 1 exactly where a decoder must not, against the causal block's [False, False, True, True]. The check demonstrably separates the two. SHIPPED: execution_coverage now carries deterministic / input_sensitive / causal beside builds and forward, with the comment saying why random weights are legitimate for a structural property and not for adequacy; and TWO TESTS SIDE BY SIDE -- one asserting the REAL Falcon-H1 config is causal (chosen because its config is on LOCAL storage and a test must not fight the operator's fill) and one asserting the bidirectional control FAILS the same check, with a message saying that if it does not, the first test is measuring nothing. CLAIM BOUNDARY: ONE LAYER, RANDOM WEIGHTS, four tokens -- causality at depth 1 does not prove it at depth 44, though the layer is the unit where the mask lives; TEXT PATH ONLY for both vision-language models with no image passed; Qwen3-VL still does not construct and its one-field gap is unchanged and untested here; determinism is measured WITHIN one process on one machine; NO REAL WEIGHTS WERE LOADED so the storage gate is unchanged and every weight-space caveat in the G048 receipts stands exactly as written; no kernel changed. 458 accelerator tests pass (was 456) -- and I wrote 459 from arithmetic first, the IDENTICAL slip the previous receipt corrected in its own last line, which is recorded because a correction that does not change behaviour is not a correction.
