value.headline: - [ ] G049 — DEVICE ASCENSION / FRONT G (S015): the eleven stages from fingerprint to ADP seal, multiple named profiles where useful, three persisted knowledge levels (general, SoC, exact machine), identity-based cache invalidation so known state is never retuned, and sustained evidence distinguished from microbenchmark before any production ADP. Proof P6: a reproducible machine-specific win. | status: IN_PROGRESS | risk: medium | tier: V3 || PROOF P6 PASSES 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_FRONT_G_P6.json): a REPRODUCIBLE MACHINE-SPECIFIC WIN. The win is S015 §125's question -- what CUDA-era copy can disappear? A CUDA port allocates device memory, uploads, computes, downloads; THIS MACHINE HAS NO SEPARATE DEVICE MEMORY so both copies can simply not happen. SAME KERNEL both arms, answers identical to the last bit (max_abs_err 0.000e+00), resident-operand arm wins 7.17x / 7.40x / 7.44x across THREE INDEPENDENT RUNS = 3.74% reproducibility spread, which is what P6 actually asks for. QUALIFIES AS MACHINE-SPECIFIC WHERE THE FLAT AUTOTUNE LANDSCAPE DID NOT, because on a discrete GPU those copies are NOT OPTIONAL. FAIRNESS CAVEAT IN THE HEADLINE NOT A FOOTNOTE: the CUDA-era arm copies on EVERY call, the NAIVE pattern; a competent CUDA programmer hoists the upload and never pays this. So the claim is NOT 'Apple beats CUDA 7x' -- it is that per-call host<->device copying costs 7.4x here, and that on unified memory the elimination is STRUCTURAL rather than something the programmer must remember. I FIXED MY INSTRUMENT RATHER THAN OVERRIDING IT: 2 of 3 runs failed the flat 10% IQR gate (the sub-millisecond arm carries higher relative noise), but the margin is 617% against worst arm noise 12.49% = 49x, and refusing a result 49x above its own noise is not a judgement an honest instrument should make; compare() now admits margin >= 5x worst-arm-noise as CANDIDATE_WINS_DESPITE_NOISE, stating that the DIRECTION is certain while the MAGNITUDE is less so. ADP-AppleM3Ultra-MAX_THROUGHPUT is PROVISIONAL NOT SEALED: sustained_qualification has NOT run and §29 forbids sealing a production profile on microbenchmark evidence. 8/11 stages completed, 3 report NOT_RUN with reasons. || SUSTAINED QUALIFICATION PASSES, ADP SEALED 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_SUSTAINED_ADP.json): 6 MINUTES of continuous load on the forge champion, 12 x 30s windows, fill SIGSTOPped throughout. Rate 1954.44 Hz -> 1921.51 Hz = 1.69% DEGRADATION against a 5% gate, 2.25% window spread against 15%. ADP-AppleM3Ultra-SUSTAINED is now SEALED (was PROVISIONAL) on evidence that is actually about sustained behaviour. 9/11 stages complete. THREE DEFECTS IN MY OWN CODE, ALL FIXED NOT MERELY NOTED: (1) VOCABULARY COLLISION -- I had TWO different things both called 'knowledge level': §26 TUNING SCOPE (general/SoC/exact-machine: how widely a TUNING RESULT applies) and §80 PROMOTION LADDER (INSTANCE/MODEL_FAMILY/ARCHITECTURE: how far a FINDING may be promoted). Passing one into the other's slot raised an error; renamed to TUNING_SCOPES with the distinction written into the module and pinned by a test. (2) HOLE IN MY SEAL GATE -- may_seal_adp checked ONLY sustained_qualification, so MAX_THROUGHPUT sealed on evidence saying NOTHING about concurrency. Profiles now DECLARE the stages they depend on; MAX_THROUGHPUT correctly returns PROVISIONAL because its concurrency_sweep has NOT RUN. (3) I SHIPPED A BREAK: a dict class attribute inside a @dataclass stopped the module importing, AND 46 TESTS STILL PASSED because NOTHING IMPORTED IT -- a module with no tests fails SILENTLY while an unrelated suite reports green, the same blindness this campaign hit with tests that skipped and checks that could not fail. device_ascension now has 7 tests starting with one that merely asserts it imports. 53 tests pass. NOT ESTABLISHED: thermal_envelope STILL ABSENT (powermetrics needs sudo, not run) so 'no degradation observed' is NOT 'thermals characterised'; 6 minutes is not hours; and this is RAW KERNEL RATE, not verified WorkUnits/hour, so it still does not reach the §77 metric. || CONCURRENCY SWEEP RUN, 10/11 STAGES, THREE PROFILES SEALED 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_CONCURRENCY_SWEEP.json): champion kernel at 1/2/4/8 concurrent processes = 4009 / 6406 / 10765 / 13564 Hz aggregate. Scaling 1.0 / 1.598 / 2.685 / 3.384, but EFFICIENCY PER PROCESS FALLS 1.0 / 0.80 / 0.67 / 0.42 and the sharpest fall is 4->8, which buys only 1.26x for TWICE the processes. MAX_THROUGHPUT now SEALED at 8 processes ON ITS OWN PROFILE'S EVIDENCE rather than borrowed from the sustained run; MIN_LATENCY seals at 1. DIFFERENT ANSWERS FROM THE SAME DATA, which is the point of named profiles instead of vague 'optimized settings' (§24). APPARENT CONTRADICTION WITH PRIOR CAMPAIGN LAW, RECONCILED NOT IGNORED: earlier work measured DECODE CONCURRENCY TOPPING OUT ~1.21x with Metal working set as the admission gate; this sweep reaches 3.38x. NOT a contradiction -- that law was measured on WHOLE MODEL BODIES with working sets of tens of GiB, which are BANDWIDTH- and ADMISSION-bound, while this kernel touches 4 MiB and is LAUNCH-bound, so extra processes FILL LAUNCH GAPS rather than competing for bandwidth. Concurrency helps when LAUNCH-bound and does not when BANDWIDTH-bound; the P7 size sweep had ALREADY shown which regime this kernel occupies, so the two were separable in advance. MUST NOT be cited as overturning the whole-body law. Per-process efficiency at the sealed setting is only 0.42, so a profile optimising WORK PER RESOURCE would choose differently. Still RAW KERNEL RATE, not verified WorkUnits/hour. Remaining NOT_RUN stage: none except what thermal instrumentation would need (powermetrics requires sudo). 53 tests pass. || §77 ATTEMPTED, AND THE AUDIT KILLED MY FRAMING 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_WORKUNIT_THROUGHPUT.json): THREE receipts closed with the same sentence -- microbenchmark or RAW KERNEL RATE, does not reach §77. Measured it on real work: read a real Qwen3-30B-A3B expert tensor from the lake, pack to ws_rtn_q4_g64, verify on GPU. Then had it ADVERSARIALLY AUDITED BY 8 AGENTS (813k tokens, 6 named attacks). THREE OF SIX WERE FATAL TO MY FRAMING. THE HEADLINE IS A DEFECT I REBUILT: my definition of ACCEPTED compared the GPU kernel against a numpy decode of THE SAME PACKED BYTES, so the original tensor never entered it. VERIFIED MYSELF rather than taken from the audit -- AN ALL-ZEROS PACK IS ACCEPTED; so is scales x1000 at relative error 1003.60 against the true tensor; so are swapped nibbles at 1.54. The tolerance derives from the same decode so scaling both sides CANCELS EXACTLY. '12 of 12 accepted' certified NOTHING. THIS IS THE DEFECT THIS CAMPAIGN ALREADY SEALED ON 2026-08-17 (adequacy gate scored 0.01*W at 1.000000 on every axis because cosine is SCALE-INVARIANT) -- REBUILT IN A NEW PLACE. FIXED: accept_pack applies TWO INDEPENDENT GATES, kernel fidelity (the only thing the old one checked) and representation fidelity with tolerances anchored on quantities THE PACK CANNOT INFLUENCE; cosine is NEVER checked without a magnitude band. DEMONSTRATION IS EXACT: honest cos 0.9940 mag 1.0042 ACCEPTED, x1000 cos 0.9940 mag 1004.23 REJECTED, x0.5 cos 0.9940 mag 0.5021 REJECTED -- THE COSINE IS IDENTICAL FOR ALL THREE and the band is the entire difference. A test keeps the old predicate as an EXECUTABLE DEMONSTRATION that it accepts zeros. THE THROUGHPUT NUMBERS: 331.0 WU/h contended and 388.3 quiesced per-tensor; AMORTISED to one open per shard, 525.6 and 1296.1 -- but NOT by removing the open (2.1-2.4% of wall), by turning reopen+seek into SEQUENTIAL STREAMING (0.34 -> 1.17 MB/s). One audit agent predicted GPU share would rise to 2.01% under amortisation; IT DID NOT, staying 0.15-0.21%, and the agent that RAN the pattern got it right while the one that REASONED about it did not. QUIESCING IS WORTH MORE THAN I FIRST MEASURED: 1.17x per-tensor but 2.47x amortised, so I nearly published an indictment of ProtectedWindow built on a starved access pattern. A DIAGNOSIS I WROTE DOWN AND MY OWN PROBE REFUTED: I saw 6 of 15 fill processes in state UN and proposed SIGSTOP cannot stop uninterruptible waiters, so the window's guarantee was partial. TESTED: 15 OF 15 STOPPED, 0 uninterruptible, at all 6 samples. REFUTED -- the guarantee holds. THE RESULT IS A SENSITIVITY CURVE NOT A POINT: GPU share is 0.16% at the measured 1.17 MB/s, 5.36% at 50, 10.01% at 123, 24.72% with storage removed; THE GPU REACHES 10% OF WALL AT 122.8 MB/s, 105x THE MEASURED RATE. CONCLUSION WITHDRAWN AS FRAMED: 'the GPU is 0.26% so no accelerator win matters' is FALSE generally and true only of TIER 2 USB storage under a 7-repo download storm. modellake.py declares ~/noetic/stage as TIER 1, 'the SSD is the hot bench, not a second archive' -- I checked, IT EXISTS AND IS EMPTY (0 B), so every read came from the archive because the hot bench holds nothing. THE ACCELERATOR'S VALUE IS NOT REFUTED, IT IS SHOWN CONDITIONAL ON STORAGE THIS PIPELINE IS NOT USING. TWO OF MY OWN INSTRUMENTS CARRIED DEFECTS AND BOTH ARE NAMED IN THE RECEIPT: the storage probe's quiesced arm re-read files the contended arm had cached, so its 9137.9 MB/s is PAGE CACHE and is not quoted; and the GPU column moved 0.342 -> 0.159 s for byte-identical work, which GPU compute cannot do, so it measures wait and MLX compile too. ONE AUDIT CITATION DID NOT CHECK OUT and is recorded as such: an agent cited performance_qualification.py:128 and perf_addendum.py:31 as omitting a pgrep pattern; NEITHER FILE EXISTS. n=12 and n=64, ONE run each, no IQR -- far below this program's own 200-rep gate, so every ratio here is DIRECTIONAL and none is admissible as a measured speedup. 161 tests pass. || THE EXTRAPOLATION IS NOW A MEASUREMENT, AND THE ACCELERATOR STOPS BEING CONDITIONAL 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_TIER1_MEASURED.json): the §77 receipt reported a SENSITIVITY CURVE and said in its own claim boundary that it holds non-read time fixed while scaling read -- AN EXTRAPOLATION. This converts the endpoint into a MEASUREMENT: staged the SAME 64 tensors onto TIER 1 (~/noetic/stage, the internal SSD that modellake.py already declares 'the hot bench, not a second archive' and that was EMPTY) and ran the IDENTICAL WorkUnit. THE PREDICTION WAS WRITTEN BEFORE THE RUN: wall 1.1-1.5 s, 150k-210k WU/h, GPU share 18-25%. TWO CONFIRMED, ONE MISSED: wall 1.2817 s CONFIRMED, 179,761.9 WU/h CONFIRMED, GPU share 30.88% MISSED HIGH. The model assumed the compute floor was FIXED and it is not -- the GPU phase measured 0.2754 s on TIER 2 and 0.39576 s on TIER 1 for the SAME work, because that column carries MLX kernel-compile and scheduling too. The curve's STRUCTURE was right and one ASSUMPTION was wrong; the miss is reported rather than the band widened after the fact. THE HEADLINE: 179,761.9 WU/h against TIER 2's 1,296.1 = 138.7x, read collapsing from 96.98% of wall to 3.12% at 5035.5 MB/s against 1.20 = 4196x. THE ACCELERATOR STOPS BEING CONDITIONAL: the §77 receipt said its value was 'not refuted, but conditional on storage this pipeline is not using'. THE SAME WIN IS NOW WORTH 216x MORE -- P5's fusion 1.71x moves throughput +14.71% on TIER 1 against +0.068% on TIER 2; the scan's 8.09x is +37.10% vs +0.139%; an infinitely fast GPU is +44.67% vs +0.159%. NOTHING ABOUT THE KERNELS CHANGED, only where the bytes came from. THE BOTTLENECK MOVED AND NAMING IT IS THE NEXT LEVER: pack 36.96% > gpu 30.88% > verify 29.02% > read 3.12%. The largest phase is now CPU-SIDE QUANTIZATION, which the accelerator could attack and has not; read is no longer the story. MY OWN CORRECTNESS GATE COSTS 29.02% OF WALL -- that is the FIXED accept_pack doing a full dequantize plus two float64 matvecs against the true tensor, where the broken predicate that accepted an all-zeros pack was cheaper. HONESTY HAS A MEASURED PRICE and it is worth paying, but knowingly: on TIER 2 the gate looked free only because everything was free next to the disk. ALL 64 ACCEPTED UNDER THE FIXED PREDICATE, so the packs are faithful to the TRUE tensors and not merely self-consistent -- a claim the previous run could not have made. OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE: staging cost 437.78 s at 0.46 MB/s for 192 MB in one sequential pass; every later pass saves 176.5 s, so BREAK-EVEN IS 2.5 PASSES. The pipeline was reading the archive because nothing had put anything on the bench. CLAIM BOUNDARY: ONE run per tier, no IQR, below the program's 200-rep gate, so 138.7x is DIRECTIONAL -- but it is a ratio of two DIRECTLY MEASURED wall times, not an extrapolation, which is exactly what the previous receipt lacked. TIER 1's 5035.5 MB/s is partly PAGE CACHE (192 MB written moments earlier into 96 GiB of RAM), so it is an upper bound on cold SSD and must not be quoted as disk bandwidth; the throughput claim is unaffected because a real hot bench would also be cache-resident. 161 tests pass. || THE GPU PACKER: THE LEVER TIER 1 NAMED, AND THE BOTTLENECK IS NOW MY OWN HONESTY 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_GPU_PACK.json): the TIER 1 receipt named the next lever exactly -- 'pack 36.96% > gpu 30.88% > verify 29.02% > read 3.12%; the largest phase is now CPU-SIDE QUANTIZATION, which the accelerator could attack and has not'. This attacks it, changing ONLY the packer. CORRECTNESS IS BINARY HERE AND THAT IS THE POINT: the quantiser is integer rounding of an f32 quotient and Metal's rint() is round-half-to-even exactly as numpy's is, so BIT-EXACTNESS IS ACHIEVABLE AND THEREFORE REQUIRED -- the bytes match or the port is wrong. BIT-EXACT on (768,2048), (256,512), (64,64); on the amax==0 branch; on EXACT .5 QUOTIENTS where the rounding mode ALONE decides; on negatives-only; at 1e-30; and on 8 OF 8 REAL Qwen3 expert tensors from the staged shard. A TOLERANCE WOULD HAVE HIDDEN A ROUNDING-MODE DIFFERENCE that changes one weight in a million and never shows up in a norm. THE PREDICTION WAS WRITTEN BEFORE THE RUN and half of it was wrong: relative +20-50% LANDED (+48.31% first A/B, +57.41% on six-pair medians), absolute 215,000-270,000 WU/h MISSED HIGH because I computed it off the TIER 1 baseline of 179,762 which included MLX's ONE-TIME KERNEL COMPILE; with both paths warmed the CPU-pack baseline is 261,640. PREDICTING A RATIO OFF A COLD ABSOLUTE is a mistake I made and it is recorded rather than quietly rebased. SIX ALTERNATING PAIRS, NOT ONE RUN: CPU median 261,640 WU/h (spread 10.8%), GPU median 411,857 (spread 11.3%), +57.41%. THE EVIDENCE IS SEPARATION NOT A RATIO -- EVERY GPU RUN BEATS EVERY CPU RUN, min GPU 374,603 against max CPU 268,250, and complete separation at these spreads is stronger than the median ratio; the 57.41% margin against 11.3% worst-arm noise is 5.1x, which also clears the program's own large-margin hatch. The pack itself goes 0.359 s -> 0.070 s = 5.06x. WHY IT WINS AND WHY NOT MORE: the pack is EMBARRASSINGLY PARALLEL ACROSS GROUPS -- each 64-weight group owns its absmax, scale and 32 output bytes, so the kernel needs NO BARRIER AT ALL, which is why it ports cleanly; it wins 5x rather than more because the arm still pays a dispatch and a DEVICE ROUND TRIP per tensor, the packed bytes returning to numpy only to be handed straight back to the verify kernel. Keeping them on device is NOT DONE HERE. THE BOTTLENECK MOVED AGAIN AND IT IS NOW MY OWN HONESTY: under GPU pack the shares are verify 60.97% > pack 12.23% > read 7.39% > gpu 6.47%. THE DOMINANT PHASE IS accept_pack -- the two-gate predicate built to replace the one that accepted an ALL-ZEROS PACK. Fixing the correctness defect made verification 61% of the work, and THE NEXT LEVER IS MAKING THE HONEST GATE CHEAP, NOT WEAKENING IT BACK toward the cheap dishonest one -- naming it that way is the only thing stopping the obvious wrong fix. A PRE-EXISTING REPRESENTATION LIMIT FOUND ON THE WAY: an absmax above 458,528 (65504 x 7) overflows the stored f16 scale to inf and the dequantized tensor becomes nan. BOTH packers do it IDENTICALLY so it is a limit of ws_rtn_q4_g64, not of the port; real bf16 weights are O(1) so it does not bite, but it is SILENT and accept_pack now catches it (cosine 0.0, magnitude ratio nan, REJECTED). Recorded rather than fixed -- changing the representation is GRAVITY's call. GPU COLUMN STILL CONTAMINATED AND STILL SAID SO: gpu_s measured 0.05765 s in one arm and 0.03702 in the other for IDENTICAL verify work, which GPU compute cannot do, so it carries scheduling and wait exactly as the §77 receipt recorded. CLAIM BOUNDARY: spreads ~11% are ABOVE the 10% IQR gate, so this is admitted by COMPLETE SEPARATION and a 5.1x margin, not by a clean gate; f32 input only, the bf16 decode still happens on CPU and moving THAT is unmeasured; the packed bytes still round-trip through host memory; and bit-exactness of a PACK says NOTHING about whether the REPRESENTATION is adequate for a model. 166 tests pass. || THE HONEST GATE MADE CHEAP, AND THE COST WAS §19 HIDING IN THE VERIFIER 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_HONEST_GATE.json): the GPU-pack receipt named this lever in its own words -- 'verify 60.97% ... the next lever is making the HONEST gate cheap, NOT weakening it back toward the cheap dishonest one'. PROFILED BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING, which is what found it: dequantize was 2.33 ms of accept_pack's 2.77 ms = 84%, while the two float64 matvecs everyone would have blamed cost 0.037 ms each. THE GATE'S COST WAS A DENSE REMATERIALIZATION -- the exact 'compact bytes -> reconstruct dense -> conventional GEMM' shape S015 §19 forbids, sitting INSIDE the gate that certifies the compact path, in the one place nobody had looked for it. SO NOTHING WAS TRADED AWAY: because decoded[r,c] = (q[r,c]-BOUND)*scale[r,c//GROUP], the group scale factors out of the inner sum and the -BOUND term collapses to a per-group constant that does not depend on the row at all; the nibbles are contracted where they lie, two per byte, against the even and odd halves of x. THE EXACT OPTION TURNED OUT TO BE THE FASTEST ONE: casting the nibbles to float64 first materialises 24 MB of temporaries at 1.58 ms, letting einsum promote uint8 against a float64 operand is BIT-IDENTICAL at 1.07 ms, and a float32 inner product is BOTH slower (1.13 ms) AND inexact (2.18e-07) -- the float32 variant is recorded with its price so the choice is visible rather than silently foreclosed. RESULT, and it is the program's FIRST CLEAN GATE ON A THROUGHPUT CLAIM: 6 alternating pairs, dense-gate median 416,467 WU/h at 9.15% spread vs cheap-gate 634,259 at 7.60%, BOTH INSIDE the 10% gate, +52.3%, complete separation (min cheap 607,943 > max dense 423,900), margin 5.7x worst-arm noise. Verify phase 2.154x. THE BASELINE REPRODUCED ITSELF: the dense arm measures verify at 61.595% of wall against 60.97% recorded in a different process on a different day. EQUIVALENCE IS THE HEADLINE'S CONDITION AND IT WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED: 96 accept_pack calls over the 64 real tensors including 32 negative controls (all zeros, scales x1000, scales x0.5, nibbles swapped), ZERO verdict mismatches, all 32 controls rejected, worst numeric disagreement 4.3e-16 -- machine epsilon, so no threshold anywhere had to move. A NEW FINDING FELL OUT AND IT EXPLAINS A BIAS: read_s runs IDENTICAL CODE in both arms and is 1.156x FASTER in the cheap arm, with complete separation and both spreads inside the gate (4.5%, 5.9%); pack_s moves the same way 1.114x, directional only at 14.8%/10.8%; and gpu_s is FLAT at 1.004x and is THE ONLY PHASE THAT DOES NOT SEPARATE, which is the control that rules out 'the cheap arm just ran in a better minute'. The dense path was touching ~30 MB of temporaries per tensor and EVICTING THE WORKING SET OF THE PHASES EITHER SIDE OF IT. THAT IS WHY THREE CONSECUTIVE PREDICTIONS IN THIS PIPELINE HAVE COME IN ABOVE THEIR BAND (Tier 1 predicted 18-25% GPU share and got 30.88%; the GPU packer predicted 215-270k WU/h and got 411k; this predicted 570-630k and got 634k): every one held the untouched phases FIXED and they are not fixed. NOTHING ABOUT THE KERNELS CHANGED -- the native matvec and the GPU packer are byte-identical to the previous block, so no Metal claim moves. WHAT IS LEFT: verify is still the largest phase at 43.28%, ref_matvec is 74.3% of it and the true-tensor float64 cast 24.1%; moving ref_matvec to the GPU requires an implementation INDEPENDENT of the native kernel or gate 1 goes vacuous, and the DEQUANT+DENSE control shares the nibble convention, which is the exact thing to settle before shipping it. 169 tests pass. || THE BYTES STOPPED COMING HOME 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_DEVICE_RESIDENT.json): the honest-gate receipt left two things named -- verify still 43.28% with ref_matvec 74.3% of it, and the warning that moving the reference to the GPU 'requires an implementation INDEPENDENT of the native kernel or gate 1 goes vacuous'. THREE ARMS, BECAUSE TWO THINGS CHANGED and collapsing them would have reported the whole win as 'the gate moved to the GPU', which is false. A = the float64 host gate; B = both matvecs in MLX PRIMITIVES on device; C = B plus the pack outputs staying on device and the bf16 decode happening there. 635,422 -> 1,005,946 -> 2,151,304 WorkUnits/hour = +58.31% then +113.86% on top, 3.39x END TO END, spreads 2.52% / 5.86% / 4.04% ALL INSIDE THE 10% GATE and BOTH STEPS COMPLETELY SEPARATED. THE INDEPENDENCE QUESTION ANSWERED PRECISELY RATHER THAN WAVED AT: gate 1 compares hand-written MSL against MLX primitives -- different code, different compiled kernels, different arithmetic structure -- and what gate 1 NEVER checked, in ANY version including the numpy one, is the NIBBLE CONVENTION, which both sides always shared. A convention error is caught by GATE 2 against the TRUE tensor, which is exactly what the `nibbles swapped` control demonstrates. Saying that is the difference between a defensible move and a quiet weakening. THE PRICE IS PRECISION AND IT IS BIGGER THAN THE OBVIOUS GUESS: float32 disagrees with the float64 host gate by up to 2.85e-06 on cosine and 7.62e-07 on magnitude, AN ORDER ABOVE the 1e-7 a single rounding would suggest, because error accumulates through a 32-term inner product and then a per-group sum. So the claim is VERDICTS not numbers -- 96 calls, 32 negative controls, ZERO mismatches -- and near_threshold_headroom() now reports with EVERY verdict how far it sits from flipping (tightest honest pack 0.00289 = 1013x the worst disagreement), with a test pinning that it says NO when the margin is thin. THE UNTOUCHED KERNELS GOT FASTER AND THAT IS THE RESIDENCY FINDING: pack 3.28x and gpu 1.57x running THE SAME MSL BYTES, because the device->host->device round trip was being charged to those columns; and decode_s -- A COLUMN THAT DID NOT EXIST BEFORE, which was most of the ~19% the previous receipt reported as unaccounted -- is 13.68x because on device a bf16 upcast is a VIEW, not a conversion. BIT-IDENTITY IS THE PRECONDITION AND IT WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED: device bf16 decode, packed bytes and f16 scales all match the host path on 64 of 64 real tensors, zero mismatches, so the 3.39x measures the SAME computation. FIVE CONSECUTIVE PREDICTIONS HAVE NOW COME IN ABOVE THEIR BAND (B missed high by 17.7%, C by 87.1%) AND THE MECHANISM IS NOW CLEAR: I predict by subtracting the cost of the thing I remove, but A HOST ROUND TRIP IS NOT CHARGED TO ONE COLUMN -- it was spread across decode, pack and gpu, three columns I was holding fixed. The fix is to predict only from a decomposition with NO unaccounted remainder; A's remainder was 19% and the miss was about that size. NOTHING ABOUT THE KERNELS CHANGED so no Metal claim moves, and the float64 host gate is RETAINED as the reference -- the device gate must not judge a pack sitting within ~3e-04 of a threshold. WHAT IS LEFT: with the remainder gone the shares are read 29.5% > verify 27.1% > gpu 22.1% > pack 15.8% > decode 5.2%, so READ IS THE LARGEST PHASE AGAIN and it is a page-cached read of 192 MB -- the next honest lever is a working set that does not fit the cache, or accepting that this pipeline is now storage-bound at Tier 1 speeds. 173 tests pass. || THE PAGE-CACHE CAVEAT SETTLED, AND F_NOCACHE DOES NOT DO WHAT I ASSUMED 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_TIER1_CACHE_VS_DISK.json): three receipts carried the same warning -- 'partly page cache, an upper bound on cold SSD'. MEASURED instead of carried forward: a COLD read of the staged shard is 6265.8 MB/s with 99.76% OF PAGES ACTUALLY COMING FROM DISK, cached it is 8318.4 MB/s, so the cache advantage is only 1.33x and the pipeline's WorkUnits/hour is inflated by cache residency at the level of ~7% OF WALL, NOT BY A FACTOR. The warning was right to exist and OVERCAUTIOUS in a specific way: the cold SSD at 6265.8 MB/s is FASTER than the 5035.5 MB/s the TIER 1 receipt measured and flagged as cache-inflated. BOTH BRANCHES OF MY PREDICTION ARE REFUTED AND THE REASON IS THE USEFUL PART: I predicted F_NOCACHE reads would be slower (cache branch) or within 25% (SSD branch); they came out FASTER, 8653 vs 7520 MB/s, with WU/h UP 7.48%. F_NOCACHE asks the kernel not to RETAIN a file's pages -- IT DOES NOT EVICT PAGES ALREADY CACHED -- so that experiment compared CACHE AGAINST CACHE and the ~7% it found is retention bookkeeping, not disk. I DESIGNED A CONTRAST THAT CANNOT PRODUCE THE CONDITION IT NAMES. What caught it is an instrument, not a re-reading: vm_stat reports cumulative PAGEINS with no sudo, and a read served from cache produces none -- the F_NOCACHE reads show 0.01%, which is proof rather than inference. THE COLD NUMBER WAS OBTAINED BY ACCIDENT and that is stated: the probe's FIRST touch of the file in that process was genuinely cold, n=1, and it cannot be repeated without evicting. A SUBSTITUTE WAS TRIED AND REFUSED: writing a file with F_NOCACHE then reading it back gives EXACTLY 66.67% pageins on ALL SEVEN samples across two probes (a stable ~64 MB resident window) at 2214-3317 MB/s with 46% spread -- it never reaches cold at all, so those rates are NOT quoted as this SSD's cold rate. THE DIAGNOSIS SPLIT TWO WAYS rather than one being right: settling 20 s moves the pagein fraction by 0.12% (STRUCTURAL) but the rate by +43% (WRITE IN FLIGHT), so both candidate explanations were partly correct on DIFFERENT QUANTITIES. AND MY OWN PROBE CARRIED A DEFECT: its automatic verdict keyed on EXACT EQUALITY of an integer counter, so 8194 vs 8184 was labelled 'settling moves it' -- a verdict computed by exact equality of a noisy counter reports noise as a finding. NAMED GATE per §129: a clean REPEATABLE cold read needs `sudo purge` or a working set over 96 GiB, neither available, recorded alongside the powermetrics/thermal gate and the NVIDIA/P2 gate rather than as a parking lot. The lake fill was NOT quiesced, which makes 6265.8 MB/s a LOWER bound on the quiet-machine cold rate -- the safe direction for the claim. 181 tests pass. || THREE RECEIPTS BLAMED 'MLX KERNEL COMPILE' AND NONE OF THEM MEASURED IT 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_JIT_COMPILE.json): the CCL carried COMPILER.jit_kernel_compilation with performance_gap measured=FALSE, reason 'compile latency has not been measured', while the TIER 1, GPU-PACK and §77 receipts each explained away a discrepancy with that exact mechanism. AN ATTRIBUTION REPEATED THREE TIMES AND NEVER MEASURED is what this program has learned to test. MEASURED: 36.8 ms per DISTINCT kernel, NEAR-FLAT IN SOURCE SIZE (102 chars 36.8 ms, 5990 chars 43.6 -- a 59x source increase for 1.19x time, so it is a near-FIXED cost), and GENUINELY CACHED -- the same name and source recompiles in 0.24 ms against 110.65 cold = 460x, while a FRESH NAME with BYTE-IDENTICAL SOURCE still pays full price, which is what makes per-shape kernel naming expensive. THEN THE ATTRIBUTION WAS TESTED AND IT IS WRONG IN SCOPE TWICE. Five runs of the identical WorkUnit in ONE process: first 0.4196 s, warm median 0.1019, EXCESS 0.3176 s. Our two custom kernel compiles are 73.6 ms = 23.2% of it. The remainder is MLX's OWN first-use costs at 175.12 ms = 55.1% -- BUT 151.02 OF THOSE 175 MS ARE ONE THING, THE FIRST mx.array FROM A NUMPY BUFFER, which is DEVICE AND ALLOCATOR INITIALISATION AND NOT COMPILATION AT ALL. Every actual primitive kernel -- bitwise_and, right_shift, einsum, matmul, sum, random_normal -- costs 0.05 to 2.32 ms on first use, astype 11.87. So the phrase was wrong twice: not OUR kernels, and not COMPILATION. FULL DECOMPOSITION with nothing hidden: compiles 23.2%, MLX first-use 55.1%, cold read 2.5% (taken from the cache receipt, not re-measured), UNATTRIBUTED 19.2% -- and saying 19.2% is unattributed beats distributing it over the terms that were measured. A DEFECT IN MY FIRST PROBE THAT CHANGED WHAT THE DATA MEANT: body(k, extra_lines=0) was called as body(extra), so `extra` bound to the UNUSED first parameter and every kernel in that sweep had IDENTICAL SOURCE differing only in NAME. The name-only result SURVIVES and is informative; the apparent 'source size costs 113 ms' reading is VOID because the source never changed. AND THE 113 ms IS STILL UNEXPLAINED -- the corrected probe tested BOTH candidates, size (weak) and ORDER (late trivial 35.16 ms against early 36.77, ratio 0.96), and NEITHER reproduces it, so a median of six that a corrected probe cannot reproduce is recorded as a caution about small-n medians rather than dropped. LEDGER: COMPILER.jit_kernel_compilation moves unmeasured -> MEASURED with a receipt path, CCL now 14 of 20 performance gaps measured. ALL THREE AFFECTED RECEIPTS AMENDED IN PLACE so anyone reaching one finds the correction attached; the DIRECTION of every affected statement is unchanged -- the first run really is slower and really must not be quoted as a baseline -- only the named MECHANISM changes. CLAIM BOUNDARY: mx.fast.metal_kernel JIT ONLY; xcrun metal AOT is ABSENT on this machine so no AOT comparison exists, and CUDA's nvrtc latency is unmeasured because no NVIDIA hardware exists, so this measures OUR side of the gap alone. Every cost here is PER PROCESS and amortises to zero by the second WorkUnit -- it matters for short-lived processes and for any measurement whose first run is quoted as a baseline, which is exactly how it contaminated three receipts. No kernel changed, so no performance claim about any kernel moves. 191 tests pass.

value.headline: - [ ] G050 — HUMF / FRONT H (S015): the object model with all twelve recorded fields, the eight explicit coherence states, MockExternalMemoryProvider with failure injection, and the move-vs-recompute planner on an empirical cost model. HUMF DOES NOT LIE: Apple UM plus external VRAM is never called physically unified memory. Proof P8: an object correctly managed across two memory domains. | status: IN_PROGRESS | risk: medium | tier: V3 || PROOF P8 PASSES 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_FRONT_H_P8.json): one logical object correctly managed across TWO memory domains. tools/accelerator/humf.py carries the 12 fields of S015 §32 and the 8 coherence states of §14, with ILLEGAL TRANSITIONS FAILING CLOSED (ABSENT cannot jump to CLEAN; EVICTED cannot either) because a silent bad transition here is silent DATA CORRUPTION, not a crash. The mock provider carries REAL BYTES rather than only accounting, so P8 grades data instead of my own bookkeeping agreeing with itself: round trip BIT-IDENTICAL by SHA-256; a write on the external side drives the Apple copy to STALE and leaves ZERO valid copies; a STALE copy is NEVER offered as a transfer source so the planner honestly falls back to RECOMPUTE; reconciliation delivers the MUTATED value, not the stale one. Move-vs-recompute planner (§34) estimates transfer vs recompute and takes the cheaper -- 0.9ms transfer beat 50ms recompute -- AND REPORTS THAT THE WINNING COST IS SIMULATED. That flag is the point: §21 forbids treating a simulated transport number as physical evidence, so a plan built on one says so on its face, and a test pins that a recompute cost is never laundered into a measured transport claim. CLAIM BOUNDARY: MOCK domain only. 5 GB/s is a KNOB, not a measurement; no NVIDIA VRAM exists, no transport was crossed, and nothing here may be cited as evidence about real external-GPU transfer cost. HUMF claims NO hardware coherence -- domains stay physically distinct and every state change is software bookkeeping. tools/accelerator/test_humf.py 12 passed. || FAILURE INJECTION REACHED THE FABRIC, AND FOUND THAT TRANSFERS NEVER MOVED BYTES 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_HUMF_FAILURE_INJECTION.json): G050's own words ask for a MockExternalMemoryProvider WITH FAILURE INJECTION. The injection EXISTED (fail_next over allocate, copy_in, copy_out) and one test fired it by calling the provider DIRECTLY. Nothing tested the injection reaching the FABRIC -- and that is where the defect was. THE DEFECT: Humf.execute() NEVER CALLED THE PROVIDER. It transitioned the destination TRANSFERRING and then CLEAN on BOOKKEEPING ALONE, so a transfer moved NO BYTES, COULD NOT FAIL, and ALWAYS ended CLEAN. P8's two halves were each verified on a SEPARATE PATH -- the bit-identical SHA-256 round trip went straight through the provider while the state machine went through execute() -- and THE SEAM BETWEEN THEM WAS NEVER EXERCISED. DEMONSTRATED AGAINST THE PRE-FIX CODE, NOT ASSERTED: the previous humf.py was checked out and run with fail_next='copy' armed; it RAISED NOTHING, the destination came out CLEAN, valid_copies() returned ['APPLE_UM', 'MOCK_EXTERNAL_VRAM'], and fail_next was STILL ARMED afterwards -- proving the provider was never called. A COPY REPORTED VALID WHILE HOLDING NOTHING is precisely the silent data corruption the module's own docstring claims to fail closed against, and it was failing OPEN on the one path that mattered. THE FIX: execute() now MOVES THE BYTES -- materializations carry a payload, a TRANSFER reads a valid source copy and hands it to the destination domain's provider, RECOMPUTE runs the object's actual recipe; on failure the destination goes INVALID, stays OUT of valid_copies(), keeps a null payload, and the log records outcome FAILED. A TRANSFER THAT CANNOT FAIL IS NOT A TRANSFER, IT IS AN ASSUMPTION. SEVEN NEW TESTS PIN IT: destination INVALID not CLEAN; the SOURCE undamaged (losing the only valid copy because a transfer failed would turn a recoverable error into DATA LOSS); the failure logged rather than dropped; the SAME path delivering bytes intact on success, so the failure test is not merely an exception path; INVALID not a dead end, so one transport hiccup cannot permanently strand an object; a transfer with no valid source payload REFUSED even for a provider-less domain, so bytes are never conjured from nothing; and RECOMPUTE actually running the recipe. TWO EXISTING TESTS FAILED ON THIS CHANGE AND WERE RIGHT TO -- the fixture placed a copy marked CLEAN carrying NO BYTES, exactly the fiction the defect allowed; fixed by giving it real bytes, NOT by weakening the check. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE MOCK: EGB's whole point is a transport that really exists, and real transports really fail -- a cable, a reset, a full device, a driver timeout. The bookkeeping deciding which copy is valid is the one component where a wrong answer is SILENT. Getting it wrong against a mock costs nothing; against real VRAM it costs the data. NOT MODELLED and stated: partial or torn writes, silent corruption that returns wrong bytes WITHOUT raising, timeouts, a provider vanishing mid-transfer. A PROVIDER THAT LIES IS A HARDER PROBLEM THAN ONE THAT FAILS and only the second is handled. P8 receipt AMENDED IN PLACE. test_humf.py 19 passed (was 12); 152 accelerator tests pass overall. || THE PROVIDER THAT LIES, AND THE AFFORDABILITY THRESHOLD FOR CHECKING IT 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_HUMF_SILENT_CORRUPTION.json): the failure-injection receipt closed by naming what it did NOT model -- 'silent corruption that returns wrong bytes WITHOUT raising... A PROVIDER THAT LIES IS A HARDER PROBLEM THAN ONE THAT FAILS'. This is that problem. WHY IT IS HARDER: a provider that FAILS raises and a state machine can react, which is what the last block built; a provider that LIES returns WITHOUT ERROR and returns the WRONG BYTES, so ERROR HANDLING IS NO DEFENCE AT ALL -- the transfer 'succeeds', the copy is marked CLEAN, it is counted in valid_copies(), and the data is wrong. ONLY VERIFICATION CATCHES IT. DEMONSTRATED WITH A CONTROL, NOT ASSERTED: corrupt_next flips a byte in what copy_out returns and raises nothing; with verify_transfers=False -- EXACTLY the previous behaviour -- the transfer completes, the destination is CLEAN, it appears in valid_copies(), and its payload DIFFERS FROM THE SOURCE. With verification on, the same corruption raises, the destination goes INVALID and out of valid_copies(), and the source is untouched. BOTH DIRECTIONS PINNED BY TESTS, because a check that only ever rejects is as useless as one that only ever accepts. THE DESIGN CONCLUSION IS A MEASURED THRESHOLD, NOT A PREFERENCE: crc32 runs at ~37 GB/s on this machine (sha256 ~2.9, blake2b ~1.37, two independent probes agreeing within 4-8%), so verification costs under a QUARTER of the transfer for any transport slower than ~9.2 GB/s. Against Apple unified memory at 589.73 GB/s it costs 16x the transfer -- UNAFFORDABLE, and UNNECESSARY, because there is no transport there to corrupt. Against Thunderbolt or PCIe at a few GB/s it costs a TENTH. A ~32 GB/s link sits ON THE WRONG SIDE at 0.87x, so this is NOT a blanket 'external transports are slow enough' -- it is a THRESHOLD, and a fast enough bridge would put verification back in question. THE DOMAIN THAT NEEDS CHECKING IS, AT TODAY'S LINK SPEEDS, THE DOMAIN THAT CAN AFFORD IT -- which is why verification applies to provider-backed transfers rather than everywhere. CRC32 NOT SHA256, AND THE THREAT MODEL IS THE REASON NOT ONLY THE SPEED: this defends against a FAULTY transport -- a cable, a reset, a driver bug -- and a checksum is the right tool for ACCIDENT. It is the WRONG tool for a MALICIOUS peer, and the module says so rather than letting 'integrity' be read as 'authentication'. WHAT VERIFICATION DOES NOT COVER, stated: corruption AFTER the check, corruption of the SOURCE before the digest is taken, a provider that corrupts CONSISTENTLY in both directions (the digest would agree with itself), and any adversary who can recompute a crc32. Detection is at TRANSFER BOUNDARIES ONLY, not continuous. CLAIM BOUNDARY HELD: the CHECKSUM rates are MEASURED here; every TRANSPORT rate in the table is a NAMED ASSUMPTION -- no external GPU exists and §21 forbids reading a simulated transport number as physical evidence -- so the affordability conclusion is CONDITIONAL on a speed nobody here has measured, and it says so. test_humf.py 24 passed (was 19, was 12); 157 accelerator tests pass. || THE THREE MODES THE CORRUPTION RECEIPT LISTED AS NOT MODELLED 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_HUMF_TORN_TIMEOUT_LOST.json): the silent-corruption receipt closed by naming what it did NOT handle -- partial or torn writes, timeouts, a provider vanishing mid-transfer. All three are now modelled and THEY NEEDED THREE DIFFERENT AMOUNTS OF WORK, which is the finding. TORN WRITE NEEDED NOTHING NEW: tear_next stores a PREFIX and leaves the tail, raising nothing, and the existing crc32 over the whole payload CANNOT MISS a truncated tail -- so a torn write is the SAME CLASS as silent corruption, and recording that beats inventing a second mechanism that would need its own tests and could drift from the first. The control is pinned: with verify_transfers=False the torn copy is CLEAN, appears in valid_copies(), and its bytes differ from the source. TIMEOUT NEEDED A DEADLINE AND A QUARANTINE: a provider that RAISES lets the state machine react, but one that HANGS raises nothing and completes nothing, so the destination sits in TRANSFERRING FOREVER and the except branch NEVER RUNS. The deadline returns control and marks the destination INVALID -- but IT CANNOT ABANDON THE CALL, the worker is still inside the provider and may still complete, which is exactly why the domain is QUARANTINED rather than merely marked failed: refusing the next transfer is the only thing stopping a second call racing the first. Real abandonment needs the transport somewhere it can be killed and that is NOT BUILT AND NOT CLAIMED. DEVICE LOST NEEDED SOMETHING GENUINELY ABSENT: a failed COPY damages ONE object, a lost DEVICE takes EVERY copy it held, and nothing did the second -- valid_copies() would have kept naming copies on a device that no longer exists and the planner would have kept choosing them as transfer sources, a SILENT WRONG ANSWER rather than an error. Demonstrated on a BYSTANDER object that was never part of the failing transfer: valid_copies() goes ['MOCK_EXTERNAL_VRAM'] -> []. DATA LOSS IS A SEPARATE FIELD, not a count: a DIRTY copy in the lost domain held the ONLY live state, so losing it is unrecoverable and is named that way, while a REPLICATED object is reported degraded and explicitly NOT lost -- crying wolf on every disconnection would make the field useless, and both directions are pinned. A DEFECT THE TESTS FOUND IN THE RECOVERY PATH: after a timeout the destination is INVALID and INVALID -> TRANSFERRING is ILLEGAL, so releasing the quarantine left the object permanently stuck. THE STATE MACHINE WAS RIGHT -- INVALID means the contents are UNKNOWN and letting a transfer 'resume' would lie about what happened -- so release_quarantine() now performs the INVALID -> ABSENT reset and returns what it cleared, making recovery ONE explicit operator action instead of a sequence a caller can half-perform. Found by WRITING THE TEST for recovery, not by reading the code. STILL NOT MODELLED and stated: a provider that corrupts CONSISTENTLY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS (the digest agrees with itself), corruption AFTER the check, a PARTIAL device loss where some memory survives, and any adversary who can recompute a crc32 -- the checksum defends against ACCIDENT and is the wrong tool for a MALICIOUS peer. MOCK ONLY: no external GPU exists, every transport rate is a knob, and §21 forbids citing one as physical evidence -- what is proven is the STATE MACHINE under three failure shapes. test_humf.py 32 passed (was 24, 19, 12); 181 accelerator tests pass. || A PARTIAL LOSS CANNOT REUSE THE FULL-LOSS HANDLER, AND A ROUND-TRIP CHECK DOES NOT VALIDATE THE RESIDENT COPY 2026-08-25 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_HUMF_PARTIAL_LOSS.json): the previous receipt listed as STILL NOT MODELLED 'a PARTIAL device loss where some memory survives' and 'corruption AFTER the check'. Both are attacked and the second turned into something sharper than it was named. PARTIAL LOSS CANNOT REUSE device_lost, and the reason is the whole point: the full-loss handler is safe because of a BLANKET ASSUMPTION -- nothing in that domain survived -- and on a partial loss that assumption is WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Assume everything survived and valid_copies() names PHANTOMS; assume everything died and a DIRTY copy the device STILL HOLDS becomes MANUFACTURED DATA LOSS, the fabric destroying live state that was never gone. SO THE FABRIC ASKS: device_partially_lost() PROBES each copy through the provider and classifies per object, because a partial loss is the case where the bookkeeping CANNOT BE DERIVED and has to be MEASURED. Demonstrated on two objects with ONE allocation cleared -- survived=['KEPT'], lost=['GONE'], valid_copies() following both ways. THE CONTRAST IS THE EVIDENCE: a DIRTY copy that SURVIVED is reported data_lost=[] by the partial handler and IS in data_lost when THE SAME STATE goes through the full handler, so the two verdicts DIFFER ON IDENTICAL STATE -- which is precisely why one cannot stand in for the other. THEN THE SECOND, AND IT IS A BLIND SPOT NOT A GAP: the integrity check compares the SOURCE bytes against what copy_out RETURNS, so IT VALIDATES THE ROUND TRIP AND NOT THE RESIDENT COPY. That is not pedantry -- on a real bridge copy_out and a KERNEL ARE NOT THE SAME PATH, one comes back over the transport and the other reads device memory directly, so a provider whose COMPUTE PATH diverges from its READ-BACK PATH PASSES VERIFICATION AND STILL COMPUTES ON WRONG BYTES. DEMONSTRATED NOT ASSERTED: compute_skew makes read_for_compute return different bytes from copy_out; the transfer verifies, the destination is CLEAN, its payload equals the source EXACTLY, and what a kernel would read DIFFERS -- one test pins all three facts together. THERE IS NO CHEAP FIX AND THAT IS STATED: catching it needs a check that reads through THE SAME PATH THE COMPUTATION USES, meaning the DEVICE computing a digest of its own memory, which is a real EGB design requirement recorded rather than invented against a mock. The limit is now written WHERE IT LIVES, in the verification block itself, so `verified` cannot be read as a guarantee about what the GPU sees. This is a SHARPER version of 'corruption after the check' -- not corruption after the check IN TIME, but a check on the WRONG PATH ENTIRELY. STILL NOT MODELLED and stated: a provider that corrupts CONSISTENTLY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS so the digest agrees with itself, and any adversary who can recompute a crc32. COMPUTE_SKEW, WHICH PASSED EVERY PREVIOUS VERSION OF THE CHECK, IS CAUGHT: the transfer RAISES and the destination stays out of valid_copies(), while the ROUND-TRIP check passed the same case -- so the two are INDEPENDENT rather than two views of one, and corrupt_next still fires on the round-trip check alone (which the resident digest would never see) with its own test pinning that. My FIRST per-item diff reported 11 of 11 entries differing; it was including wall_s, which differs by construction. THE FUSED 756-DISPATCH GRAPH IS CLEARED FOR THE RESIDENT ON CAPABILITY GROUNDS. SPEED, AND THE NUMBER I ALMOST PUBLISHED: the naive aggregate says FUSED IS 12.17% SLOWER (964.83 -> 1098.55 s) AND THAT IS ONE ITEM -- fact-capital[2] took 287.45 s to emit its 43 tokens against 6.85 s unfused, a 42x STALL producing the IDENTICAL tokens with finish_reason=stop. Fused is FASTER ON 41 OF 43 ITEMS, median per-item delta -0.496 s; excluding that one item, 42 items and 18027 tokens go 958.0 -> 811.1 s = 18.11% FASTER, raw TPS 18.82 -> 22.23 and ACCEPTED TPS 13.13 -> 15.51. BOTH NUMBERS ALONE ARE WRONG and reporting either without the other would be the more dishonest choice. SAME OUTLIER CLASS as the decoder bench's 3-of-12 at 1.6-2.0x, far more extreme, CAUSE STILL UNKNOWN and not attributed. THE GAIN SCALES WITH GENERATION LENGTH: median ms/token by band gives +3.69% at 101-300 tokens and +3.46% at 301-800, close to the decoder bench's +2.41% at 64 -- and +29.09% ABOVE 800 TOKENS over 8 items, an ORDER LARGER. The <=100 band's +7.97% is marked UNRELIABLE because startup is over half those items' wall. WHY the gain grows with length is NOT MEASURED and no mechanism is offered: the fused add_residual_rmsnorm removes a context-INDEPENDENT pass, so the obvious story does not fit, and inventing one here is the untested diagnosis this program has written down five times and found wrong twice. A HARNESS FAILURE THE NEW GUARD CAUGHT: the first identified run returned 0 of 43 in under 60 s on ModuleNotFoundError transformers, and harness_health (added this session) reported every_call_errored, scoreable=false and rate=NULL rather than 0/43 -- which would have read as THE RESIDENT IS CAPABILITY-DEAD UNDER IDENTITY, a conclusion about the model drawn from a missing package. ROOT CAUSE IS A NAME COLLISION: TWO python3.12 interpreters exist here, the framework 3.12.6 WITH transformers 5.5.4 and mlx, and PATH `python3.12` at 3.12.13 with NEITHER. CHECKPOINT_002 sealed 'a test count without its interpreter is not a measurement' -- correct and NOT SPECIFIC ENOUGH, because that string names two interpreters; an interpreter must be recorded by PATH. CLAIM BOUNDARY: THE TWO CAPABILITY RUNS ARE NOT PAIRED (unfused first, fused ~25 min later) and the stall proves the machine was not quiet, so 18.11% carries possible drift -- the DIRECTION is confirmed by two independent instruments and the LONG-LENGTH MAGNITUDE needs a paired re-measurement; ONE run per arm; ONE arm (open_think), so pre_closed_think is uncleared; the 3.627 s startup constant is the unfused fit's intercept applied to both arms because the stall drives the fused fit to R2 0.0518; the stall's cause is unknown and nothing here bounds its probability.

value.headline: - [ ] G075 — TOKEN EXECUTION ATLAS FOR THE SEALED RESIDENT [S031 §3]: instrument one decode token of the 3.1393 resident and record, per dispatch, the ordinal, operator family, layer, organ, shape, input and output representation, bytes read and written, FLOPs where valid, duration, synchronization dependency, command-buffer membership, intermediate allocation, reusable operands, residency state, whether the output escapes the next operator, fusion eligibility and representation-native eligibility. Aggregate by operator, layer, primitive, time, dispatch count, bytes and graph boundary, and produce the four Pareto rankings (time, count, bytes, synchronization). THE ATLAS IS THE PRECONDITION FOR TOUCHING THE GRAPH: S031 §3 says do not assume the most numerous kernel is the most expensive, and this campaign has already been wrong about which refusal reason was binding three separate times. Not closed until every one of the ~964 dispatches is attributed or the unattributed remainder is stated as a number. | status: OPEN | risk: medium | tier: V2 || FIRST ATTEMPT REFUTED BY A REAL RUN 2026-08-26 (receipts/headless/TOKEN_EXECUTION_ATLAS.json): I built the count column by PARSING qwen38_64_layer_execution_schedule.rs and it reconciled to 964 exactly with zero unattributed -- q4_matvec 401, rmsnorm 129, add_residual 128, silu_mul 64. Then crates/hawking-core/examples/qwen38_dispatch_trace.rs, WHICH ALREADY EXISTED, was run on the sealed 3.1393 resident and dispatched 14 distinct kernels of which ONLY SEVEN APPEAR IN THE SCHEDULE. gk_swiglu_f32 replaces qwen80_silu_mul_f32 (a different kernel, not a rename) and qwen_affine_q2_group32_matvec is dispatched while appearing NOWHERE in the schedule. The runtime's own census explains it: tensors=755 affine=192 q4=210 f32=353, genome mlp_kernel=qwen_q2f_group64 dn_kernel=qwen_uniform_q3_group64 -- THE SEALED RESIDENT IS A MIXED-CODEC BODY and the schedule describes a uniform-q4 one. THE HISTOGRAM IS WITHDRAWN as a description of this resident. The arithmetic 1+64*15+3 and the runtime dispatch counter are untouched -- what is refuted is the ATTRIBUTION, not the count, and whether THIS body runs 15 per layer is unmeasured because the trace reports distinct names (14) and not per-token counts. A PERFECT RECONCILIATION AGAINST A DECLARATION IS NOT A MEASUREMENT. Next: per-kernel COUNTS from a real decode, not names. || COUNT COLUMN CLOSED, AND MY WITHDRAWAL WAS TOO BROAD 2026-08-26 (receipts/headless/TOKEN_EXECUTION_ATLAS_COUNTS.json): 964 DISPATCHES PER DECODE TOKEN IS NOW MEASURED ON THE SEALED RESIDENT, not declared -- by DELTA so prefill cancels, (15424-11568)/(6-2) = 3856/4 = 964.000 exactly. THE COUNTS EXISTED AND WERE DESTROYED AT ONE BOUNDARY: the runtime pushes one label per dispatch into a Vec (metal/mod.rs:5013) and the session harvest collapsed it into a HashSet, throwing away exactly the multiplicity the question is about; seen_kernels is now a BTreeMap<String,u64> with a non-draining dispatched_kernel_histogram(), and drain_dispatched_kernel_names keeps its old observable behaviour. THE ARITHMETIC 1 + 64*15 + 3 IS NOW STRUCTURALLY CONFIRMED, every term a measured count with an attribution: embed 1, layers 960, head 3 (final rmsnorm, lm_head, argmax) -- AND BOTH LAYER KINDS COST EXACTLY 15 BY DIFFERENT ROUTES, DeltaNet 6 matvec + 4 specific against GQA 7 matvec + 3 specific, so the single QWEN38_FULL_LAYER_DISPATCHES constant is right for both, which the schedule file never showed and could not have. MY WITHDRAWAL ONE BLOCK AGO WAS CORRECT IN KIND AND TOO BROAD IN EXTENT: rmsnorm 129, add_residual 128 and total matvec 401 are ALL MEASURED CORRECT; what was genuinely wrong is attributing those 401 to one uniform-q4 kernel, since this body splits them 209 q4 / 192 affine-q2 CLEANLY BY ORGAN (q4 takes every mixer projection plus lm_head, affine-q2 takes every MLP projection, nothing mixed within an organ). A WITHDRAWAL IS A CLAIM TOO -- withdrawing a whole result because part of it is wrong destroys the correct part, and here that was three numbers of four; the right move was to withdraw the ATTRIBUTION and mark the counts UNVERIFIED. FOUR FUSION LEVERS ALREADY EXISTED AS ENV FLAGS AND NO RECEIPT HAD EVER MEASURED THEM: all four on gives 756 dispatches/token, (12096-9072)/4, -208 and -21.6%, with output TOKEN-IDENTICAL 6/6 and fallbacks 0 in both arms -- stated as identical GREEDY OUTPUT and NOT identical logits, because argmax absorbs small numerical differences. THE INERT LEVER IS THE FINDING: FUSE_ADD_RMSNORM saves 128, FUSE_DN_INPROJ 48, FUSE_GQA_QKV 32, and FUSE_MLP SAVES EXACTLY ZERO -- affine_q2 stays at 192 per token, unchanged -- and it is the lever aimed at the LARGEST single kernel family in the fused graph at 25.4%. Every fusion that fired is on a uniform-q4 mixer projection and the one that did not is on the affine-q2 MLP, which reads as a REPRESENTATION-COVERAGE gap rather than a graph limitation; THAT READING IS NOT VERIFIED, what is measured is that the flag changes nothing and not why. Worth 64/token if closed, taking 756 -> 692 and under the S031 §4 <750 target with margin. CLAIM BOUNDARY: COUNTS ONLY, nothing timed, so this discharges the count column of the §3 atlas and NOT time/bytes/FLOPs, and §3 says explicitly the most numerous kernel need not be the most expensive; NO TPS measured, so 21.6% fewer dispatches is not a wall-time claim; NO capability run, so 6/6 greedy agreement is a smoke check and not the §18 floor of 30/43; one artifact, one prompt, one machine. The pre-existing failure model::qwen38_hybrid_decode::mixed_catalog_contract_tests::incumbent_extract_matches_cpu_oracle_above_uint32_overflow was verified to fail on the CLEAN tree by stashing, so it is not mine; 53 passed 1 failed in the qwen38 filter. || THE DISPATCH LADDER IS TIMED AND IT CANNOT REACH 50 2026-08-26 (receipts/headless/TOKEN_GRAPH_REDUCTION_TIMED.json): G075 measured 964 -> 756 dispatches/token under the four pre-existing fusion levers. A DISPATCH REDUCTION THAT IS NOT A WALL-TIME WIN IS NOT A WIN, so it was timed on the sealed resident: 6 ALTERNATING PAIRS, 64 tokens, no lake fill running. 21.6% FEWER DISPATCHES BUYS 2.41% WALL TIME -- 30.2536 -> 29.5420 ms/token, 33.05 -> 33.85 TPS, complete separation (max fused 29.5678 < min unfused 30.1148) with clean-arm spreads of 0.58% and 0.13%. OUTPUT IDENTICAL 64/64 tokens, fallbacks 0 in every run -- stated as identical GREEDY OUTPUT and not identical logits. A VACUOUS CHECK OF MY OWN, CAUGHT: the first identity check compared two EMPTY files and printed TOKENS IDENTICAL, because both greps returned nothing when the flags were passed as one shell word; caught by printing wc -c beside the verdict, and a non-empty guard now refuses that. THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS IS THE DERIVED ONE: 0.7117 ms over 208 removed dispatches = 3.42 us PER REMOVED DISPATCH, 3.2x cheaper than the ~11 us the AirGraph sweep measured on synthetic elementwise kernels -- NOT a refutation of that number, a different regime, and these fusions do more than delete a launch. THE SAVING IS 79% GPU-SIDE and only 19% host: GPU 28.9333 -> 28.3743 ms against host 1.3223 -> 1.1844, and host is 4.37% of wall. So S031 §1's PREMISE IS CONFIRMED -- host submission is not the lever -- while its CONCLUSION is now bounded. CEILING, under an explicitly LINEAR and explicitly false-in-detail assumption that every dispatch costs the same 3.42 us: deleting EVERY dispatch overhead gives 37.1 TPS, and the §4 target of <200 dispatches gives 36.2 raw = 25.2 ACCEPTED at the 30/43 floor. THE DISPATCH-REDUCTION LADDER CANNOT REACH 50 RAW, LET ALONE 50 ACCEPTED, ON THIS BODY -- 50 raw is above the ceiling of deleting every dispatch, and the reason was visible in the first measurement, GPU is 95.6% of wall and the bytes still have to move. WHAT IS BOUNDED IS DISPATCH COUNT AS THE LEVER, NOT the execution-graph hypothesis: a change that removes BYTES rather than launches -- gate+up fusion so the activation is read once, or consuming a packed representation without a separate unpack -- is a different mechanism this says nothing about, and being 95.6% GPU-bound is exactly what makes byte elimination the remaining candidate. OUTLIERS REPORTED NOT DROPPED SILENTLY: 3 of 12 runs ran 1.6-2.0x slow (2 fused, 1 unfused, so ARM-INDEPENDENT), entirely in gpu_ns with host indistinguishable, cause UNKNOWN and not investigated; excluded from the medians with the raw table published, and n=5/n=4 is admitted by complete separation and not by a rep count -- a 25% outlier rate is far below this program's own 200-rep standard and saying so beats quoting 2.41% as if it were clean. NO CAPABILITY SUITE RUN under fusion, so the fused graph is NOT cleared for the resident until the 43-case §18 floor runs. No kernel was written or changed; the four levers pre-existed. || I REFUTED MY OWN +29% BY DOING WHAT ITS CLAIM BOUNDARY SAID 2026-08-26 (receipts/headless/FUSION_GAIN_IS_LENGTH_INDEPENDENT.json): CAPABILITY_FUSED_GRAPH_CLEARED.json measured +29.09% in the >800-token band and called it AN ORDER LARGER than the decoder bench's +2.41% at 64 tokens, while naming in its own claim boundary that its two runs were NOT PAIRED and needed re-measuring. RE-MEASURED PAIRED AND ALTERNATING IN ONE SESSION at 64, 256 and 1024 new tokens: THE GAIN IS FLAT IN GENERATION LENGTH. Clean unfused 30.2282-30.3325 ms/token and clean fused 29.5537-29.6653 at EVERY length across a 16x range, giving 2.19% -- the SAME as the original 64-token number, and both floors reproduce a different day's different process (30.2536 / 29.5420) to 0.1%. WHAT THE 29% ACTUALLY WAS: the capability run's >800 band showed unfused at 45.44 ms/token against a clean floor of 30.28, 1.50x INFLATED by contention on unpaired runs 25 minutes apart, so the band table read DRIFT ON THE UNFUSED LONG ITEMS as a fused advantage. The +18.11% excluding-the-stall figure rests on the same pair and is SUPERSEDED as a magnitude; its DIRECTION was right. WHAT SURVIVES UNTOUCHED is the capability equality -- 30/43 both arms and 43/43 repetitions semantically identical -- because that compares OUTPUTS and outputs do not drift, so the fused graph stays cleared on capability grounds. AND THE TIGHTENING MATTERS: a length-independent gain means TOKEN_GRAPH_REDUCTION_TIMED's ~37 TPS ceiling does NOT improve at longer generations either, which +29% would have implied. THE STALL HAS A NAMED CANDIDATE AND IT DOES NOT COVER EVERYTHING: 12 of 24 runs in this block ran 1.2x-2.9x slow, worst 87.87 ms/token, and looking with `ps -Ao pcpu -r` rather than a grep found pid 40536 running tools/mlx_boot.py from ~/Downloads/personalmodel/Personal-Model at 50-95% CPU holding 30.9 GiB -- AN MLX MODEL BOOT, which is the RIGHT MECHANISM because this campaign sealed on 2026-08-22 that METAL WORKING SET is the admission gate and not free RAM, and a 31 GiB resident competing with this 9.9 GiB one is exactly that gate. ALSO fileproviderd at 99.6% and mds_stores at 99.0% BOTH FOR FIVE HOURS. BUT mlx_boot was TEN MINUTES OLD when found so it CANNOT explain TOKEN_GRAPH_REDUCTION_TIMED's 3-of-12 or the 287 s capability stall, both of which predate it -- those remain UNKNOWN, and a named candidate for one spike is not a cause for all of them. MY QUIESCENCE CHECK WAS SCOPED TO THE CONTENDER I KNEW ABOUT: TOKEN_GRAPH_REDUCTION_TIMED recorded 'no lake fill running (pgrep modellake = 0)' and I read that as MACHINE IS QUIET, while two system daemons had been pegged near 100% for five hours the whole time. A check that names one process family and is read as machine-wide reports WHAT IT LOOKED FOR, NOT WHAT IS THERE -- the same shape as the coverage curve that counted the absence of probed blockers. NOTHING WAS KILLED: mlx_boot is the operator's work, on the same rule as the lake fill. CLAIM BOUNDARY: 5 clean runs per arm after excluding 12 of 24, an enormous exclusion rate, admitted by COMPLETE SEPARATION of two tight clusters plus cross-session reproduction and NOT by a rep count or a noise gate; the outlier cause is a NAMED CANDIDATE WITH THE RIGHT MECHANISM and not a demonstrated one, since the settling experiment is to kill it and re-measure and that was not run; three lengths, one prompt, one artifact, one machine, so length-independence is established over 64-1024 and says nothing beyond; no capability re-run; no kernel changed. || THE TIME COLUMN EXISTS PER LEVER, AND IT REFUTES THE COUNT PARETO 2026-08-26 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_DISPATCH_IS_NOT_THE_COST.json): S031 §3 says in its own words do not assume the most numerous kernel is the most expensive. MEASURED, and the count column closed last block is NOT the time column. Marginal GPU cost per removed dispatch by lever: add_rmsnorm+gqa_qkv+dn_inproj 2.64 us over 208 dispatches, mlp gate_up PAIR 17.35 us over 64, mlp swiglu elementwise 2.86 us over 64. THREE LEVERS AGREE AT 2.6-2.9 AND ONE IS 6.6x THAT, and the flanking control is the OTHER HALF OF THE SAME FLAG (both are FUSE_MLP), measured in one session on one machine with one instrument -- so ~2.7 us is a real per-dispatch cost and 84% of the pair lever is something else. Host is flat at 1.5-1.8% of wall across all five arms and moved +0.017 ms across the step that moved 1.094, so the outlier is GPU execution; and it is not DRAM bandwidth, because the 22.82 GB of input element-loads the fused kernel eliminates would imply 20.55 TB/s against this machine's measured 589.73 GB/s, a 34.8x overshoot. The BYTE lever measured in the same block says the same from the other side: eliminating gk_swiglu_f32 removes 8.91 MB of genuine DRAM traffic per token, worth 15 us at 589.73 GB/s, against a measured 183 us -- so 8.3% of that lever is bytes and the rest is the dispatch. AT THE MAGNITUDES AVAILABLE ON THIS BODY AT DECODE, S031 §2's ordering of ELIMINATE BYTES above ELIMINATE DISPATCHES IS INVERTED, which is a statement about these magnitudes and not a reversal of the principle. WHOLE-TOKEN BYTES ARE NOW EXACT: 9,878,898,416 weight bytes read per decode token, reconciled from payload_bytes 10,554,328,856 minus the 675,430,440-byte embedding table (untied, read as one row), giving 358.1 GB/s effective = 60.7% of the wall and 1.65x of TOTAL remaining headroom for all execution-graph work combined. STILL OPEN AND NOT BLOCKED: there is still NO PER-DISPATCH duration, byte or FLOP column -- every figure here is a MARGINAL derived by differencing two graphs, because GPU time is per-COMMAND-BUFFER (GPUEndTime-GPUStartTime) and Metal timestamp counter sampling is probed as SUPPORTED and deliberately not encoded at crates/hawking-core/src/metal/mod.rs:704 on the stated grounds that markers would perturb the command buffer. That is a DESIGN CHOICE, not a hardware gate, and it is recorded as such rather than as a blocker. The four Pareto rankings are one of four. || THE 628 BYTE ATLAS RECONCILES TO 0.101% AND ITS RANKING DISAGREES WITH THE DISPATCH RANKING 2026-08-26 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_TOKEN_BYTE_ATLAS_628.json): S032 §9 says the 964-dispatch atlas is stale. Rebuilt for the 628 graph from exact element counts x codec bpw -- affine_q2 g64 at 2.5 bpw for every MLP tensor, HQ30UQ4 g64 at 4.25 for every mixer projection, the head and the embedding. IT RECONCILES AGAINST THE ARTIFACT'S OWN PAYLOAD: derived total plus the embedding table is 10,543,677,440 against payload_bytes 10,554,328,856, UNACCOUNTED 10,651,416 = 0.101% -- AND THE RESIDUAL HAS A NAME, because MIX_REPORT records f32_bytes 10,584,840. That is what separates this from the first atlas, which reconciled to 964 EXACTLY by parsing a schedule file and was then refuted by a real run for describing a uniform-q4 body. RANKING BY TOKEN BYTES: MLP 54.19% over 128 dispatches, DeltaNet projections 29.93% over 96, GQA projections 9.03% over 48, lm_head 6.84% IN ONE. THE PER-DISPATCH RANKING IS THE OPPOSITE: the head moves 675,430,400 bytes in a single dispatch against 55,705,600 for the largest MLP dispatch, 12.13x, and is still only 6.84% of the token because the MLP runs its dispatch 128 times. A ranking by dispatch cost and a ranking by token cost DISAGREE -- the same lesson as dispatch-count-is-not-time, arriving on the byte axis. WHAT THIS ATLAS IS NOT: the TIME column. Bytes are exact; the ms figures divide by ONE effective bandwidth and ACCELERATOR_EXPERT_BATCH already measured 161.9 vs 426.4 GB/s for two kernels on this machine, so a family's ms here is a LOWER BOUND and only the BYTE ranking is claimed. KV, activation and DeltaNet-state traffic are excluded and are not thereby zero. Per-dispatch duration still does not exist: Metal timestamp sampling is probed as SUPPORTED and deliberately not encoded (crates/hawking-core/src/metal/mod.rs:704), which is a DESIGN CHOICE and not a hardware gate. || THE BOUNDARY CENSUS, AND THE EXCLUDED TRAFFIC IS NOW A NUMBER 2026-08-26 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_628_BOUNDARY_CENSUS.json): S032 §9's second half. Twelve producer/consumer boundaries in the 628 graph, TWO OF THEM UNDELETABLE AND MARKED SO -- GQA's qkv and rope/cache outputs ESCAPE into the KV cache and are read by every later token, and marking two of twelve is what keeps the other ten meaningful. 401 OF 628 DISPATCHES sit at non-escaping boundaries (63.9%); deleting all of them would leave 227, inside §4's <300 rung. AND THAT IS THE CEILING ON THE WHOLE LEVER: 401 x the 2.75 us marginal measured for non-operand-sharing levers is 1.10 ms of a 28.02 ms token = 3.9%, plus 31.68 MB of intermediate traffic = 0.32% of weight bytes. Against the 1.65x the byte wall leaves, EVERY REMAINING GRAPH BOUNDARY TOGETHER IS ~4% OF A 65% GAP -- the third time this session a count-based ladder has proved worth far less than its count. THE STRUCTURE ALSO CHANGED SHAPE: unfused, both layer kinds cost exactly 15 by different routes; FUSED THEY DIVERGE, 48 DeltaNet at 10 dispatches and 16 GQA at 9, because FUSE_DN_INPROJ collapses 2 matvecs into 1 on 48 layers while FUSE_GQA_QKV collapses 3 into 1 on 16. THE CLEAREST ABSTRACTION TAX BY RATIO: ba_to_decay_beta -> gated_delta_decode spends a whole dispatch moving 384 BYTES, 48 times per token -- 0.0004% of weight traffic for 7.6% of the dispatches. AND THE ATLAS'S NAMED EXCLUSION IS NOW MEASURED: the DeltaNet RECURRENT STATE is 48 value heads x 128 x 128 f32 = 3.146 MB PER LAYER read and written every token = 301.99 MB/token = 3.06% of the weight bytes, invisible to every weight ranking because it is not a weight and invisible to EBPW because it is not quantized. With the conv cache (22.02 MB) and KV at context 60 (7.86 MB), non-weight traffic is 331.87 MB = 3.36%, so the token reads ~10.20 GB not 9.87 and the byte-wall fraction moves 60.7% -> ~62.7%. The previous ceiling was OPTIMISTIC exactly as its own claim boundary said. THE KV TERM IS THE ONLY ONE THAT GROWS WITH CONTEXT -- 1.07 GB/token at 8192, 10.9% of weight bytes -- the first term in this accounting that makes the ceiling context-dependent.

value.headline: - [ ] G076 — HCLI VERIFIER PATH SEMANTICS [S031 §21]: mission ef3745542c5b returned exit 126 REFUSED: command names protected path 'receipts', and mission 245a88b6d9b5 failed because a repo-relative path does not resolve inside .hcli/delegations/<id>/. TWO DISTINCT DEFECTS: (1) the delegation workspace does not contain the repo, so a repo-relative verifier path is unresolvable; (2) shell_runner refuses any command whose TEXT CONTAINS a protected-path substring, which blocks READS as well as WRITES and makes 'protected' and 'verifiable' mutually exclusive for receipts -- the class of file that most wants to be both. S031 §21 forbids fixing this by weakening workspace isolation: establish an explicit canonical repository root with deterministic verifier path resolution. MUST BE MUTATION-TESTED, and the negative control is load-bearing -- a verifier that WRITES to a protected path must still be refused after the widening, or the guard has been traded for a convenience. | status: OPEN | risk: medium | tier: V2 || BOTH DEFECTS REPAIRED WITHOUT WEAKENING ISOLATION 2026-08-26 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_HCLI_VERIFIER_PATH_SEMANTICS.json, hcli/delegate.py): (1) THE REPO IS NAMEABLE. Three roots exported into the verifier's environment -- HAWKING_REPO_ROOT via hcli.paths.find_repo_root, which walks to a .git or Cargo.toml rather than counting directory levels; HCLI_MISSION_ROOT from mission_dir(ws), the existing authority rather than a new layout; HCLI_WORKSPACE_ROOT. THE CWD IS STILL THE WORKSPACE AND THE REPO IS STILL NOT COPIED IN, pinned by a test, because S031 §21 forbids trading isolation for resolution and NAMEABILITY IS NOT REACH. A wrong root yields a path that visibly fails test -d rather than a silent fallback. (2) THE GUARD NO LONGER REFUSES READS. The rule is one sentence -- a protected path may not be WRITTEN, reading it is what it is for -- with the three ways to write one checked where each lives: a redirection TARGET over the whole line, a writing verb handed the path per segment, and a verb nobody vouched for handed the path refused because it CANNOT BE SHOWN not to write. `cat receipts/r.json | python3 -c ...` now runs, because the read-only verb names the path while python gets bytes on stdin. THE READ-ONLY LIST'S ABSENCES ARE THE DESIGN: python3, python, pytest, awk, sed, sort and find are NOT in it, because every one can write a path handed to it. THE NEGATIVE CONTROL CAUGHT MY OWN GUARD WITHIN MINUTES -- the first version had python3 in the read-only set, and the control ran a python3 -c that opened the receipt for write and RETURNED 0 having written it. S031 §21 calls that control load-bearing and it was, for about four minutes. AND A MUTATION PROVED MY OWN RULE INCOHERENT: deleting the whole-command redirection check changed NOTHING, which exposed that the per-segment check was refusing on the PRESENCE of a redirection rather than its TARGET -- so `cat receipts/x | tee copy.json` was allowed while `cat receipts/x > copy.json` was refused, two commands that both read the protected file and write elsewhere. Fixed by checking the target; a surviving mutation is usually a missing test and this one was a wrong rule. THREE OF MY OWN TESTS ASSERTED THE WRONG THING and each was corrected against the code rather than the reverse -- all three encoded WHOLE-COMMAND thinking, which is the exact defect under repair, so writing the test first did not protect me from the assumption the test existed to remove. FIVE MUTATIONS WATCHED FIRING, NO SURVIVORS: the original whole-command guard (5 failed), python3 back in the read-only set (2), no redirection-target check (3), an unknown verb allowed (3), the three roots dropped (2). hcli 34 -> 45 passed. NOT CLOSED: this is NOT a shell parser and a test asserts so -- a path reached by symlink or reassembled from a shell variable is NOT caught. NO REAL MISSION HAS RUN END TO END through the repaired path; the two failing missions named above were not re-run.

value.headline: - [ ] G077 — WHY 2.60 LOSES STRUCTURED OUTPUT AND 3.14 KEEPS IT [S031 §20]: the identified 2.60 run scores structured_output 0/15 while sealed-3.14 scores 30/43 overall, and structured output is the axis HCLI's planner needs most. Bounded Doctor/Gravity lane comparing logits, grammar-critical token margins, late-layer divergence, attention sensitivity, LM-head sensitivity and format-transition behaviour between the two bodies, to determine whether a small targeted information injection restores it. If it does, 2.60 re-enters the resident frontier at 0.54 EBPW less than the current resident. PARALLEL LANE, EXPLICITLY NOT THE CRITICAL PATH -- S031 §20 says do not let this dominate Accelerator. | status: OPEN | risk: medium | tier: V2 || THE QUESTION IS NOT ONLY ABOUT 2.60 -- THE RESIDENT'S STRUCTURED OUTPUT WAS ALSO TEMPLATE-LIMITED 2026-08-26 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_RESIDENT_TEMPLATE_ARM.json): this obligation frames structured output as a 2.60-vs-3.14 difference. Measured on the RESIDENT, sealed-3.14's structured_output is 5/15 on open_think and 10/15 on pre_closed_think -- the SAME BODY, zero bytes changed, and the only axis of seven that moves. So the resident was ALSO losing structured output to the template arm, and half of what this obligation attributes to the 2.60 body's density was a serving-mode effect present in both bodies. THE MECHANISM IS VISIBLE PER ITEM, not inferred: json-kind-correct goes 0/5 -> 5/5 and its open_think replies are EMPTY after the think block is stripped, having generated 222-1135 tokens with finish_reason=stop -- the model emits the correct JSON object and the think block consumed the budget. Across the suite, empty replies go 8 -> 0 and total completion tokens 18070 -> 2035. WHAT REMAINS IS A DIFFERENT DEFECT AND IS NOW ISOLATED: json-answer stays 0/5 under pre_closed_think with 'JSON parsed but missing keys [operations, tests]' -- the model answers correctly and omits two EMPTY ARRAYS the system prompt asked for. That is PROMPT ADHERENCE, not density and not template, and the grader is right to demand them because a planner that must branch on `operations` cannot branch on an absent key. So this obligation's comparison must be re-run ARM-MATCHED before any density conclusion is drawn from it: the existing 2.60 figure (0/15) is open_think and the resident's was too, and neither was the body's best.

value.headline: - [ ] G078 — BENCH_STATE IS A HARD RECEIPT FIELD [S032 §3, §16]: every receipt that can make a performance claim carries recorded quiescence -- contender count, contender CPU, contender RSS, measurement timestamp and machine identity -- with BENCH_STATE three-valued and NEVER defaulting to quiet: QUIESCED when sampled and clean, CONTENDED when sampled and dirty, UNKNOWN when not sampled. A speed claim resting on UNKNOWN is PROVISIONAL by construction. A contended arm may not be silently compared to an uncontended one. Sampling must bind to the window without perturbing it, so it happens immediately around the benchmark and not inside every micro-timed kernel. Latency is first-class: ms/token, p50, p95 where appropriate, within-run spread and across-run spread. Acceptance requires comparable quiescence, low enough spread, repeated PROCESS measurements, the exact same workload, and capability preservation. | status: IN_PROGRESS | risk: low | tier: V2 || PARTLY LANDED 2026-08-26: bench.machine_quiescence enumerates rather than name-filters and is wired into capability_suite.py (machine_state block with worst_repetition_spread_pct) and into every timed arm of ACCELERATOR_DISPATCH_IS_NOT_THE_COST, ACCELERATOR_RESIDENT_TEMPLATE_ARM and ACCELERATOR_LM_HEAD_EXACT_BOUNDS_REFUTED via a PRE-REGISTERED admission gate; resident_seal.validate REFUSES a speed claim carrying UNKNOWN unless the seal is marked PROVISIONAL, mutation-tested with the PROVISIONAL escape verified to work so the rule is not a ban. STILL OPEN: it is NOT a schema requirement -- no validator refuses a PERFORMANCE RECEIPT that omits BENCH_STATE, only the seal does, so an ordinary receipt can still make a speed claim with no machine state at all. p95 is nowhere. || AND THE GATE REFUSED A RUN RATHER THAN PUBLISHING IT 2026-08-26: the three-arm MLP mechanism experiment returned NO ADMITTED SWEEP inside its budget and wrote BENCH_STATE = CONTENDED with no timing claim, while the two-arm run that preceded it was admitted 3/3 at max_rss 0.13-0.15 GiB. Same harness, same gate, opposite verdicts on the same day -- which is what makes the QUIESCED label on the admitted run mean something rather than being a word every receipt carries. || BENCH_STATE IS NOW A SCHEMA REQUIREMENT AND THE CORPUS WAS 296/297 SHORT 2026-08-26 (receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_BENCH_STATE_IS_A_SCHEMA_REQUIREMENT.json, tools/accelerator/receipt.py, tools/accelerator/bench.py::bench_block): S032 §3 says every performance receipt carries the machine state it was measured under. Only the resident seal enforced it. Census over receipts/headless: 297 receipts quote a duration, a rate or a speed ratio; ONE carried any machine state. An absent state is NOT NEUTRAL -- every downstream reader, the AKB and a later me included, reads a timing number with no machine state as a clean measurement, and the silence made a claim the receipts never made. receipt.build now REFUSES a receipt whose result tree quotes timing and passes no bench block, and the scan walks the WHOLE tree: the mutation that removed recursion still passed 15 of 17 tests, because a top-level-only rule is defeated by one level of nesting, which is the shape of every real receipt here. QUIESCED HAS TO BE EARNED -- bench_block takes NO state argument, so the state is derived from samples and a caller cannot stamp QUIESCED on a contended measurement without editing the derivation; QUIESCED with no sample, or with contenders recorded, is refused; and a `ps` that exited non-zero derives UNKNOWN, because it found nothing only because it could not look -- the 0-of-0-cases shape this program has sealed four times. THE BACKFILL IS UNKNOWN, NOT QUIESCED: 278 UNKNOWN, 1 CONTENDED derived from samples the receipt already carried, 0 QUIESCED, 27 raw data dumps skipped as not receipts. Stamping QUIESCED would have been a fabrication across 278 files; UNKNOWN is what those runs were measured under and costs nothing that was true. The backfill LABELS ITSELF so a state recorded at measurement time is distinguishable from one reconstructed afterwards. Three mutations watched failing. THIS IS COVERAGE, NOT ACCURACY -- no historical number became more trustworthy today, the unqualified ones are now VISIBLY unqualified. First attempt reformatted all 297 files to a different indent and produced an 863,000-line diff hiding the one added field; reverted and redone preserving each file's own indentation. 22 new tests, 543 passing under tools/accelerator/. STILL OPEN: p95, and carrying bench_block into the live harnesses so NEW receipts derive a real state instead of inheriting UNKNOWN.
